summary: Group aware Polls
description:
Polls is a pretty straightforward tool, and it has been without a group-aware feature for years.

Currently, it allows maintain/instructor users to create a new poll for the entire site, and access/student users in the site can answer it. This new feature would not require any new permissions or additional widgets to configure them.

In the creation settings, a simple group selector could display all existing groups in the site. If one or more groups are selected, only access/student users in those groups would be able to answer the poll.

summary: Moderate and Require users to post before reading does not show student their pending post
description:
In a moderated only forum topic, the student is able to see their own pending post. If the forum topic is moderated and has "Require users to post before reading" set, the student does not see their own pending post.

To reproduce:
As the instructor, create a moderated forum
Add two topics, with the following items set:
1) Moderated
2) Moderated and Require users to post before reading

As the student, post to 1: Moderated topic
Post displays with "Pending" before the subject
Now post to 2: Moderated, Require users to post before reading
Post does not display, the message count has updated, but the student has no clue if their post was actually submitted

summary: Limits in the UserEntityProvider (getEntities) seem to be incorrect
description:
This problem seems like it's been around for awhile, maybe since the beginning of the provider. In order to really test it you have to have more than 50 users in the system.

The user api is set to work on "first" and "last", where this /direct interface is set to use parameters (generally _start and _limit). It looks like it's incorrectly manipulating the _start and _limit to try to fit into the values for first and last.

The way the code is, it looks like there's no way to search above the first 50 users, it will always keep the first and last less than 50, keeping the set in the first 50, but there are a variety of defaults that *might* be set. It's good to restrict it so it doesn't return *more* than some number 50 forcing you to page but there is an error here back from the initial version of this code that seems break this.

For example say you have 200 users

* direct/user.xml?_sessionId=[SessionID]&_page=3

You'd expect 50 users from page 3 (so 151-200 users) instead it returns an empty set.

* direct/user.xml?_sessionId=[SessionID]&_page=2
 
You'd expect 50 users from page 2, instead you get back the 10th user

* direct/user.xml?_sessionId=[SessionID]&_start=55

Returns the first 50 users, because it sets start to 1 since start > 50.

There's a lot of similar problems like this in this call when using all of the parameters (_limit, _perpage, etc) based on how  these are limited by the entitybroker and then passed through as "first" and "last" by this method.

summary: OAuth should be disabled by default
description:
In our testing of Sakai 11.0, I noticed at least one error because the table OAUTH_ACCESSORS does not exist in our database.

This seems odd, because according to the [default.sakai.properties|https://github.com/sakaiproject/sakai/blob/master/config/configuration/bundles/src/bundle/org/sakaiproject/config/bundle/default.sakai.properties#L4312], oauth should be disabled by default. According to the OAuth project’s [components.xml|https://github.com/sakaiproject/sakai/blob/master/oauth/pack/src/webapp/WEB-INF/components.xml#L70-L76] file, it looks like it is in fact enabled by default?  Also, the [readme|https://github.com/sakaiproject/sakai/blame/master/oauth/README.md#L125] says it’s enabled by default.

It should either be disabled by default or the default.sakai.properties file should be changed and the tables created in a conversion script.

summary: Create a centralized Grading Service that all Sakai tools use
description: A centralized grading service for all Sakai tools would simplify and harmonize the overall application. Instead of each tool managing its own grading and then passing grades back to the Gradebook, all tools that generate grades (including Gradebook) would use this new central service. This means that the code for handling grades does not need to be built into each tool separately. The grading service can simply be called by a tool when grading is needed. It also means that faculty can input or update grades from either the Gradebook or the tool (such as Assignments, Samigo, Forums, or Lessons) since the same service is being called in all locations where a grading interface appears.

summary: Calendar import from site with Tests & Quizzes events results in old links
description:
If a user imports from one site to another, calendar events created by Tests & Quizzes remain, with the link to take the test pointing to the original site. 

We have instructors who copy content from a master template into their courses for each semester using the Site Info - Import from Site method. We also have instructors teaching multiple sections who will import from section 1 into section 2. We have seen that if the original site has Tests & Quizzes published and set to create the calendar event, these events are also present in the destination site, with the URL to take the test still pointing to the original. If the instructor publishes the test in the destination site, that test could be on the calendar twice. One link works for students, one does not. 

I feel that these events should not be imported, as they will be recreated if/when the instructor publishes the tests. This would also mirror the behavior of calendar events created by Assignments. 

*Developer Note*: Actually since this fix borrows logic from CC+Import, this fix should suppress the copying of T&Q Dates, Assignment Dates (already in the code), and Discussion Topic deadlines.

summary: Add link to Rubric showing where Lock comes from
description:
If a rubric is linked to an assignment, gradebook item, test or quiz, a lock shows up next to its title to show that it can no longer be edited. This lock should show which items the rubric is linked to , so if an instructor needs to edit the rubric they can see items they need to remove the rubric from to edit it. 

This could be done by 
 # Creating a link/tooltip in the lock icon, so clicking on it or hovering over it would show linked items
 # Adding a linked items link which opens in a flyout under one of the existing columns
 # Adding a linked items column with a list of items the rubric is linked to. The listed items should be links which the instructor can click to access the items and change them without having to manually search for them.(See Attached)

summary: Site Info > upgrade to Apache FOP 2.0+
description:
In SAK-41909 we upgraded the {{xmlgraphics-commons}} library from 1.5 to 2.3. This caused the Site Info > Manage Participants > Printable View to stop working, because site-manage is still using Apache FOP v1.0, which requires a method that's not present in {{xmlgraphics-commons}} v2.0+.

As a stop-gap measure, we added the v1.5 of {{xmlgraphics-commons}} back to the site-manage project so that the feature will work again in the interim (SAK-42346). However, this is only a temporary solution. The proper fix here is to upgrade site-info to Apache FOP v2.0+.

The library versions are defined in {{site-manage/site-manage-tool/tool/pom.xml}}:

{code:xml}
        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.apache.xmlgraphics</groupId>
            <artifactId>fop</artifactId>
            <version>1.0</version>
        </dependency>

        <!-- This old version of xmlgraphics-commons is needed to support Manage Participants > Printable View.
             With the newer (2.3) version (provided by master's pom.xml), you'll get a runtime NoSuchMethodError on org.apache.xmlgraphics.xmp.Metadata.mergeInto(Lorg/apache/xmlgraphics/xmp/Metadata;)V.
             Until the code in SiteInfoToolServlet.generatePDF() is updated to use FOP v2.0+, this needs to stay here. -->
        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.apache.xmlgraphics</groupId>
            <artifactId>xmlgraphics-commons</artifactId>
            <version>1.5</version>
        </dependency>
{code}

The code that needs to be updated is located in {{SiteInfoToolServlet.generatePDF()}} (possibly other locations that generate PDFs in the Site Info tool).

summary: Convert ckeditor data uri base64 images to Resources linked images
description:
https://groups.google.com/a/apereo.org/g/sakai-dev/c/ZR8VEOXMg3c/m/HsITfWsRCAAJ

Is there any way to NOT have ckeditor save pasted in images (or source with base64) as an embedded base64 image?  And instead, automatically add the image to resources and have the ckeditor source link to it?

This plugin looks like it might have some of those features:

https://ckeditor.com/cke4/addon/imagepaste

In our case, we have a class that uses Etudes Meme - Assignments, Tests, Surveys (but I suspect this could happen with Samigo too) and it has 1000s of questions in several question pools.  Many of those questions contain base64 images, which I suspect the instructor pasted into ckeditor.  And I think because of the base64 images, we're seeing some slow queries accessing that tool for that site.

Also, that instructor imports those tests from one semester to the next so the problem continues to happen each semester.  It would be great if we could automatically convert those existing base64 images into an actual file in resources and link to it from the test. (otherwise, we'd have to ask the instructor to manually convert each image into a resources image link)

I also suspect that many sites have pasted in bas64 images into their Overview tool -> Worksite Information.

Further, when I've analyzed Heap Dumps, there are lots of objects in memory that look like base64 images, which I suspect come from the examples above.

summary: Lessons: Add Content Link -> URL ignores item name
description:
In 21, the add content link workflow changed a bit.  Now when a user adds a URL via content link, there is a new Custom Name field.  Prior to 21, the link just used the Item Name field.  I think it should use the Item Name field if no Custom Name is provided.  However, the Custom Name field is not being retained on Edit.  So, if a user wants to modify the link, they see the Item Name still shows what was added in Custom Name previously but, when you save, if you don’t re-add the custom name field, it gets blanked out and the URL is now used as the title of the content link.

summary: Date Manager: Remove the use of the jQuery datepicker in favor of datetime-local
description:
The date manager uses the jQuery datepicker which can take some time if the number of items is very high, see SAK-46122.

I suggest moving the jQuery date picker to datetime-local input objects, that could be a more long term solution.

https://www.w3schools.com/tags/att_input_type_datetime-local.asp

summary: Search: Announcement search results not respecting date settings
description: If a student uses the Search WC or tool to search for an announcement, they can view that announcement, even if the specified dates should make it unavailable to them.

summary: Conversations | Statistics reporting incorrect numbers
description:
The Conversations Statistics panel does not seem to be totaling correctly. In a test site with multiple topics, answers, comments & reactions created/added by different students, the Stats table continues to show zeros where known activity has occurred for a user.

Examples

# Topics Created - Multiple users have created a topic yet all users still have zeros
# Topics Read - Reporting 1s for some users but known users have read multiple topics that are available
# Reactions - Multiple users have added reactions yet all users still have zeros
# Posts - Multiple users have added posts/answers to topics yet all users still have zeros

Are the stats run on a periodic cron? Dynamically built every time an instructor goes to stats page?

Is ‘Topics Read’ count reading a topic a user created themself?

summary: Search: Assignments with rich text display html tags in search results
description: Announcements with rich text only display the text, while assignments display all the html tags when using site or portal search. The html tags need to be removed from the assignment search results. See screenshots for differences between announcements and assignments.

summary: Tests & Quizzes: Show owner of question pools used in tests
description:
We have tests that are randomly drawn from question pools that were created in shared template sites, and multiple instructors copied the tests to their own classes. At this point, an instructor needs to update a pool, but it is no longer clear who the owner is. 

I would like some means of identifying the owner of a particular question pool from the assessment builder page.

Current text: 

Part 1 Random draw from <Pool 1> - # questions

The questions for this part were generated from the question pool, *<Pool 1>*, on *<date>* at *<time>*. To get latest changes made to the pool, click *Update Questions* or click *Edit* for this Part and then click *Save*. Clicking *Preview* or *Publish* will automatically update the pool-drawn questions as will exporting an assessment.

My suggestion: 

Part 1 Random draw from <Pool 1> - # questions

The questions for this part were generated from the question pool, *<Pool 1>* {color:#ff5630}*(owned by <userID>)*{color}{color:#ff5630},{color} on *<date>* at *<time>*. To get latest changes made to the pool, click *Update Questions* or click *Edit* for this Part and then click *Save*. Clicking *Preview* or *Publish* will automatically update the pool-drawn questions as will exporting an assessment.



This way, knowing who owns the pool would enable the instructor to poke them about updating the pool(s), or, if the owner is no longer with the institution, work with their Sakai admin to share or transfer ownership of these pools.

summary: Conversations: In Chrome, Using Keyboard to Access Bookmark, Pin, or the Elipsis in Answer Does Not Have Border to Indicate Selection/Active
description: When using keyboard (<Tab> <Enter>) to move through Conversations screen, the user is able to delete a new question, as the elipsis has a border to show it is active, and pressing Enter opens options. Using the Tab key to move through the remainder of the screen, there is no border indicating when the user has reached Bookmark, Pin, or the elipsis in the Instructor’s Answer area.

summary: When adding items to a GB category, category order does not match GB settings.
description: In Gradebook settings, the instructor can control the order of the categories. This seems to control the order the categories are displayed in within the gradebook when items are grouped by category. However, when selecting a category for an item (either in Gradebook, or in Tests & Quizzes or Assignments) the category order is all messed up. It’s not in the order of the settings page. It isn’t in alphabetical order. It’s not in the order the categories were created in. I feel that when selecting the category for an item, that list should be in the same order as the GB settings page.

summary: Assignments: Instructor is now forced to send a graded assignment to the gradebook
description:
This is not an issue on 22. On trunk, if the instructor creates a graded assignment, they are forced to send it to the gradebook if the Grade Scale is points. The option “Create new Gradebook item” is now a radio button, so cannot be deselected. The instructor should not be forced to send something to the GB.

I have not found a Jira where this change is mentioned, so I believe this is incorrect.

summary: LTI Content Item links in the Rich Text Editor should be updated when importing content from another site
description:
The work on this Jira is documented in this 6 hour long video:  [https://youtu.be/SzgUtgYB_4E|https://youtu.be/SzgUtgYB_4E|smart-link] 

After configuring a content item in LTI for use with the rich text editor, it is possible to embed content any location that the rich text editor is used.

When this content is then imported to a new site the embedded content will not work since the link belongs to the old site. Note that for users that members in the old site as well as the new site then the embedded content will work.

To be fixed - all are both site copy and CC+Archive import:

* Assignments
* Announcements (Site copy only - adding merge() support is another JIRA)
* Calendar
* Polls
* Syllabus - Also de-duplicate syllabus items on CC+Archive import
* Discussions  - Also de-duplicate in CC+Archive import
* Conversations - A CC+Archive implementation is needed - separate JIRA
* Lessons - Already works before this patch, feel free to retest

Content Item links from the old site should be migrated to the new site when content is imported.

summary: When a group is created on Section Info, the user who has created should be assigned TA automatically
description:
When a user (instructor or teaching assistant) creates a new section in the Section Info tool, it might be interesting to have it automatically added as a TA.

This would avoid an extra step for the user. If he/she is not interested, he/she can always delete it but, in our institution, this happens less often than the opposite case.

summary: Admin Site Management: Add/Edit groups seems to be missing property fields
description:
I’m not sure exactly how the Add/Edit groups is supposed to work as an admin in sites, but the test plan in the regression scripts does not work. If the instructor creates a group in a site, and the admin searches for the site and clicks on Add/Edit groups > group link, there are 2 properties: group_prop_view_members & group_prop_wsetup_created.

If the admin then creates a group while in the add/edit group page, those properties are not there and the instructor does not see the group in the site that the admin created.

If I’m not understanding how this should work, please add an explanation and a test plan that can be followed successfully so it can be added to our regression scripts.

summary: Roster: Clear button should not reset Layout setting
description:
The ‘Clear’ button in the Roster tool resets the Layout to the default value of ‘Card’ whereas this setting should retain its previous value when the name filter is cleared.

More details are in the Test Plan and the attached screencast, RosterClearButtonResetsLayout.mp4.

summary: Roster tool does not retain "No results found" upon switching layout
description: After having entered a search in Roster which yields no results, switching to a different layout will incorrectly display last successful user search, or a cleared search (i.e. all participants on the roster) if there is no previous successful search. Switching layout should instead preserve the search between layouts, results found or not.

The file in the resource folder contains the collection_id, which is the connection to these tables. The hardDelete of a course sites removes this file, but the corresponding citations remain in the database.

summary: Assignments: Peer review assignments imported published do not assign reviewers
description:
If an instructor imports assignments published into a new course site, any peer assessment assignments are not distributed for peer review unless the instructor edits and reposts the assignment. There is no indication this is a problem until the peer review period starts, and then only if the instructor goes into the grade screen to see that the peer reviewers are not assigned. 

Ideally, the peer review assignments should be fixed so they will distribute the peer assessments without the instructor needing to re-post the assignment.  If this isn’t feasible, a good alternative would be to have any peer review assignments unable to be imported published, but always import as drafts, like group assignments do, so it is clear to the instructor at a glance that it needs to be reposted in order to work.

summary: Rubrics-Tests & Quizzes: Clicking the grading rubric tab displays the rubric below the response
description:
Possibly [https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-48837|https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-48837|smart-link] broke how the rubrics display in T&Q when grading. Each question has a tab called Student Response and a Grading Rubric tab. Previously, and on 22, when the instructor clicks to grade a quiz by clicking the student’s name, the Student Response would display, then clicking the Grading Rubric tab would only display the rubric.

Currently, the first time Grading Rubric is clicked, it displays beneath the student’s response. Clicking Student Response then hides the Grading Rubric. Clicking Grading Rubric again the only displays the rubric as expected.

summary: Gradebook should support removal of data when a site is hard deleted

When a site is hard deleted Gradebook should remove all of it’s related data for that site.
Note: Sakai 22 and earlier versions do implement ContextObserver in class GradebookNgContextObserver.

summary: Lessons: Unable to post to Discussion when prerequisite option set
description:
If an instructor links to a forum topic, setting the option to not release until prerequisites are completed, when a student completes that prerequisite (or if there are no prerequisites), the button to Start a New Conversation is missing. 

The button appears as expected if the topic does not have the prerequisite option set. If the instructor edits the link in Lessons and removes the prerequisite, the Start a New Conversation button appears. 

Update - 2/24/2025: Did more digging - it looks like the Lessons prerequsite option isn’t setting the permissions  in the Discussion topic. It’s changing the permissions for the Student role to “None”, but isn’t setting the corresponding Access: group to “Contributor”.

Due date is passed, however late responses are accepted

summary: Modify the default behaviour of the "mark as read" in the forums tool.
description:
This is a suggestion made to us by a group of teachers in our institution and we thought it was quite reasonable.

In some of our subjects we make quite a lot of use of the Virtual Classroom Forum, and I wanted to suggest a change to the 'Mark as read' functionality, which I think could improve the user experience for teachers and students.

As the tool is currently configured, it is not enough to read a message for it to be marked as read, but you have to click on the 'Mark as read' sign. In other words, the default option is that the message is not marked as read, even if it has been opened for viewing.

Naturally, most people who use the tool do not take the trouble to mark as read every message they have read, and this has two undesirable consequences:

(1) When a teacher checks the number of messages that a student has read, he/she sees the number of messages that he/she has clicked on as read, instead of the number of messages that he/she has opened and presumably actually read. So, if a student does not take the trouble to mark as read each message that he/she has actually read, it may appear to the teacher that he/she has not read any of them, which may result in an unfair assessment of his/her attention to the Forum.

If the aim is to avoid the mischievousness of students opening messages and closing them quickly, without having actually read them, it should be pointed out that this mischievousness is not avoided by the requirement to 'mark as read'. This is so for two quite obvious reasons: firstly, because a student can open messages and mark them as read quickly, without reading them. And secondly, because the tool itself allows one to stand at the top of a conversation and mark all messages as read one after the other, without even opening them.

(2) The second undesirable consequence of the current configuration is that when a person (whether teacher or student) opens a message in the Forum, the number of people who have read it is indicated. But this number, once again, does not correspond to the people who have opened that message and presumably have in fact read it, but corresponds to the people who have clicked on those messages as read.

The result is that a message may appear as having been read by 2 participants when in fact it has been read by 25. I therefore suggest that the default option of the tool should be that when a message is opened and the text is displayed, it is automatically marked as read.

And along with this suggestion, I would like to make an additional and complementary suggestion, and that is that the little boxes that currently allow you to 'Mark as read' messages, be changed to precisely the opposite, 'Mark as unread', for the special case in which someone wants to highlight a message to read it again later.

Moreover, this change is more in line with the reality of the words themselves: if I open a message to read it, it is normal to assume that I have read it. The requirement to mark it as read is, in my view, an excessive and unjustified burden.

Finally, it should be noted that in other communication tools, such as email managers or wassaps, it is unthinkable that the tool would require you to mark every message you open as read. The default option is 'message open = message read'. And the special option is that there is a procedure to 'mark as unread' a particular message, despite having opened it, because you want to remember it for whatever reason.

Thanks.

summary: Gradebook: support for group instances and update external integrations
description:
Gradebook tool is used for grading different items, configuring weights and categories which allow a customized final grade calculation. Unfortunately, just a single configuration is possible on each site, which can generate conflicts when instructors have different points of view. This development will add support for grading in different ways each of the existing groups on a site, adjusting configuration to the preferences of the teachers associated to each one, using the same options currently available at site level.

Some notes referring the initial scope of this feature:

* The GB ui will be the same as it is, changes are just on making the backend work at group level instead than at site level separating the previous siteId = gradebookUid simplification.
* A new vuecomponent multiselect to pick one entry (item or category) from the available gradebooks has been added.
* No database changes are required.
* It can be disabled by property.
* For this feature to work there must be some restrictions/validations:
** Enabled by site info configuration, similar to other tools with multiple instances.
** IMPORTANT: in order to try to provide a simple common solution for every different case, considering usablity and trying to reduce duplicated code as much as possible, when creating an assignment or an assessment assigned to these gradebook instances *group selection is delegated in the existing group options of each tool*. Validation of the matches between the seleced groups and the existing gradebooks takes places when trying to create/update.
** A student can belong to different gradebooks on a site, but can only be member of one of the groups assigned to an item (similar to group submissions)
** There won't be a site-level gradebook tool on these sites (mode can be switched from site to group and data will be kept, just can’t be groups AND site at the same time).

summary: Roster: Separate user ID from default view
description:
In Roster tool, the OOB permissions allow only the instructor/maintain role to view all participants. Students by default see only the instructor role. Instructors may want to allow students to view all participants so they can see their peer’s name, profile, picture, and other profile information. The permission to view all participants includes all user’s Sakai profile picture, name, nickname, pronounciation, user ID, and role. Viewing the user’s email address is a separate permission that can be modified for the site. 

In the US, the user ID may not be directory information released by FERPA. There’s very few other locations in Sakai that allows students to see other student’s IDs. (only other one I could find was assignments group submissions) It seems odd that Roster does include the user ID if the default permission is changed to allow students to view their classmates. 

I would like to see viewing the user ID as a separate permission like email. Institutions that consider the User IDs to be directory information can then share them, and those that consider those protected information can allow students to view all participants without sharing the IDs.

However, after importing site content, instructors with hidden tools then have to go back to Site Info > Tool Order and re-hide (or re-lock) all of the hidden/locked tools that were copied. summary: Tests & Quizzes: Allow question to be copied into the current question pool (duplicate question)

There is a good use case for allowing the instructor to duplicate question(s) in the current pool. If they are creating a set of questions that follow a common theme, it is much faster to copy a question then edit then to create a new one with the same text and answer options.

Also, this limitation against duplicate questions only protects against copying a question into it’s existing pool. An instructor can create a copy in a temporary pool, then copy it from the temp pool back to the main pool. It doesn’t check to make sure they don’t manually create two identical questions. It feels a bit arbitrary, when you can have duplicate questions created by other methods, but not using the Copy functionality.

summary: Assignments/LTI Add a "release grades automatically" option for LTI Assignments
description:
Currently, when you create an LTI Assignment type and configure the assignment settings to go to the Gradebook, the LTI score is not actually sent to the gradebook until the instructor releases the grades for that assignment. While the release grades feature is useful when hand-grading assignments, it is much less useful in the case of LTI assignments which are graded automatically. In fact, the need to release the grades in order for students to see them in the gradebook adds an extra task for the instructor for auto-graded LTI assignments, since instructors must go in and release grades for each assignment. 

This is not the case in Lessons. When you add a graded or auto-graded LTI item on a Lessons page, it will send the grade immediately without the need to manually release grades. However, Lessons does not give you many of the other features that are part of Assignments, such as due dates, email notifications, reminders, calendar events, etc. which make using the Assignments tool preferable to using Lessons for LTI items.

I would like to propose that we add a “release grades automatically” option in the assignment settings screen for LTI assignments. The default behavior can remain as it is, with grades requiring release. However, having the option to automatically release scores when sent via LTI would be a nice time-saver when used with automatically graded LTI items. 

I’ve included a mockup below. Perhaps this new option could be grayed out or not shown at all for non-LTI assignments.

summary: Enable a side-by-side view for grading student submissions in Assignments on desktop
description:
At today’s T&L/UX call, we discussed feedback from faculty in writing intensive courses about the new grading UI in Assignments in Sakai 23. Faculty are saying that that the new mobile-friendly grading interface in Assignments is actually making grading slower for desktop users. The problem is that the grading panel slides out from the right, overlapping the student submission and making the submission content area inactive. Since it is inactive, there is no way to scroll or view additional student submission content. Faculty have to close the grading panel in order to scroll up or down or to view the entire width of the submission. While closing the grading panel is usually quick when it is empty, after some feedback has been entered, it takes some time to save the feedback (maybe a second or two, depending on the amount of feedback) before the panel closes. This slows down the entire process. 

See the screenshot of the current interface below.

!gradingui-current.jpg|width=100%,alt="gradingui-current.jpg"!



A side-by-side view is typically preferred when grading on a large screen such as a desktop. Therefore, we would like to propose that the student submission content not be made inactive, and that the grading panel appear side-by-side (instead of overlapping) by default when viewed on the desktop. This will make it possible for faculty to view the student submission with the grading panel open, which will speed up the grading process overall. 

See proposed mockup below. (We acknowledge that the double scrollbars may need some work.)

!assignment-grader-side-by-side.jpg|width=100%,alt="assignment-grader-side-by-side.jpg"!



 Comments and suggestions on the proposed change are welcome!

summary: T&Q SEB - Autosave modal message is sometimes permanently displayed
description:
SAK-46026 added a modal window that warns the users their work is being saved automatically. When the modal window is showed, buttons are disabled and the form data is saved. Then buttons are enabled again and the modal window is hidden. User can continue with the test.

We have autosave configured every minute (60000 ms) and we have been using this feature for years without known issues so far. But after adding Safe Exam Browser tool to our exams, we have found one same issue in two different scenarios.

1) In some exams with 30-40 students we have been reported that for one or two students the modal autosaving window is showed and then it never dissapears. It can't be closed in any way. As users are browsing in a locked window they can't continue with the test. Even restarting the computer and the exam the modal window still remains.

This is very hard to test, we don't know the conditions to cause the error. There are other exams that have been completed without issues, but when this happens teachers and students have a very bad experience.

2) When SEB is configured with an exit button, we have found that starting a test, exiting from SEB with the button, starting SEB again and continuing the test always fails, causing the modal to be permanently in screen and preventing to continue the exam.

This always happens in our 22.5 version, so we have a test plan. I have tested it in master QA server and it happens too.

summary: LTI Add the Personal Needs and Preferences (PNP) url to the LTI 1.3 Launch Data
description:
The “Learning Tools Interoperability (LTI)® Access For All Personal Needs and Preferences (AfA PNP) Connector Service” is an “almost final” 1EdTech specification:

[https://www.imsglobal.org/sites/default/files/spec/afa/3p0/connector_service/1edtech-ltipnp-servicev1.html|https://www.imsglobal.org/sites/default/files/spec/afa/3p0/connector_service/1edtech-ltipnp-servicev1.html|smart-link] 

In the fullness of time, the overall PNP specification might end up with a pretty significant influence on Sakai and other LMS’s.  PNP itself has a large data model which will be adopted in its own time.  Those specifications are still in draft and not publicly accessible as of 3-Dec-2024 - these links will break unless you are an 1EdTech member:

[https://www.imsglobal.org/afa/afapnpv1p0/imsafapnpservicev1p0_confcertcfv1p0.html|https://www.imsglobal.org/afa/afapnpv1p0/imsafapnpservicev1p0_confcertcfv1p0.html]

[https://www.imsglobal.org/afa/afav3p0/imsafapnpv3p0_infomodelpdv2p0.html|https://www.imsglobal.org/afa/afav3p0/imsafapnpv3p0_infomodelpdv2p0.html]

However, tool vendors, governments, and other institutions are starting to experiment with the spec as part of the later stages of approval.  This Jira will add a single claim to LTI launches to communicate to tools what the currently configured PNP Rest endpoint URL is for the current logged in user.   It is pretty simple and low risk to add this launch parameter to Sakai’s LTI implementation to facilitate further work and testing using Sakai as a test platform and for demos of this important work - especially in the area of large scale assessments.

Here is an example of a PNP profile we can use for testing this feature

[https://pnp.amp-up.io/ims/afapnp/v1p0/users/[email]/activities/default/afapnprecords|https://pnp.amp-up.io/ims/afapnp/v1p0/users/[email]/activities/default/afapnprecords]

Adding this support to Sakai was proposed by Paul Grudnitski of [amp-up.io|https://amp-up.io] and for a while he will be its primary user as part of his work with QTI 3.0 - which in time we might find very interesting inside of Sakai.

To enable this requires two properties described as follows:

{code:none}# Configure a 1EdTech Personal Needs & Preferences (PNP) Server
# The @ sign is a place holder in the PNP URL for either the user_id or email (see below)
# lti.pnp.baseurl=https://pnp.amp-up.io/ims/afapnp/v1p0/users/@/activities/default/afapnprecords
# DEFAULT: none

# Normally for PNP we include the user_id value from the LTI launch.  How the user_id is
# set in Sakai and in the PNP server is a bit of a complex issue but using the user_id
# from the launch if the right default.  However, sometimes for testing it is simpler to
# user the email so a tester can reliable re-create a user on an empty system to test
# PNP.  Setting this to true is fine on dev or test servers but probably is not suitable
# on a production system.  If there is no PNP base URL, this value has no effect.
# lti.pnp.use_email=false
# DEFAULT: false{code}

Apache FreeMarker™ is a template engine: a Java library to generate
text output (HTML web pages, e-mails, configuration files, source
code, etc.) based on templates and changing data. Templates are
written in the FreeMarker Template Language (FTL), which is a simple,
specialized language. Usually, a general-purpose programming language
(like Java) is used to prepare the data (issue database queries, do
business calculations). Then, Apache FreeMarker displays that prepared
data using templates. In the template you are focusing on how to
present the data, and outside the template you are focusing on what
data to present.

on behalf of the Apache FreeMarker community

summary: Site titles with ampersands distorted during publishing
description:
If a site title contains an ampersand (e.g., “R&D Trends 2025”), the site title will be distorted when manually publishing the site (i.e., not during a scheduled publish nor during any unpublishing event).

After which the site in the topmost breadcrumb will display the ampersand HTML entity (e.g., “R&D Trends 2025”). The SAKAI_SITE.TITLE also reflects a change where an ampersand is replaced with the ampersand HTML entity. Given this change in the actual title, this bug exacerbates the critical jira: [https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-49823|https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-49823|smart-link] , causing more instances of that problem, which is why I’ve designated this jira as critical, too. (I’m not sure if this bug similarly affects 22.x.)

summary: Student View broken for TAs
description:
We have a use case where an institution would like their TAs to be able to use the Student View. In 22.x they were able to do this. However, with the changes to Student View in 23.x, they are no longer able to use this feature. 

We have completed the following steps, which should make this feature available for the Teaching Assistant role.

# Modify the sakai.properties to remove Teaching Assistant from the following list: "studentview.roles=Student,Teaching Assistant,access"
# Add the “site.roleswap” permission for the Teaching Assistant role. 

Nevertheless, if you log in as a TA after completed the above steps, the Student View appears to be broken.

The “Enter Student View” link does now appear for the TA user, as shown below:

!ta-student-view1.png|width=91.66666666666667%,alt="ta-student-view1.png"!

But, if you select the Enter Student View link, you get a message that the site isn’t available and the site and tool links in the left hand navigation disappear.

!ta-student-view2.png|width=91.66666666666667%,alt="ta-student-view2.png"!

Selecting the Exit Student View button does return you to the normal TA view, but it seems to kick you out of the site. 

!ta-student-view3.png|width=91.66666666666667%,alt="ta-student-view3.png"!

Luckily, the tool menu links do reappear, so it is possible to navigate back to the original site using the left menu. However, it is not a good user experience to see the Site Unavailable message.

(Note: The Instructor Student View works fine. This issue is only present for the TA role.)

summary: Gradebook Keyboard Accessibility Issues in Sakai 25
description:
Some issues I found when testing with the keyboard only for Gradebook in Sakai 25 on trunk. 

* When using the tab key to navigate through the Gradebook table, you cannot go from one row to the next. You can tab through the first row but cannot move to the next row. In Sakai 23, you can go from row to row using the tab key. In Sakai 23, you tab to the end of the current row you are on and then the next tab keystroke will bring you to the next row in the Gradebook table.
* The first row in the Gradebook table is not accessible. The first row with all the column headers you cannot access using the keyboard. It automatically goes to the first student upon entering the Gradebook table. I was thinking you may want to rearrange some columns in some instances. So this would be nice if we could access the first row of the Gradebook table. 
* The gear icon inside the Gradebook table entries I could not access using the keyboard. Maybe there is a keystroke that I am missing to access them?

summary: Assignments: Submission can delete previous entered/released grade and comment.
description:
A released grade and/or feedback comment is removed from the assignment if a student submits the assignment where they previously have not (i.e. it had been graded by instructor without submission). Additionally, if the assignment is configured to use the gradebook the grade and comment *can persist in the gradebook such that the gradebook and the assignment do not match.

The use case that made the assignment/grade removal behavior evident was an instructor’s assignment that was accepted via paper in class or via Sakai. The instructor entered and returned grades in the Assignment tool for the assignments turned via paper. However, a few students later (additionally or by mis-communication) also submitted via Sakai resulting in the grading the instructor had done for the paper submissions to be removed from Sakai.

Adding further confusion for the instructor, the assignment submission status became “Re-submitted”. (fyi: the Allow Resubmission box was not checked) 

See attached video.

The removal of a grade/comment is incorrect behavior. If an assignment grade/comment has been released by the instructor, that should prevent a subsequent submission by the student (provided the assignment is not configured to allow resubmission).

*An exception to the gradebook behavior noted earlier is if the instructor subsequently uses the legacy grading interface and either navigates between submissions or uses the ‘Return to List’ link. In that case the grade or comment of the submission visited is deleted. This does not happen if using the new grading interface.

Perhaps it would be appropriate for the Teaching & Learning group to consider/weigh in on the desired Sakai behavior for the use case(s) described in this jira.

1-17-2025 - An additional data point:  Once the students click Proceed, but before they Submit or if then don’t Submit but Save Draft, the status changes to “Ungraded - in progress” (see attached image) and the grade/comment is removed (relegated to past submission section if viewing using the legacy grading interface). If student Submits then or at a later time the status change to “Re-submitted” as described at the start of this ticket write-up. Just as above it would be expected that this behavior wouldn’t happen because once a grade has been returned the student should no longer be able create a submission (unless “Allow Resubmission” was checked).

summary: Resources: Locked Resources should not block the hidden Attachments folder
description:
If access to the Resources tool is locked, it doesn’t just block access to the files and folders listed there, but to the hidden Resources as well. This makes it so students can’t attach files to Assignments, Messages, or access files attached to Announcements, Messages, Assignments, Tests & Quizzes, or other items. 

The QA team and Earle discussed this at a recent QA meeting, and we agreed that locking the Resources should just lock access to the items that the instructor would see listed in Resources, that an instructor wouldn’t necessarily expect locking Resources to block attaching files to other tools, or viewing files that are not visible in Resources.

summary: Peer Review-Rubrics: Instructor does not see the peer review rubric when grading
description:
Testing [https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/S2U-34|https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/S2U-34|smart-link] 

After the peer reviews have finished, and the instructor grades, after clicking Grade Submission the peer review rubric is not available for the instructor to view.

When a student does a self-review, there is an autoevaluation button in the Sakai grader that allows the instructor to view the student’s self-review. I think there should be a button for the peer review rubric also so the instructor can view it as they grade.

summary: Gradebook: rubrics view for group submission does not display graded rubric
description:
I believe this is related to [https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/S2U-34|https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/S2U-34|smart-link] and [https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-50916|https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-50916|smart-link] 

I’m not sure what the expectations are for group-submission self-reporting assignments, but the regular group-submission assignments with a rubric no longer display the graded rubric in the Gradebook. This also affects the Grade Summary when clicking on a student’s name (instructor role).

There is also an issue with the individual self-reporting assignment, but that will be a separate Jira. This case does not even display the rubric icon in the gradebook, but has an error in the server logs.

I think the group submission assignment without self-reporting should display the rubric when clicking on the icon in the gradebook, as it does on 23x.

The expected behavior of a group-submission with self-reporting needs to be determined and am adding TL to this Jira.

summary: Grader: Intended ‘Submission History’ button not displayed
description:
The scope of this jira is intended to:

# primarily fix a bug coincident with [https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-49836|https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-49836|smart-link], where a ‘Submission History’ feature for Grader was developed but not fully realized given that it never displays. (Refer to the test plan and the attached screenshots for expected behavior, SubHistoryButton-PanelCollapsed.png and SubHistoryButton-PanelExpanded.png.)
# secondarily (and longer term) advocate for the preservation in Grader of this student submission event log data-- such as when a student saves a draft. This data is absent from the proposed feature request, [https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-50264|https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-50264|smart-link]. (I’m not implying here though that it wasn’t considered, as I’m not privy to that context.)

Regarding the second point, our institution’s instructors have benefited in a number of cases by having the submission log in Assignments-- specifically, the legacy grader. I also assume that Grader will ultimately supersede the legacy grader for some future version of Sakai. 

Without having to resort to the valuable, yet more cumbersome Statistics tool for similar data, our admins and instructors have found the presence of the student submission log in the Assignments grading interface valuable. I can elaborate on this later, but for now just want to acknowledge here that SAK-50264 is at least relevant to and may somewhat be in tension with addressing and fixing the first point above. 

(I also recognize/anticipate non-trivial design issues inherent to integrating the preservation of the legacy ‘History’/’Submission History’ and the newer revised ‘Submission History’ proposed in SAK-50264, especially if the two were to “independently” coincide on the same grading view. E.g., how to name these two features to distinguish them? I defer all that to later or some other forum as needed.)

summary: SAK-50945 Assignment cc+archive should not export group data
description:
When importing a cc+ file containing a group submission assignment, the assignment changes from Assign to: “The selected group(s), as a group assignment” to “Each individual member of the site”, which I was expecting since I do not have the groups in the import site. 

However, the little icon indicating it’s a “group submission” is still present, and I did not expect that:

!image-20250202-215821.png|width=465,height=92,alt="image-20250202-215821.png"!

Just an FYI how site import handles this: When doing a Site Info > Import from Site, it does keep this as a group submission assignment and creates the groups in the “import” site.

!image-20250202-220341.png|width=717,height=349,alt="image-20250202-220341.png"!

From [user] The cc+archive export should turn off groups submissions and not include groups so imported assignments should revert to site-wide assignments.  Groups can be added post import.  Site copy and Site Archive import have different behavior because CC+Archive is never to include any student personal information at all.

I went on a spelunking mission.  This is what I found.

There is no code anywhere in Sakai that reads a Zip (CC, CC+Archive, Site Archive) and creates groups empty or otherwise.  “Import from Site” is not a ZIP at all and it does copy groups as we have seen.

Further I reproduced things and looked at the archive outputs did a bunch of imports and checked if things can be patched up when a group Assignments passes through a ZIP file.

I will say that it works swell as is.  I have attached some screen shots.  As mentioned in the JIRA you see a group icon in the assignments list but no groups.  There are no empty groups in Site Info.  If you go into the assignment there is  wonderfully helpful message about groups no longer existing that tells you to either go make groups and come back or just safe it and the assignment will be de-groupified when published.

This feels awesome to me.  It does the best it can leaving hints in plain site and then lets the user fix it up.

I took the opportunity to tidy things up a bit.  I made sure the roles got exported minus which user was in which role - I hade deleted all this but put it back minus the user id list.   The roles are in site.xml but have never been imported from a ZIP.  I also put back the group data in assignment.xml.  It is just a list of group (no names) we would need to add some export and import code for groups later and having the group ids (but not the users) in assignments will allow for easy reconnect later.

Sooo.

If you really want to make best effort importing empty groups and all that - it will take a bunch of new code - and so it is a feature request.

I will update the current  SAK-50945 JIRA with lots of detail about how stuff rolls with some sample cartridges, etc and a test plan for QA of the changes I did make under the auspices of the JIRA.

summary: Avoiding the use of CSS utility classes within webcomponents
description:
Reviewing the changes made between Sakai 22, which we have right now, and master (Sakai 25) and the new trinity interface, I have seen that utility classes have been used within the JS components, for example, sakai notifications [https://github.com/sakaiproject/sakai/blob/master/webcomponents/tool/src/main/frontend/packages/sakai-notifications/src/SakaiNotifications.js.|https://github.com/sakaiproject/sakai/blob/master/webcomponents/tool/src/main/frontend/packages/sakai-notifications/src/SakaiNotifications.js.|smart-link] 

This creates a small problem for us when it comes to adapting the corporate images that the communication departments require us to maintain uniformity between all the applications of our institution.

Until now, in Sakai 22, we only had to adapt the skin inside the library and create our own. By using utility classes in the velocity, it also forces us to adapt them, which would not be a major problem. In the case of our instance, we have two different corporate images (one specific to UMU and the other to Universia, belonging to Banco Santander) using two different skins (not only colours, they require us to make deeper changes such as weight or size of the font used between the different skins).

The approach we are using right now with the skin, and that we will use with the velocity, is to have a copy of what the community has so that, if it is necessary to apply a patch, we would apply it as it is and then adapt it to our changes, which so far is the easiest and fastest way to do it.

But, when it comes to using the webcomponents, we do think it is more likely that we will need to fix behaviours of the webcomponents to add new functionality or bug fixes, so we would like to have exactly the same, unadapted, webcomponents that the whole community has. We don't think it is feasible to have a copy of each of the webcomponents just to maintain a different CSS / styling classes.

Our proposal would be as follows:

* *Add BEM / similar / semantic classes in the webcomponents*. For the example above, use a sakai-notifications class that matches the name of the webcomponent and, from there, the rest of them. We don't care what methodology you use if you prefer another one, as long as it is semantic.
* *Take out the utility classes used in each webcomponent and inject into it a CSS style generated* with [user] or similar from these same utility classes but inside the library using SCSS, similar to what the [user] of Tailwind CSS can do. This would allow adaptability to different corporate images from within the skin itself.
* *Pass an optional className attribute to any webcomponent* that is injected into the rendering of the webcomponent, which would allow only the velocity to be changed.

summary: Lessons Conditions - View items based on grades/requirements
description:
The recent enhancement [https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/S2U-35|https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/S2U-35|smart-link]  allows users to create conditions for items to be used as prerequisites for other items on the page. Unlike the existing requirements/prerequisites feature in Lessons, these conditions do not have to be in a linear order on the page. You can also apply more than one condition as a prerequisite. All of these things add nice new functionality to Lessons. 

However, in reviewing the feature, the T&L/UX group thought it was very confusing to use, since it operates completely separate from the existing Lessons requirements/prereqs, but it is still similar enough to cause users to confuse the two. It is not clear if or when the two can be used together, or if one takes precedence over the other. There is also a bit of overlap in both the terminology used and in the functionality (at least for linear items) of the feature. T&L/UX feels that it is important to merge the two features together so that they can be used in conjunction more easily and so it is more obvious to users how the features work.

In addition, there is no visual cue for the instructor to let them know if/when a condition has been created for an item, or applied to another item. This means that they have to edit each individual item and open up the prereq section just to determine if a condition is associated with each item on a page. In the existing Lessons req/prereq feature, a note visible only to instructors is added next to each item stating that the prerequisites exist. Something like this is needed for the new conditions prerequisites as well.

The T&L/UX group also felt that adding gradebook items as potential condition elements is an important missing feature. Rather than limiting the conditions to assignments, quizzes, and inline questions (which are already available to be added as prerequisites with/without points via the existing Lessons requirements system), integrating the condition feature to pull from the Gradebook would have a number of benefits:

* Anything in the gradebook could be used as a condition, including all assignments, quizzes, and questions if they are being sent to the gradebook. This would allow for the removal of what seems like partially duplicate functionality.
* All GB items could appear in the list automatically, removing the need to first add the condition to one item, and then select it as a prerequisite on another item. The condition (i.e. point value) could be specified at the time the condition is selected as a prereq.
* Most importantly, it would open up the ability to use other items like Discussions, Conversations, Student Content, LTI items, and even GB Categories, or the final Course Grade as a condition for release of content. This would be a huge step forward in creating learning paths and self-paced, adaptive style content within Lessons.
* Having all gradebook items would also enable the specification of requirements across pages - something which is now not possible with either the existing Lessons reqs/prereqs, or the newer conditions system.

For these reasons, we would like to propose the following changes:

# Modify the UI so that it visually combines all of the requirement/condition settings into a more cohesive set of options. Having them broken into two different sections with very different UIs is a big part of the confusion. This includes:
## Combine both types of requirements into a single section.
## Reorder the check boxes to move “Require this item” to the top. This provides more space below for the requirement/condition options to expand.
## Progressively release setting options based on user selection (i.e. hide drop-down menu unless conditional radio button is selected, don’t display points input box for requirement only items, etc.).
## Make the default behavior consistent with the current Lessons req/prereq options (i.e. required items in linear order selected).
# By default, list all gradebook items in the condition selection menu, as well as any required items on the page.
# Add a visual cue for all page items with prerequisites associated (both linear and conditional).



See mockups below:

Upon checking the box for “Don’t release item until all prerequisites are completed” the “All required items above this item in linear order” option is selected by default. This maintains the currently expected behavior.

!condition0.png|width=83.33333333333333%,alt="condition0.png"!



After selecting the “Conditional prerequisites” radio button, a dropdown menu appears to select from the currently available options. It includes the required items on the page, as well as all Gradebook items by default. 

!condition1.png|width=83.33333333333333%,alt="condition1.png"!



If the user selects a graded item such as Assignment 1, the selection appears with two additional input items: 1) a condition dropdown with selection options such as greater than, less than, equal to, etc. and 2) a manual input field to designate the point value desired.

!gb-item-selected.png|width=58.33333333333333%,alt="gb-item-selected.png"!

If the user selects a Lessons required/completion-only item, the selection appears with one dropdown menu containing selection options such as complete and incomplete.

!req-item-selected.png|width=58.33333333333333%,alt="req-item-selected.png"!

Once a requirement has been added, it will appear listed, along with an option to edit or delete it, and an option to specify ADD/OR for another condition if desired.

!add-another-condition.png|width=83.33333333333333%,alt="add-another-condition.png"!



Once a user selects from the AND/OR menu and clicks “Add another condition”, the item selection menu reappears and they can select another item from the list. 

!add-another-condition2.png|width=83.33333333333333%,alt="add-another-condition2.png"!



After adding the new item, both items (as well as the conjunction between them), appear listed with Edit and Delete icons. (Note: Deleting the conjunction should remove conditions below it. A confirmation popup such as “Are you sure you want to delete this conjunction and the conditions below it?” should be shown to the user prior to deletion.)

!add-another-condition3.png|width=83.33333333333333%,alt="add-another-condition3.png"!

summary: Resources: Edit folder permissions regression
description:
In Sakai 22 and earlier (at least with Sakai 21), folder permissions that are granted for a particular role could not be revoked. 

In other words, when editing folder permissions for a folder nested immediately beneath the root folder, an instructor could not revoke any of the permissions granted in the Permissions tab of Resources. For example, one could not revoke the ‘Read resources’ permission for students in a given folder. The corresponding checkbox in the ‘Edit folder permissions’ panel would be both checked and disabled. All checked permissions inherited from the tool level or inherited from other folders would be disabled. 

In Sakai 22 and earlier, an instructor could only grant more permissions for a given folder. I assume this was by design given problems with the status quo for Sakai 23 & 25, elaborated below.

In Sakai 23 and 25, any folder’s permissions can be set completely independently, regardless of the folder hierarchy in which a given folder is nested. Furthermore an inheritance of permissions no longer seems to occur. This is problematic because it seems as though an instructor can revoke the ‘Read resources’ permission for a student. However, any file stored in that folder can be accessed (read) by students.

This jira assumes that the primary bug is upstream from the more obvious problem described in the previous paragraph. In other words the primary bug pertains to behavior changes where

# Sakai 23 & 25 now allow instructors to revoke permissions granted in parent folders 
# Sakai 23 & 25 no longer inherits permissions from parent folders

summary: CC+Archive refactor attachments handling
description:
In the current approach to handling attachments in CC+Archive imports, the archive.xml file is processed before the rest of the files and the archives are temporarily loaded into /content/attachment under folders with guids.  Then as the other services processs their imported objects, it makes copies from the /content/attachment/gid folders into the /content/attachment/site folders.

This approach will be changed so use a “late copy” similar to how the basiclti.xml is handled.  When the attachment.xml file is processed early, it is simply parsed and placed into a map - then as the tools are doing their imports, it will consult the attachment map and copy the file data from the original zip file directly into ContentHostingService.

The result of this is that (a) data will only be copied once and (b) there will be no need to make temporary attachments and (c) clean up the temporary attachments at the end of the archive import process.

Attachment handling on import was fixed / improved in [https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-50946|https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-50946|smart-link] without refactoring the overall process - this Jira will build on that and change the overall process.

summary: Resources/Lessons: File access as a function of hiding & locking resources
description:
Detailed in the test plan, there are multiple unexpected cases where students are granted access to files stored in Resources where an instructor would expect students to instead receive http responses of 403 Forbidden. The test plan covers a range of hiding methods in Resources as well as two locking techniques for the Resources tool.

This jira encompasses unexpected behavior from Resources, Lessons, and the Portal. So as to not overly complicate the scope of this jira, it intentionally focuses only on the behavior of content links within Lessons. Similarly related options would otherwise include “Embed Content on the Page” and “Add Resources Folder”. At our institution, content links are by far the most common. Once the 403s are appropriately reflected in Lessons for content links, then I presume solutions for the other two could soon follow, scoped in separate jiras. Similar issues regarding embedded content are already reported in [https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-50896|https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-50896|smart-link].

Finally, other issues pertaining to an editing folder permissions regression in the Resources tool are reported in [https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-50984|https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-50984|smart-link]. Once those issues are resolved, they would mostly likely have bearing on content links and similar items in Lessons. I intentionally omit those concerns from this jira’s test plan because the issues described in [https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-50984|https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-50984|smart-link] are currently upstream and relatively distinct.

Note: This Jira mostly affects Sakai 23 and 25. However, parts of it also affect Sakai 22. The differences are identified in the test plan.

*Addendum:* Wary of the line separating jiras that are bugs from jiras that are feature requests or improvements, there are a few feature requests worth mentioning and perhaps pursuing when developing a fix for this jira:

* In Lessons: the introduction of italicized text to the right of content links when that content is ‘Hidden’ or ‘Locked’ (or ‘Hidden or Locked’ if its much more complicated to distinguish between those two states). This text is akin to the italicized ‘Deleted’ label that appears when a linked resource is no longer present.
* In Portal & Site Info: When the Resources tool is locked via Resources > Permission and removing student’s ‘Read resources’ permission, it may be of value for instructors to see a lock icon to the right of Resources in the tool menu. Furthermore, the lock icon and state for Resources should be represented in Site Info tool. This would at least be a step toward making Sakai’s behavior consistent between the two methods, as well as allow for either sets of controls (Resources or Site Info) to undo the locking.

None of the noted feature requests and behaviors are represented in the test plan. If the developer decides to incorporate any of them, the test plan should be revised accordingly.

summary: Announcements: Add Status column and filter
description:
I originally wrote this for the Admin MOTD tool, but I think it could be also useful for site announcements. 

For Announcements, I’d like to see a status column and four status options that can be filtered for, either by adding to the existing View menu (which shows Public / By Group / By Role ) or by adding a new status filter. 

Status options: 

* Hidden - User selected the “HIDE” option on availability. No dates set. 
* Active / Visible - User selected “Show” on availability or set dates that make the announcement currently visible
* Past / Expired - User set an end date that is now in the past.
* Future / Scheduled - User set a start date that is now in the future
* All - Default. All announcements shown, current behavior.

summary: Discussions: Date read-only option toggles Lock Topic, requires instructor to disable in order to update dates
description:
An option added to Discussions settings, under Availability is to allow users to view discussions after close date (read only).  This appears to work by setting to Lock Topic option when the close date passes. The problem is that when instructors need to update the dates for new semesters, they must know to uncheck the Lock Topic option. 

The specify dates option without the read-only option selected does not require an additional option to be changed in order to make it available again - just the dates.  

I feel like the Lock Topic option should be available only when the Availability is set to “Show immediately”, and the Specify Dates to Open/Close with read-only selected should not toggle this checkbox, but use a different method so instructors can update dates without needing to check an additional option.

Add New Feature to Generate Assessment Questions/Pools Using AI
description:
I would like to propose the addition of a new feature in Samigo to generate quiz questions using AI. This would be a useful time saver for faculty in helping them to create course content. It is also consistent with some of the other AI developments in the LMS market.

This new feature would be based on a few assumptions:

* It would be something you could enable/disable via property.
* It would include support to connect to a variety of LLM generative AI platforms (ChatGPT, Gemini, etc). Institutions could choose which one they want to use and configure this selection in sakai.properties. (This is similar to the content review service that allows users to plug in Turnitin or other plagiarism services. Institutions would need to have a separate license or subscription to an AI service.)
* It would provide a UI within the Tests & Quizzes tool which essentially helps the user to create a prompt, send that prompt to the LLM, and retrieve the questions in Mark-Up Text format which is then parsed by Samigo to take users directly to a screen where they can review and validate the questions. 
** Because the import of questions from the LLM is leveraging the Mark-Up Text format, it will be limited to the question types currently supported in Sakai’s Mark-Up Text for copying and pasting questions.

See mockups below:

When a user goes to the *Add* tab in Tests & Quizzes, a third option would appear in the list of radio buttons. (This option would only appear if the Sakai instance has the AI feature configured and enabled in properties.)

!ai-quiz-generation-select-option.png|width=100%,alt="ai-quiz-generation-select-option.png"!

Upon selecting the *Generate Questions Using AI* option, the user goes to the following screen where the UI provides a selection of input choices so that the user can construct the prompt. 

* The dropdown menu selections for Difficulty Level would be Easy, Moderate, Hard, and Mixed. 
* The dropdown menu selections for Grade Level would be Elementary, Middle School, High School, College/University, and Professional/Adult Education. Additionally, it might be nice for these options, or at least the default selected option, to be configurable in sakai.properties.

!ai-quiz-generation-UI-step1.png|width=100%,alt="ai-quiz-generation-UI-step1.png"!

When the user fills in the information on this screen and hits *Next*, the information is sent to the LLM, the markup text is retrieved, and the questions are parsed using the Mark-Up Text functionality in Samigo. All of this happens behind the scenes. The next thing the user sees is the screen below, which is the same as the current “Step 2” in the Mark-Up Text workflow, where the user has a chance to validate the questions, or hit *Back* to make changes before proceeding to create the assessment or question pool. 

!ai-quiz-generation-UI-step2.png|width=100%,alt="ai-quiz-generation-UI-step2.png"!

 Comments and suggestions on the proposal above are welcome!

summary: Cursor briefly appears then disappears in Announcement Title field when creating a new announcement

summary: Integrate CKEditor's AI Assistant into the Rich Text Editor in Sakai
description:
CKEditor 5 has an AI Assistant that can be added to a CKEditor installation. The AI Assistant integrates with the AI model of your choice (Open AI, Azure Open AI, or Amazon Bedrock). 

For more information about the features of the AI Assistant, see [https://ckeditor.com/ai-assistant/|https://ckeditor.com/ai-assistant/|smart-link] and for more information on installation and configuration, see [https://ckeditor.com/docs/ckeditor5/latest/features/ai-assistant/ai-assistant-overview.html|https://ckeditor.com/docs/ckeditor5/latest/features/ai-assistant/ai-assistant-overview.html|smart-link] (It would require an API key to be configured, so the integration would be something that gets configured and enabled/disabled in sakai.properties.)

If we integrated the AI Assistant into Sakai’s Rich Text Editor, it would provide the opportunity to embed AI features into Sakai tools anywhere the CKeditor is available. The AI Assistant is fully customizable, and can be configured to use ready-to-use prompts or create our own custom prompts for specific use cases. 

A few use cases that come to mind are:

For instructors:

* Help generating content, such as creating quiz questions, Lessons content (e.g. adding learning objectives, recommending supplementary materials, etc.), creating discussion prompts and assignment instructions within the editor as a draft so that the instructor can edit/modify from there.
* Help summarizing information, such as student discussion posts or frequently asked questions.
* Making content more accessible by generating alternative formats for content, such as audio descriptions.

For students:

* Instant, personalized feedback on assignments or practice activities.
* Translating text into the student’s preferred language.
* Creating study guides.

The items above are just some suggestions. Obviously, there would need to be more discussion among community members to determine which features are most desirable within a teaching and learning context and where we should focus our efforts. Privacy concerns would need to be addressed. And the primary goal is to ensure that AI plays a constructive role to enhance - but not replace - the student or instructor teaching/learning experience. 

I have created this Jira as a roadmap item. We can create individual issues for specific tasks or feature requests and link them to this item. 

Note: The AI Assistant integration in CKEditor is dependent upon completing the upgrade to CKEditor 5 in Sakai.

description: When using [https://www.imsglobal.org/spec/lti-ags/v2p0|https://www.imsglobal.org/spec/lti-ags/v2p0|smart-link] with Sakai, tools are only shown grade book columns that belong to them.  The simplest way for an LTI tool to own a grade book column is for the tool to create that grade book column with AGS.   There is another important use case recently identified when working with TJ from Microsoft.  When an LTI tool is launched from the Assignments tool, it should also be able to find the grade book column associated with the tool and match each tool launch with its column using the {{resourceLinkId}}value in the AGS return data.  This way there can be several assignments that launch to the same tool and the tool can figure out which assignment the launch came from and which column will get the grades returned to it.

summary: cc+ import: when importing the same file twice in the same course, there are many warnings in the server logs
Resources: Performance issues zipping large file sizes
description:
We experienced a Sakai 23 tomcat crash when a user attempted to zip a folder in Resources containing 1.8 Gb of content within a course site where the quota is set to 2 Gb. For this scenario in production with active load in production, led to jvm pausing for 50 seconds. This consequently triggered Apache Ignite to shutdown the node.

Our tomcat nodes have 20 Gb of RAM and a JVM footprint of: {{-Xms10g -Xmx10g -XX:NewSize=4g -XX:MaxNewSize=4g -Xss512k}}

When reproducing this scenario in a developer (non-production) environment, same memory footprint but minus the active load, I’ve observed that JVM pausing can be in excess of 20 seconds which could lead to a shutdown via Ignite. 

In the same developer environment, I’m finding that setting the Resources quota to Unlimited sometimes still does not yield a zip file for the 1.8 Gb test case. For instance, in one case we got a nested java.lang.OutOfMemoryError. 

I’ve attached a screencast (TestCaseWithoutMuchLoad.mp4) showing an attempt in the same developer environment, but the jvm pausing wasn’t as extreme, resulting in 1-2 seconds at most. (In the screencast I round incorrectly. That said I’ve seen over 20 seconds in prior attempts, not recorded.) For a system under a production load, I would expect the pausing to be longer per previous cited example of 50 seconds.

ADDENDUM: Considering the user’s events in SAKAI_EVENTS, I’ve recorded this newer screencast (MoreLikelyCaseExacerbatingJvmPause.mp4) which shows what likely happened during the node crash and how a jvm pause in excess of 30 seconds can result on a non-production system. Ignite didn’t take down the node in this case though. 

While I’m not opposed to tweaking server specs and/or JVM specs as mitigation steps, I’m wondering if there might be some Sakai design or coding guardrails to develop and implement that would more effectively mitigate risks surfaced by this case.

This might be a problem in Sakai 25 too. I just haven’t tested that case yet.

summary: LTI 1.3: Grade sync intermittently broken with McGraw Hill Connect (LTIA)
description:
Working with McGraw Hill tech support, I’ve been troubleshooting a case where grade synchronization breaks between McGraw Hill and our local instance of Sakai 23 for some students and some activities. The breakage seems to occur after an instructor deploys a McGraw Hill assignment to Sakai and then subsequently revises the assignment, such as to allow for a student extension.

What seems to be happening is that requests from McGraw Hill to Sakai trigger the calling of LineItemUtil.updateLineItem (via LTI13Servlet.handleLineItemsUpdate). This in turn calls: 

{{String external_id = constructExternalId(tool_id, null, lineItem);}}

This null value above for constructExternalId’s “content” argument is hard coded. (Content seems to be only defined for a subset of scenarios.) This null value forces the content ID within the “line item” or gradebook item’s external id to be set to 0. I presume it would be ideal if the original lti_content.id value be preserved if within the chain of calls the loading of a content object is not possible.

When McGraw Hill requests line items from Sakai, the resourceLinkId for the case above is “content:0”. I think the grade sync problem happens when multiple line items share the same resourceLinkId of “content:0”.

McGraw Hill is claiming that this is a bug, and I’m inclined to believe them, though not yet sure from a design approach how to resolve this except for supplanting the aforementioned hard-coded null with an attempt to look-up/derive the lti_content.id.
