summary: Assignments: add teacher if peer reviewers with no modifications should be randomized again when changing end date
description:
This request came from a teacher who explained the students sometimes work offline when reviewing the submissions of their peers. The issue came as he modified the end date of the assignment and the assignations were randomized again, with students complaining as they had to review a different submission.

We have researched the current peer review process and the key aspects are:

* Peer reviews randomization takes place when an assignment is entering the peer review window, but besides the regular “time passing” way, it also happens when modifying the assignment dates.
* The randomization / assignation process is as good as it gets mostly, trying to match the pending reviewers with the configured number of assignations.
* Peer reviews submitted or saved with added points or comments don’t enter the second randomization process, which is also fine.

We don’t think a big change to the process should be applied, but maybe it would be good to give more info and options to a teacher when modifying the end or peer dates.

A banner like “You are modifying the peer review dates and this will have an impact in the current empty reviews. Do you have to randomize those again or leave the assignation as it is?“ and then 2 buttons - depending on the teacher’s choice, work on skipping the randomization part.

summary: Surface Release Status in Assignments Window
description: Faculty and Teaching Assistants are often making decisions on how best to use their time grading assessments, so making data easily available can improve their workflow and efficiency. The Assignments window supports this by providing the In/New column in the Assignments overview page. This Jira proposes to add an additional set of data to the In/New column in favor of a In/New/Released column. Essentially not the addition of another column, but the surfacing of the underlying data revealing how many of the submissions and graded items have been released.  This would allow TA’s and Faculty a way to focus attention on just those items that need grading and release.  For example, some faculty assign TAs to assess low-end assessments, but then review and release them themselves (faculty). However, it is sometimes difficult, given multiple sections to recall where a faculty member would need to focus their review attention. Adding this data (of those graded submissions that have been released) would help instructors to focus their attention w/o having to click into each assignment only to release items, which may already be released (and therefore do not need to be reviewed).

summary: Lessons/Gradebook: Lesson Question gradebook item can remain associated to soft-deleted lesson page
description:
We had an instructor run into issues setting up a site using Site Import, Lesson Questions and Gradebook. The instructor imported from a past site that had Lesson questions configured for grading. During the course of building the site the instructor errantly deleted one of the Lesson pages. After realizing the mistake they imported just the Lessons from the source site. After students answered the questions the instructor found that while the answers/score were available in the question grading pane they did not propagate to the gradebook.

Investigating the Sakai database lesson_builder_pages and lesson_builder_items and the index of pages I determined that the gradebook items remained associated with the original lesson page (now soft-deleted and seen in the index of pages).

The workaround I had the instructor do was to permanently delete the soft-deleted lesson page. This resulted in the gradebook items now longer appearing in the gradebook. I then had the instructor visit each lesson question via its Edit option and simple click Update date. That reestablished a gradebook item to lesson question relationship. Gradebook items now existed and the lesson question scores propagated to the gradebook.

When the lessons were re-imported from the source site I believe the lesson question to gradebook item relationship should have been established instead of the gradebook items remaining associated with the soft-deleted lessons.

summary: Sitestats: Event collection duplicates event processing
description:
Bug introduced in [[SAK-31879] Sitestats aggregator fails if first 1000 events selected dont have a session - Jira|https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-31879].

Currently, when processing the SiteStats Event Aggregator job, {{sqlBlockSize}} events are collected starting from a specific {{eventId}}. The next batch then collects another {{sqlBlockSize}} events starting from the previous {{eventId + sqlBlockSize}}.

The issue is that the SQL query returns exactly {{sqlBlockSize}} rows, excluding events from invalid sessions. As a result, if {{sqlBlockSize}} is 1000 and the first {{eventId}} is 5000, and the query encounters 100 invalid sessions, it will return events from 5000 to 6100. However, the next batch starts collecting from 6000 (5000 + 1000), causing 100 events to be processed twice.

summary: Upgrade Hibernate from 5.6.15 to 6.x
description:
We need to upgrade from Hibernate 5.6.15 to Hibernate 6.x to maintain framework currency, improve performance, and leverage new features. This is a significant architectural change that will
  require careful planning and execution.

  Background

  Our codebase currently uses Hibernate 5.6.15 with Java 17. Hibernate 6 introduces breaking changes to the API and behavior that will require modifications throughout the codebase.

  Tasks

* Research Hibernate 6.x migration guides and identify breaking changes
* Create POC branch to test basic configuration changes
* Update dependencies in master pom.xml
* Migrate from JPA 2.2 to Jakarta Persistence 3.0
* Update Ignite integration (currently using ignite-hibernate_5.3 version 2.16.0)
* Refactor entity mappings and HBM files where needed
* Revise Hibernate query language usage (HQL)
* Test with all supported databases (MySQL, Oracle)
* Update any Spring Data JPA configurations (current version 2.5.12)
* Review and update caching configuration
* Ensure OpenSearch integration continues to work
* Performance testing comparing 5.6 vs 6.x

  Impacted Areas

* All modules using Hibernate (significant portion of the codebase)
* Spring integrations (5.3.39)
* Cache configuration with Ignite (2.16.0)
* Entity mappings and HBM files
* Query APIs
* DAO implementations

  Acceptance Criteria

* All existing functionality works with Hibernate 6.x
* All tests pass
* No performance regression
* Documentation updated to reflect changes

  References

* [https://docs.jboss.org/hibernate/orm/6.0/migration-guide/migration-guide.html|https://docs.jboss.org/hibernate/orm/6.0/migration-guide/migration-guide.html]
* [https://jakarta.ee/specifications/persistence/3.0/|https://jakarta.ee/specifications/persistence/3.0/|smart-link]

summary: Upate Apache HttpComponents Core 5.3.4 GA
description:
{noformat}Release 5.3.4
------------------

This maintenance release fixes several corner-case defects in the asynchronous HTTP/1.1 protocol
handler as well as several other minor defects.


Change Log
-------------------

* HTTPCORE-778: URIBuilder to not encode sub-delimiters in URI fragment component for consistency
  with query component encoding
  Contributed by Oleg Kalnichevski <olegk at apache.org>

* Bug fix: Fixed a race condition in the async message stream handlers that can occur when
  a message with no content body is being submitted asynchronously.
  Contributed by Oleg Kalnichevski <olegk at apache.org>

* Bug fix: Async message stream handlers to avoid firing data produce events from multiple
  threads.
  Contributed by Oleg Kalnichevski <olegk at apache.org>

* HTTPCORE-777: I/O reactor to cancel out incomplete connect requests when shutting down.
  Contributed by Oleg Kalnichevski <olegk at apache.org>

* Resource release corrections and code improvements in the base implementations of client
  and server async exchange handlers.
  Contributed by Oleg Kalnichevski <olegk at apache.org>

* Bug fix: Corrected the state management in the async HTTP/1.1 protocol handler when
  committing requests asynchronously.
  Contributed by Oleg Kalnichevski <olegk at apache.org>

* Bug-fix: Corrected message stream termination by the async HTTP/1.1 protocol handler
  when the connection has been half-closed by the opposite endpoint.
  Contributed by Oleg Kalnichevski <olegk at apache.org>

* Bug fix: Shared output buffer #writeCompleted fails to signal the end of the stream correctly
  when there is no buffered data.
  Contributed by Oleg Kalnichevski <olegk at apache.org>

* Bug fix: Corrected handling of invalid HTTP protocol version by HTTP/1.1 async client
  protocol handler.
  Contributed by Oleg Kalnichevski <olegk at apache.org>

* Bug fix: Corrected state tracking of pipelined message exchanges by HTTP/1.1 async client
  protocol handler.
  Contributed by Oleg Kalnichevski <olegk at apache.org>

* HTTP/1.1 server protocol handler to use exception callback to report exceptions that cannot
  be handled by individual exchange handlers.
  Contributed by Oleg Kalnichevski <olegk at apache.org>

* Bug fix: ServerHttp1StreamHandler throws an NPE when attempting to handle a corrupt/invalid
  incoming request message head.
  Contributed by Oleg Kalnichevski <olegk at apache.org>
{noformat}

If these 2 conditions are met:

# Student has an exception for an assessment where late submissions are allowed indefinitely
# The student does not begin the assessment until after the exception due date
# The assessment is either timed or the exception has a due date that is earlier than the the assessment date
then they will not be able to start the assessment. By virtue of the indefinite late submissions they should be allowed to take the assessment.
Two variations have been observed:
# Un-Timed assessment:
Where the exception due date is earlier than assessment due date, the student is faced with a ‘Late Submission not allowed’ message.
# Timed assessment:
The original filed jira. Exception does not have its own due date, but does have a different timed allotment. Student faces  “Work is being saved’ message which persists for several minutes before auto-submission occurs. If the student does not begin the assessment until after the due date, they will not be able to start the assessment.

In both cases the correct behavior should be that the assessment is available for the student to start.
The two cases are distinct in that one utilizes a timer such that the bug triggers the auto-submit and the other without the timer blocks the start of the assessment with the ‘Late Submission not allowed’ message.





*===============================================*

*Original Jira Title:* ‘Tests & Quizzes: Timed test Exception started after due date displays “Work is being saved” message’

*Original Jira Description:* “If a student has an exception for a timed assessment where late exceptions are allowed and the student does not begin the assessment until after the due date, they will not be able to start the assessment.

Instead a Message box will appear stating “Work is being saved’. While the message is displayed no work on the assessment can be done and eventually it is auto-submitted. The message persists for many minutes leading the student to think they are locked out and cannot proceed, which is essentially the case.

In my testing on nightly the message persisted for roughly 15 to 20 minutes past the due date-time after which the assessment auto-submitted.

The correct behavior should be that the assessment is available for the student to start and when they do, the timer with the amount of time specified in the exception is displayed and started.”

*Original Test Plan:*

# Create new site with Tests & Quizzes tool
# Create test student account
# In site 
## Add test student to the site
## Create an assessment
### Add a few T/F questions
### Set a Start date shortly from now so you don’t have to wait too long to test, set Due date that is 5 minutes after the start date, and allow for late submission with no deadline
### Set assessment to be timed, allow for 1 minute
### Add an exception for the student keeping the same start and due dates, same late submission with no deadline, but set the timer for 2 minutes
# Wait until the due date-time has past
# Have student attempt to start the assessment
## {color:#36b37e}*Expected:*{color} The assessment can be started and the time appears and begins the 2 minute countdown
## {color:#ff5630}*Observed:*{color} A message model with “Work is being saved.” appears and the student cannot answer the first question - the modal backdrop is greyed and inaccessible. Several minutes after the time when the exception timer would have expired, the assessment auto submits

summary: Gradebook modals should trap tab key
description:
Currently, when a modal dialog (e.g., Add Gradebook Item) is opened, keyboard focus is not restricted to the elements within the modal. Users navigating via the keyboard (using {{Tab}} and {{Shift+Tab}}) can inadvertently move focus to interactive elements in the underlying page _behind_ the modal overlay.

*Problem:*

This behavior causes significant issues:

# *Accessibility Barrier (WCAG Failure):* This violates WCAG 2.1 Success Criterion 2.4.3 (Focus Order). When a modal dialog is displayed, the keyboard focus order must be logical and confined to the modal's content. Allowing focus to escape disrupts the intended interaction flow, making it difficult or impossible for keyboard-only users and screen reader users to interact effectively with the modal. They can become "lost" on the page behind the overlay.
# *Poor Usability:* Users expect modals to temporarily restrict interaction to the modal's context. Tabbing out of the modal to background elements is confusing and can lead to unintended actions on the main page while the modal is still active.
# *Inconsistent User Experience:* Standard web accessibility patterns dictate that modals should trap focus. Failing to do so creates an inconsistent and non-standard interaction.

*Solution:*

Implemented JavaScript logic within the {{GbModalWindow}} component (or relevant modal component) to:

* Identify all focusable elements within the active modal dialog (including header elements like the close button and content elements).
* Attach an event listener that intercepts {{Tab}} and {{Shift+Tab}} key presses.
* When tabbing from the last focusable element, loop focus back to the first.
* When shift-tabbing from the first focusable element, loop focus back to the last.
* Ensure this trapping behavior is only active when the modal is open and is removed when the modal is closed.

*Importance:*

Implementing focus trapping is crucial for:

* *Meeting Accessibility Requirements:* Ensuring compliance with WCAG guidelines and providing an equitable experience for users with disabilities who rely on keyboard navigation.
* *Improving Usability:* Creating a predictable and constrained interaction flow that prevents user confusion and errors.
* *Standardization:* Aligning our modal behavior with established web standards and user expectations.

summary: Regression: Behaviour on slow LTI tools
description:
In Sakai 22, when you connected to an LTI tool that was taking a long time to respond, a JavaScript message appeared saying: "Unable to send launch to remote URL...". Despite this message, the LTI POST to load the tool was not abort, allowing it to load even though it took longer than the specified time to display the warning.

Now in Sakai 25, the message is no longer displayed, and after 2 seconds, the POST is abruptly canceled, only to have to resend the same POST. This causes an error in LTI signature validation due to the reuse of the LTI signature (invalid nonce), rendering the process unable to connect to the LTI tool.

summary: Dashboard: Grade widget sort concern
description:
The Grades widget on Dashboard has multiple sort orders: 

* New: Lowest First
* New: Highest First
* Average: Lowest first
* Average: Highest first
* Assignment: A-Z
* Assignment: Z-A
* Course: A - Z
* Course: Z - A

The problem is that the New and Average sorts are really aimed at the instructors - sort by number of ungraded, sort by average course score. 

For students, the New sort options do nothing, leaving the list in the previous order. If the student wants to sort by their score, they must select Average. This doesn’t seem intuitive, as students don’t see their score as an Average at all. Students would expect the New option to sort by most recently graded. 

# Can the New sort option be hidden for users who have no grading powers the relevant site(s)? If not, does the option to sort by number of ungraded provide enough value to the instructor to be worth confusing students?
# Can we rename Average to Score, which would match that column heading? That should be clear to both students and instructors.

summary: Resources: Over quota errors during compression
description:
In cases where a user is attempting to compress content in Resources where the addition of the resulting zip file would exceed the quota, the user is currently presented with the following generic error message:

_An error has occurred while compressing to zip archive_

Meanwhile, logged to catalina.out an error message with an OverQuotaException stack trace is logged, unknown to the user. 

The generic message may incline the user to waste time by trying again. Instead, a more helpful message to present to the user when an OverQuotaException occurs would be the message defined by the “overquota” property in content.properties:

_Adding this resource would place this account over quota. To add this resource, some resources may need to be deleted._

FYI: This particular case was partly the impetus in discovering the bug described in [https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-51067|https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-51067|smart-link].

summary: Gradebook: Rubrics with percentage grade entry
description:
If the gradebook is set for percentage grade entry, any rubrics are treated as percentages - an item with the rubric has a max score X%, where X is the maximum point value of the rubric. I noticed it with rubric-graded discussions, it does the same thing if the rubric is graded from there. 

Assignments with rubrics come to Gradebook as expected - A 10 point assignment and rubric, scored at maximum is 100% in the gradebook. However, a gradebook item with a 10 point relative weight, scored with that same rubric has a maximum score of 10%

summary: Add feature for Sakai to read and import publisher testbanks exported in Canvas format
description:
Publishers often provide testbanks that are exported in several formats, but not ones that can be imported directly into Sakai. Typically, there is a Canvas export, and often a BrightSpace or Blackboard export. However, even if there is a QTI export available, it does not always import into Sakai, depending on which version of QTI is used. Testbank exports of any sort that are not specifically made for Sakai are usually problematic. For example, you might end up with the questions, but they are all the wrong question type. Or maybe you get the questions and question types, but they have incorrect or missing answers. Or, you might get the questions, but they are all missing the images associated with the question or answer text. 

Often, instructional support staff end up doing lots of workaround imports and exports into other tools (such as into Respondus or even another LMS and then back out again) just to get a format that will work for Sakai. Since the process is largely trial and error, it isn’t something that can be easily explained to faculty. As a result, many faculty get frustrated with their import options, assuming that the testbanks they want are simply not available for Sakai.

If Sakai had the ability to correctly read and import testbanks that have been exported in Canvas format, that would solve nearly all of the use cases, since Canvas format is almost always one of the testbank export options. 

See mockup of proposed new option in the *Tests & Quizzes > Add > Import From File* screen:

summary: UserMessagingService thread safety improvements
description:
Improvements have been made to the UserMessagingServiceImpl class to enhance code quality, maintainability, performance, and error handling. These changes improve the overall robustness of the messaging system.

h2. Key Improvements

h3. Code Organization and Structure

* Made constants in EmailSender inner class static and final for better memory management and code clarity
* Extracted repeated logic into dedicated methods to follow DRY principles
* Improved method organization for better readability and maintainability

h3. Error Handling and Robustness

* Added comprehensive null checks to prevent NullPointerExceptions
* Implemented proper try-catch blocks with specific exception handling
* Improved logging with more descriptive error messages and appropriate log levels
* Added validation for user inputs and service dependencies

h3. Documentation

* Added comprehensive JavaDoc comments to all methods in the EmailSender class
* Improved inline comments to explain complex logic and implementation details
* Standardized comment format for better readability

h3. Email Formatting and Content

* Improved HTML email structure with proper charset specification
* Enhanced email formatting for better readability on various email clients
* Extracted preferences link logic to a separate method for better maintainability
* Simplified string building with more direct approaches in several methods

h3. Performance Optimizations

* Reduced unnecessary string concatenations
* Improved resource management with proper try-with-resources blocks
* Enhanced thread pool management with configurable size and proper shutdown

h2. Benefits

* *Increased Reliability*: Better error handling reduces the likelihood of runtime failures
* *Improved Maintainability*: Better documentation and code organization makes future changes easier
* *Enhanced User Experience*: Better formatted emails improve readability for end users
* *Better Performance*: Optimized code reduces resource usage and improves response times

summary: Date Manager: Order Resources section by folder structure
description:
When updating dates in Date Manager, each section lists the various items alphabetically. I suggest we change this for the Resources section and instead list the items within the folder structure of Resources.

An example - There are three subfolders in Resources. All three have a “Readme.txt” file in them. In Date Manager, it lists all three Readme.txt files, with no way to identify which one it is. 

A basic solution may be to include the file path with the name: Folder1\Readme.txt, Folder2\Readme.txt, and Folder3\Readme.txt. This would at least ensure that the content was grouped by folder/subfolder.

I think it would be even more useful to have any folders as expandable/collapsable within the Resources section of Date Manager, like how the folders are within Resources. If I want to set a date restriction on Folder2\Readme.txt, I would click the expand button or folder for Folder2, then find Readme.txt below it and enter the date. I would assume that having a date restriction on the folder would restrict all files within that folder, so having the folders visible first seems like it would make it simpler for instructors who set the date restrictions for folders.

summary: LTI / Tsugi refactor and clean up the numeric conversion routines and enhance the Tsugi unit tests
description:
Because LTI uses FooRM and deals with Map<String, Object> data structures that come straight from the JDBC connector for each database, Sakai’s LTI code needs to cope with a wide range of possible types when it expects an Integer value.   There have been routines in FooRM and LTI13Util like getLong() that take an object as the first parameter and return a Long by casting or converting (with error checking) so that a line like this can be done:

{noformat}Long toolKey = getLongKey(content.get(LTIService.LTI_TOOL_ID));{noformat}

This is of particular importance to maintain compatibility between MySQL, Oracle, and HSQL.

Over the years, these object → number conversions have lived in various packages within LTI.  Different areas of LTI use different implementations of these methods depending on when and where they were written.

This change will move the actual implementations of these methods into org.tsugi.lti.LTIUtil and change the rest of the code to use these implementations.  The LTIUtil code is the lowest level dependency in all of the LTI code in Sakai.

Unit tests will be updated / built.

Ultimately this is just a refactor / cleanup of existing code and nothing should change.

summary: LTI Remove the XMLMap Library from LTI
description:
Some of the earliest Sakai LTI 1.1 code uses a XML parsing library invented by [user] called XMLMap - it seemed like a good idea at the time.  It would parse an XML document and return it as a Java Map with expanded paths.  It allowed the quick development of code to parse small XML documents like the POX requests.  What was nice is that XMLMap was tolerant of flawed XML and allowed for the development of code that only looked for the elements it was expecting and did not choke on spurious elements.

For LTI 1.3 we figured out how to build a nice, clean, well documented set of hierarchical objects that were serialized and de-serialized using {{com.fasterxml.jackson}}- and this approach solved the de serialize and “accept imperfect XML” as long as the essential elements were present in the XML.  With this approach, once the XML is de-serialized all of the elements are available as properties in objects - which makes for more testable and more reliable code.  You can find an example of some of those Jackson based objects in:

{{./tsugi-util/src/java/org/tsugi/nrps/objects}}

The goal of this Jira is 

find all the places in the LTI code base that parse incoming XML or produce outgoing XML using XML Map

define new objects in {{./tsugi-util/src/java/org/tsugi/}} for the XML and build good unit tests for those objects

then switch all the XML de-serialization and serialization using XMLMap to these new Jackson based objects - adding unit testing where appropriate

remove XMLMap

Thorougly test all the LTI 1.1 code paths that have been changed

summary: LTI Remove Foorm and replace with JPA
description:
This is a place holder for the work to remove the Foorm library from Sakai completely.  More detail will be provided in time.  I think a phased approach is the right approach - here are my draft milestones:

# Build full coverage unit tests for the current Foorm libary and how it is used in Sakai’s LTI.
# Build JPA POJOs for each of the core LTI objects, Tool, Content, Deploy, Membership.
# If the POJOs can be connected to the current data model without changing the underlying model do so and add parallel unit tests that cover the same scope as the unit tests for Foorm.  If this cannot be done, make a simple mapping layer from the Map<String, Object> data to the POJOs and then write unit tests for the “faked POJOs”
# Then go through everything except the LTIAdmin tool and have the code use the POJO forms of the service calls.   Run this through a full regression test.
# Go through the LTIAdminTool and VM files and convert to (a) POJO form of service calls and (b) switch from Foorm generated HTML accessing the Map<String, Object> to explicit HTML  that finds its data in the POJOs.  Full regression test would be nice.
# At this point there should be no remaining use of Foorm.
# If we did not connect the POJOs to the model, we need to do that now.  
# Delete Foorm and run full regression test.

summary: Grader: feedback and private note inconsistencies
description:
When adding feedback or a private note in the Grader, the Done and Save buttons have very inconsistent behaviors.

* With both feedback and private note expanded, entering text in both, then clicking Done for the private note (but not on the feedback): *both feedback and private note are saved*
* With both feedback and private note expanded, entering text in both, then clicking Save at the bottom of the grader: *feedback is automatically saved but the private note is not*
** Note: if you now go to the next student, the private note is automatically expanded
* With both feedback and private note expanded, entering text in both, then clicking Done for the feedback comment (but not for the private note): *both feedback and private note text are removed and the private note remains expanded* {color:#ff5630}*in some cases*{color} *- I saw this when moving from student to student in grading*

Suggestions for improvements (taking into account issues reported in [https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-50229|https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-50229|smart-link] ):

* Replace the Done buttons with Clear buttons that will clear the text in feedback or private note
* Allow the Save button to save any text entered into feedback or private note
* Instead of having buttons for Add Feedback Comment, Add Attachment and Add Private Note, make these expandable divs
* If the feedback and private note had a clear button, a Remove link would not be needed

However, looking at the clear() method in SakaiRubricGrading.js, it seems like there might be a typo: it sets {{this.evaluation = {};}} instead of {{this._evaluation = {};}}. Additionally, it doesn't reset the _totalPoints.
Let's correct the clear method in SakaiRubricGrading.js to properly reset this._evaluation and this._totalPoints. This should ensure that when dispatchRatingChanged is called after clearing, it correctly identifies that there's no existing evaluation ID and performs a POST to create a new one.

summary: Test & Quiz Tool Usability Without Internet – Performance Issues & Alternatives?
description:
We are planning to conduct exams using the *Tests & Quizzes tool* in Sakai but are concerned about students engaging in malpractice if internet access is allowed. To address this, we’re considering *disabling internet access for students* during exams.

However, when internet is disabled on student machines, *Sakai becomes extremely slow or unresponsive*.

* Is it possible to run the *Tests & Quizzes tool* effectively *without active internet*?
* Are there any known solutions or *alternative tools* that support *offline exam delivery* or are more stable in restricted network environments?

Any suggestions or workarounds would be helpful.

summary: erformance Impact of "Random Draw from Question Pool" – Any Fixes in Recent Releases?
description:
We are using the *"Random draw from question pool"* feature in the *Tests & Quizzes* tool and would like to understand its impact on performance.

Specifically:

* Does using *random draw* (e.g., drawing 100 questions per student) cause *performance issues*, especially during large-scale assessments?
* If there were known issues in the past, have *any performance improvements or fixes* been made in *recent Sakai releases*?
* Is it *recommended or safe* to use random draw for *100 questions* in a high-stakes test scenario?

Any insights or documentation references would be greatly appreciated.

summary: Test & Quiz Tool Usability Without Internet – Performance Issues & Alternatives?
Impact of "Random Draw from Question Pool" – Any Fixes in Recent Releases?
description:
We are using the *"Random draw from question pool"* feature in the *Tests & Quizzes* tool where one question-pool has 2000 questions and 4 subpools. (200 questions in each subpool)

We are having 4 parts ( Each parts setting as Random draw from subpool )

Each part has 25 questions each ( total 100 questions)

Our users/students are complaining slowness of the pages when taking up the exams.

* Does using *random draw* (e.g., drawing 100 questions per student) cause *performance issues*, especially during large-scale assessments like 1000 students taking the exams simultaneously ?
* If there were known issues in the past, have *any performance improvements or fixes* been made in *recent Sakai releases*?

Any insights or documentation references would be greatly appreciated.

summary: In Conversations, move Statistics out from under Settings to have its own button
description:
In the Conversations tool, the Statistics for user posts are currently listed underneath the Settings link. However, Statistics don’t really make sense there, since they are not a type of Setting. Also, the feature would be more discoverable if we surfaced it in the interface with its own button. Also, breaking it out to its own section would eliminate the need for the bulleted list of other Settings subitems to the left of the Statistics display.

We discussed this on the T&L/UX call and there was consensus that it makes more sense to have Statistics separated out in this way. We also agreed that using consistent button styling with the rest of Sakai would be preferable to the look of the Settings and Create New Topic links as they currently appear. 

Please see the mockup below of the proposed changes.

See new button appearance in the top right:

!conversations-statistics-button.png|width=100%,alt="conversations-statistics-button.png"!

summary: Add "Post Replies" to Conversations Statistics
description:
Currently, the Statistics in Conversations tracks the number of user Posts, but does not differentiate between an original post to the topic, and a reply to another user’s post within the topic. 

A very common type of discussion assignment in courses is to have a Discussion Question that is posed to the class, and students are instructed to post one original reply to the topic, and then reply to one or more other student posts within the topic. This is meant to generate some student-to-student interaction and encourage further discussion within a thread. Often, faculty will assign points to each type of post differently. For example, they might allocate 3 points for an original post, and 2 points for the follow-up reply, for a total of 5 points for that discussion topic.

To facilitate the grading of Conversation posts based on type of post, it would be helpful to have an additional column in the Statistics for “Posts Replied” to differentiate between the user’s original post to the topic, and any replies (or comments) to another user’s post within the topic.

See mockup below:

!conversations-statistics-posts-replied.png|width=100%,alt="conversations-statistics-posts-replied.png"!

Additionally, it would be helpful to be able to filter the Statistics view by topic. I’ve created [https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-51476|https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-51476|smart-link] for that.

summary: Add option to filter by topic in Conversations Statistics
description:
Currently, the Statistics in Conversations tracks activity for all topics, but does not have a way to view the Statistics for a specific topic only.

It would be helpful to have a filter where the instructor can select from the list of topics present in the site, so that they can view stats for one topic at a time if desired.

See mockup below:

!conversations-statistics-filter-by-topic.png|width=100%,alt="conversations-statistics-filter-by-topic.png"!

summary: Add Student View for Conversations Statistics
description:
In reviewing the location and display options in Conversations Statistics, it occurred to me that it would be nice to have a student view of Statistics where students can see their own activity only. This would be consistent with Discussions, which gives students a user-specific view of their own activity.

If we move Conversations Statistics out from under Settings as proposed in [https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-51474|https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-51474|smart-link] it would make it easier for students to access their own stats, since we could allow the Statistics button to display for students without showing the Settings button.

summary: Initial Failure fails to Remove Invalid Usernames
description:
When the instructor logs in and clicks the 'Add Participants' button, invalid usernames for both official and unofficial participants are not automatically removed. If the instructor clicks 'Cancel' and then reopens the Add Participants page, the issue no longer occurs.

Andrea comments:

At one time, if an invalid username was added to Add Official Users, the message would display that it was an invalid username and it would automatically be removed from the list.

This would allow instructors to move ahead with adding other students without having to remove the invalid usernames. If there are only a few, it’s not a big deal to remove one from the list, but if you have a few hundred users you are adding to a site, it is a lot of work to then have to find any invalid usernames and remove them first. 

For the unofficial usernames….since this requires email addresses to be added, if the username is not in the form of an email address, an error message displays, but the username is not removed from the list.

*As Yicheng pointed out in his video, once the initial failure happened, the invalid names were not cleared, but after cancelling, or leaving Add Participants, the next try does remove the invalid names.*

The removal of invalid names should happen every time.

summary: Update Apache HttpComponents Client 5.5 GA
description:
The Apache HttpComponents project is pleased to announce 5.5 release of
HttpComponents HttpClient.

This is the first GA release in the 5.5 release series. This release
finalizes the 5.5 APIs and adds several experimental features and
improvements, such as request multiplexing over a shared HTTP/2
connection and the Classic API facade acting as a compatibility bridge
between classic I/O client services and the asynchronous message
transport used internally.

Notable changes and features included in the 5.5 series:

* Improved conformance to RFC 7616 (HTTP Digest Access Authentication).
* The connection pool implementation acts as a caching facade in front
of a standard managed connection pool and shares already leased
connections to multiplex message exchanges over active HTTP/2
connections. This is experimental.
* Extended Auth API and improved authentication protocol logic to
support mutual authentication.
* The Classic API facade now acts as a compatibility bridge between the
classic I/O client services (based on the standard InputStream /
OutputStream model) and the asynchronous message transport used
internally. This is experimental.
* HTTP/2 support for the Fluent Facade (via Classic API facade). This
is experimental.

summary: Resources: TA permissions & unexpected permission inheritance
description:
The following issue is partly obscured by the relatively minimal default permissions granted by TAs for the Recourses tool (content.*) on nightly: 

* content.read
* content.hidden

Our institution has instead granted TAs the following permissions by default:

* content.read
* content.upload
* content.edit.own
* content.edit.any
* content.delete.own
* content.delete.any

Given the context at our institution (which is simulated in the test plan) and for instructors who want to revoke several TA permissions that are otherwise asserted with that default, the results from revoking permissions are currently unexpected. For example, the test plan outlines a case where an instructor wants to revoke all TA permissions except for “Read resources” (content.read) in order to safeguard against TAs inadvertently deleting content uploaded by the instructor. In line with this the instructor intends to have a designated subfolder where the TA can upload content and edit and remove only what they upload. This case exhibits two related bugs:

* The revoked permissions do not take effect. The TA can upload content anywhere in Resources.
* Furthermore, the default permissions in the subfolder should solely match those the instructor has set for the site or the folder above it. Instead, permissions that the instructor had earlier revoked for the site are granted by default.

This bug is dependent on features from SAK-50984 and SAK-51375. When these commits are merged to 23.x, then this jira would also be relevant for 23.x. Reviewing/studying the behavior of 22.x, specifically how realms are formed vis-a-vis the admin Realms tool, may be instructive toward resolving these bugs in 26.x, 25.x and eventually 23.x.

summary: Resources: Revoking content.read does not deny access
description:
Allowing an instructor a means through the Resources permissions panels to revoke the ‘Read resources’ (content.read) permission sets the expectation that content in the site will not be accessible. Revoking content.read for a given role does not deny that role access. Refer to the test plan for an example.

Prior to the second commit for [https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-51375|https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-51375|smart-link], the content.read permission could not be revoked by the instructor, as the checkbox for this permission was disabled. (No default permissions could be revoked.) Since that commit, another set of bugs also became active: [https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-51556|https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-51556|smart-link].

In Sakai 22.x, the revocation of content.read causes the Resources tool to become invisible for the affected role. In other words, Resources does not display on the tool menu for that role.

As of this writing, Sakai 23, which does not have commits for SAK-51375, is also vulnerable to the core problem: revoking content.read for a given role does not deny that role access.

summary: Resources: Preserve folder permissions when copied via Import from Site
description:
When copying course content via Site Info > Import from Site, the folder permission settings in the source site-- unlike ‘Edit Details settings-- are not preserved after being copied to the target site.

*An example use case:* When an instructor who teaches a given course over successive academic terms, that instructor is always allotted a teaching assistant. That instructor also always has a folder (or set of folders) for which the teaching assistant should be granted permissions that differ from the site’s default. For example, the TA should always be allowed to upload, edit, and delete their own content for that particular folder, but no where else in Resources. Given the status quo, the instructor must reassert these permissions after copying content from one site to another instead of relying on the copying process to preserve those permissions.

*Related design considerations:* When designing this feature, the developer may want to bear in mind the following related aspects about permission sets (or realms) for folders. Counter to (new) user expectations, previously saved folder permissions (which let’s assume, differ from the default of the parent folder) are not preserved if the instructor does any of the following:

* Move a folder from one place to another in the folder hierarchy
* Delete the folder and then restore it (likely by having to restore everything that’s currently in the Trash, given that the Trash view does not currently allow for discrete folders to be restored without restoring everything).

Whether or not considerations of preserving folder permissions for those related cases can be deemed in scope or not is at the discretion of the developer. (As of this writing, the test plan does not include these related concerns.)

summary: Profile Tool: Remove "Lock this profile" button and  Preferences tab with "Use my gravatar" option
description:
The Profile tool in 25 was recently updated to remove a lot of the old and unused features. However, there are a couple of items that were left behind. T&L/UX reviewed the changes to the tool and we suggest the following additional changes:

# Remove “Lock this profile” button (or hide it)
There is a “Lock this profile” button on the user’s Profile page which doesn’t seem to serve any purpose, since the user can lock/unlock their own profile. If this was intended as a feature for admin users to lock non-admin profiles, it might be useful. However, the way it is now, it doesn’t seem to work. Admins can only get to this page if they impersonate a user, and this means that the user can still lock/unlock their own profile. If we can fix it so that only admins see the lock button, that would be great. However, it appears that this lock feature was added in 2009 and I don’t think it has ever worked since it seems to have been hidden since then. We believe it may have become unhidden when the other features were removed from Profile. 
# Remove the “Use my Gravatar” option on the Preferences tab
T&L/UX agreed that gravatars are outdated and seldom used anymore. It makes sense to remove this option. Given that this is the only thing left on the Preferences tab in Profile, we can also remove the entire Preferences tab from that tool. 

Ideally, it would be good to make these changes prior to the 25.0 release so that users upgrading to this version will not be confused with non-working or outdated items now that the rest of the Profile tool has been streamlined and updated.

See screenshots of the problematic options here: [https://docs.google.com/document/d/1WNNrjdL8cpTmameMcpMyHtclVlQb4KE84wiDrTukkDs/edit?tab=t.0|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1WNNrjdL8cpTmameMcpMyHtclVlQb4KE84wiDrTukkDs/edit?tab=t.0|smart-link]

summary: Update Apache Tika 3.2.2
description:
{noformat}Release 3.2.0 - 05/21/2025

  * Detect inline images in MSG files (TIKA_4391).

  * Improve extraction of metadata in MSG files (TIKA-4381).

  * Fix concurrency bug in TikaToXMP (TIKA-4393).

  * Fix potential GDAL deadlock (TIKA-4385).

  * Improve extraction of properties from msg files (TIKA-4381).

  * Include internal attachment path in tika-eval reports (TIKA-4374).

  * Upgrade jsoup to 1.20.1 with workaround for change in self-closing tag behavior (TIKA-4419).

  * Upgrade dependencies (TIKA-4379).

Release 3.1.0 - 01/28/25

   * Allow users to turn off the injection of some headers into the content stream of MSG
     files (TIKA-4345).

   * Add a wrapper for Google's magika detector (TIKA-4344).

   * Add support for MachO via Alexey Pelykh (TIKA-4309).

   * Add logic to inject spaces in XPS files based on font widths via Ruairidh Williamson (TIKA-4315).

   * Mime type "application/json" is now a sub class of "text/javascript" not "application/javascript" (TIKA-4336)

   * Remove tagsoup from the project entirely. Note that
     some of the tags produced by the SourceCodeParser are slightly different (TIKA-4338)

Release 3.0.0 - 10/15/2024

   * Fix regression in TextAndCSVParser (TIKA-4278).

Release 3.0.0-BETA2 - 07/09/2024

   BREAKING CHANGES

   * Updated PST parser to use standard Message metadata keys and improved
     handling of embedded files (TIKA-4248).

   * Convenience methods for XML readers were moved from ParseContext to
     XMLReaderUtils (TIKA-4259).

   Other Changes

   * Add GRPC server (TIKA-4181).

   * Improved configurability in tika-pipes (TIKA-4243).

   * Add optional PST parser based on libpst/readpst (TIKA-4250).
{noformat}

summary: Portal: Tutorial is shown again for all users after the version upgrade
description:
In [[SAK-49755] Fix Persistent Tutorial Display Issue: Ensure Tutorial Only Appears for the first time user - Jira|https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-49755], the property used to store whether a user had already viewed the tutorial was updated. As a result, the SAKAI_PREFERENCES table still retains the old property, and after upgrading, all users are required to view the tutorial again.

22:

{code:xml}    <properties>
        <property enc="BASE64" name="sakaiTutorialFlag" value="MQ==" />
    </properties>{code}

master:

{code:xml}    <properties>
        <property enc="BASE64" name="sakaiTutorialFlag" value="MQ==" />
    </properties>
    <prefs key="sakai:portal:tutorialFlag">
        <properties>
            <property enc="BASE64" name="tutorialFlag" value="MQ==" />
        </properties>
    </prefs>{code}

summary: Gradebook: Leave Create Another checked or replace + button
description:
In 23, there were three buttons at the bottom of the Add Gradebook Item modal - Create, +, and Cancel. + was create and add another. 

In 25, this was changed to Create and Cancel, with a checkbox to Create Another. The problem is that the checkbox doesn’t remain checked, so if a user is adding multiple gradebook items, it doesn’t save any clicks. I would like to see the + button return, or the Create Another checkbox remain checked until the user unchecks it or clicks Cancel. Flagging this for T&L discussion.

summary: Search improvements
description:
This is an umbrella Jira for several improvements to the Search tool in Sakai to improve usability of the tool. 

Currently, the Search tool is not widely used because many users don’t understand how to configure it for use  properly, they worry that it will degrade system performance, or they assume that it is broken if it doesn’t respond as expected. There have been a lot of changes to Search to make it much more efficient than earlier versions of the tool, but the user interface is still somewhat lacking. 

I will be creating several related Jiras and linking them to this issue.

summary: Turn Search on for all sites by default
description:
Currently, the default configuration for Search is to have it only available in sites where the tool has been added. This goes back to the early days of Sakai when Search was much more brittle. Limiting the indexing of content to sites that specifically enabled it was one way of limiting the amount of data to be indexed in order to avoid performance issues. 

However, in practice, this means that site owners must first add the Search tool to their sites, and then any new content in that site will be indexed upon upload and/or creation. However, if an instructor adds Search to a site with lots of content already in it, then the admin must rebuild the index in order to index any existing content in that site. The instructor does not have permission to rebuild the index, which can cause unexpected results when they search for existing content but return nothing in the search results. Since not all site owners are aware of this, they may not know to add Search to their sites, or they may assume that the tool is broken. 

Since the Search tool is now in the top global nav (beginning in 23.x), that implies to users that they can search for content across all sites. But, since not all sites have the tool enabled, users often do not get the search results they expect. Students in particular may become frustrated by this, since they can’t control whether or not their instructor has added Search to a particular course site. 

Also, with the addition of Search in Conversations - which uses the Sakai Search to power it - users can’t search for items in Conversations without first adding the Search tool and then indexing any existing Conversations content. (While other tools have their own tool-specific search, such as Assignments or Tests & Quizzes, those tool-specific searches do not rely on the global Sakai Search to function.)

Recent changes to the default configuration of Search make it unlikely to cause performance issues in most implementations. Particularly if it is enabled system-wide so that items are indexed as they are created. Changing the default setting to have Search on all the time for all sites, not just the ones who have selected it as a tool, will make the global nav Search behave in a much more predictable and expected way for most users.

summary: Queue Search items by size rather than number
description: Currently, the Search tool queues items for indexing and completes them in groups of 500 items at a time. However, since search has to digest each of these items in order to index them, very large items (such as large Powerpoint files, or lengthy PDF documents) may take more time to index than smaller ones. It might be more efficient to queue items by file size rather than number of files. This way, large items will take up a proportional amount of the queue for more predictable indexing.

summary: Add filters to Search fly-out panel
description:
Currently, the Search in the top global navigation searches all of a user’s sites (in sites where Search is enabled). However, it would be more useful if the user had an easy way to filter the search results by site or by tool. 

I propose that we add two drop-down menus to the top of the Search fly-out panel: one for the site, and another one for the tool. This is similar to the Calendar tool which currently allows you to filter by site. 

The site menu would allow users to select “All Pinned Sites” pr choose a specific site from their list of all sites. 

The tool menu would allow users to select a particular tool (from a list of all tools which participate in Search). 

See mockups of the Search fly-out with the new filter menus at the top.

!search-menus-open.png|width=382,height=666,alt="search-menus-open.png"!

description:
In the Administration Workspace admin version of the Search tool, there are several items that can be cleaned up to make the display more functional and clear. 

# None of the buttons in the tool look like buttons unless you mouse over them. If you aren’t hovering over them, they look like regular text on the page. They would be better styled as buttons which are visible as such all of them time. 
# The Refresh Site/Whole Index options are not really needed and can be removed.
# The Index Functions drop down menu contains “default” and “questions” as the two choice, but it isn’t clear what “questions” are as compared to “default” or why you would want to index one and not the other. Some explanatory text or better labeling would be helpful.
# The section at the bottom contains a number of statistics that were relevant in past versions of Search, but are no longer relevant, tracked, or updated. This section should be removed if it presents no usable information.

summary: Add additional search filter options to Search tool in sites
description:
The Search tool can often be a bit intimidating for users if they don’t know how to filter the results via their search queries. In order to make the tool more user-friendly, it would be nice to include several common filters at the top, to help users limit their search results without having to know a lot about constructing the appropriate search parameters.

It would be helpful to have filter menus for:

* Sites
* Tools
* Date Ranges
* Users (for example, the item owner or author)

Note: These filter menus would be available only within the Search tool in a site, not in the global search accessed via the top nav. The idea is that the global search in the top nav is more of a “quick search” and the Search tool within a site is the complete tool with additional options.

summary: Update UnboundID LDAP SDK for Java 7.0.3
description:
We have just released version 7.0.3 of the [+UnboundID LDAP SDK for Java+|https://github.com/[user]/ldapsdk]. It is available for download from [+GitHub+|https://github.com/[user]/ldapsdk/releases] and [+SourceForge+|https://sourceforge.net/projects/ldap-sdk/files/], and it is available in the [+Maven Central Repository+|https://central.sonatype.com/artifact/com.unboundid/unboundid-ldapsdk/7.0.3]. You can find the release notes for this release (and all previous versions) at [https://docs.ldap.com/ldap-sdk/docs/release-notes.html|https://docs.ldap.com/ldap-sdk/docs/release-notes.html|smart-link] , but here’s a summary of the changes:

* We fixed an issue in which the LDAP SDK did not properly handle certificates with a notBefore or notAfter timestamp that fell in the year 2049 if that timestamp was encoded with the antiquated UTCTime syntax (which only uses two digits to encode the year). It incorrectly used a year of 1949 instead of 2049.
* We updated the {{ldifmodify}} tool so that it will report an error if any of the {{sourceLDIF}}, {{changesLDIF}}, or {{targetLDIF}} arguments refer to the same file. Previously, the tool would run, but could yield incomplete results if an input file was also used as an output file.
* We updated the IP address argument value validator to improve performance and to catch additional types of malformed IPv4 addresses that were previously accepted due to leniency in Java’s {{InetAddress.getByName}} implementation.
* We simplified and improved the {{toLowerCase}}, {{toUpperCase}}, and {{getBytes}} methods in the {{StaticUtils}} class. The former implementations were more efficient than the versions provided in the Java String class in older Java versions when primarily dealing with ASCII strings, but this is no longer the case in newer versions of Java where strings are backed by byte arrays rather than character arrays.
* We updated client-side support for the Ping-proprietary transaction settings request control to make it possible to request that the server acquire a lock using a client-specified scope under a specified set of conditions. This allows more control in the event of lock conflicts in cases where the client is able to determine which operations are most likely to conflict with each other. For example, in a multi-tenant server, it may be useful to specify a scope that includes a tenant-specific identifier so that only operations associated with that tenant will be affected by the scoped lock.
* We also updated the transaction settings request control to make it possible to override the conditions under which the server may attempt to acquire a single-writer lock. This was previously only controlled through the server configuration.
* We improved error reporting in the dump-dns tool for use with the Ping Identity Directory Server.
* We updated client-side support for the Ping Identity Directory Server’s version monitor entry to handle attributes used to indicate whether the server is running in FIPS 140-2-compliant or FIPS 140-3-compliant mode.
* We updated the documentation to include the newest versions of the draft-bucksch-sasl-passkey, draft-bucksch-sasl-rememberme, draft-codere-ldapsyntax, draft-ietf-kitten-sasl-ht, draft-ietf-kitten-sasl-rememberme, and draft-schmaus-kitten-sasl-ht specifications.

summary: Grade field is not cleared when navigating to next/previous student in Assignments
description: In Assignments, if you enter a score into the Grade field without any other feedback entered, and then you navigate to the next or previous student without saving, the grade you entered for the original student stays in the Grade field when you navigate to the new student. While the score is not saved, it is confusing and could easily cause incorrect scores to be saved by mistake.

summary: Ability to import/export rubrics as csv
description:
Currently, users must manually create rubrics within the tool. It would be a big time-saver if users had the ability to import and export rubrics. Often, users have existing rubrics that they would like to use in Sakai, but there is no easy way to bring them in without a lot of manual work. Likewise, there is no way for users to export rubrics in an editable format (i.e. not pdf) which would allow them to be transferred to other systems, or saved and/or modified offline. 

I’d like to propose that we create a standard format for csv files which could be used to import and export existing rubrics into and out of Sakai.

summary: Add "save as default" option in Rubrics
description:
Some users do not like the default ratings in the Rubrics tool. For example, if they don’t want the “Inadequate” title used for the first rating in a default new rubric, they have to change “Inadequate” to “Needs Improvement” (or their preferred term) every single time they create a new rubric. 

It would be a nice enhancement if users had the ability to create a starting rubric with the criteria and ratings that they prefer to use, and then have an option to “Save as default” for that rubric, so that each new rubric in the site is patterned after their custom default, rather than the system default.

summary: In Lessons Questions, allow check boxes for multiple correct items
description:
In Lessons, when you add a Question to the page, it is possible to indicate that more than one answer is correct for multiple choice questions. 

However, when students view the Question on a page, they are presented with answers that have radio buttons, and students can only select one item from the list. 

If an instructor has indicated that there is more than one correct item for a Lessons Question, there should be check boxes instead, which would allow students to select more than one option from the list.

summary: Lessons Questions: Make customizing style easier
description:
In Lessons, the default style for Questions on a page is defined within the Lessons CSS. While it is possible to change the CSS in Lessons to override the default Questions appearance, it does require a bit more advanced work. Many times users find the default Question styling too large for the page, or they would like to change the color, size, or width of the item, but they aren’t proficient enough with CSS to know how to do this. 

It would be nice if instructors could more easily format the style of Question items, ideally without having to use CSS at all. A selection of color or size options, not unlike some of the color, style, or size choices for subpages or embedded items would be nice. Or, at a minimum, something like the “appearance” options for Checklist items where you can more easily specify a custom CSS class for the item.

	•	Cross-browser coverage: Chromium + Firefox + WebKit out-of-the-box.
	•	LTI/iframe reliability: Native multi-origin support, fewer flaky hacks.

	•	One PR, one CI run, one review path.
	•	No extra repo sync, submodule pain, or version pinning.

summary: Gradebook percentage grades showing blank in student grade summary after SAK-51562 optimization
description:
h2. Problem

When instructors configure a gradebook to use percentage grades instead of points, student grades appear blank (-) in the student grade summary page, instead of showing the actual percentage values.

h2. Root Cause

The recent optimization in commit ea21206b6b5 (SAK-51562) changed the percentage grade calculation logic in {{GradingServiceImpl.convertGradeRecordToGradeDefinition()}}.

*Before (working):*

{code:java}final Double percent = calculateEquivalentPercent(assignment.getPointsPossible(), gradeRecord.getPointsEarned());
if (percent != null) {
    gradeDef.setGrade(percent.toString());
}{code}

*After (broken):*

{code:java}final Double percentEarned = gradeRecord.getPercentEarned();
grade = percentEarned != null ? percentEarned.toString() : null;{code}

The issue is that {{getPercentEarned()}} doesn't return the expected percentage value for percentage gradebooks.

h2. Steps to Reproduce

# Create a gradebook with percentage grade entry type
# Add an assignment with points possible (e.g., 22 points)
# Grade a student with some points (e.g., 18 points)
# View the student grade summary as the student
# Notice the grade shows as "-" instead of "81.8%" (18/22 * 100)

h2. Expected Behavior

Percentage grades should display the calculated percentage (e.g., "81.8%") in the student grade summary.

h2. Actual Behavior

Percentage grades show as blank (-) in the student grade summary.

h2. Fix Applied

Restored the original percentage calculation logic in {{GradingServiceImpl.convertGradeRecordToGradeDefinition()}} to use {{calculateEquivalentPercent()}} instead of {{getPercentEarned()}}.

h2. Files Modified

* {{gradebookng/impl/src/main/java/org/sakaiproject/grading/impl/GradingServiceImpl.java}} (line 1895-1896)

summary: Portal recent sites limit property not enforced - users accumulate 50+ recent sites
description:
h2. Problem

The {{portal.max.recent.sites}} property is defined in {{default.sakai.properties}} but completely ignored by the code, causing users to accumulate 50+ recent sites instead of the intended limit (default 3).

h2. Root Cause

{{PortalServiceImpl.addRecentSite()}} method uses a hardcoded limit of 3 and never reads the {{portal.max.recent.sites}} configuration property.

*Files affected:*

* {{portal/portal-service-impl/impl/src/java/org/sakaiproject/portal/service/PortalServiceImpl.java:963}}
* {{config/configuration/bundles/src/bundle/org/sakaiproject/config/bundle/default.sakai.properties:68}}

h2. Impact

* Users with 50+ recent sites experience degraded portal navigation performance
* {{portal.max.recent.sites}} property has no effect regardless of value
* System administrators cannot control recent sites limit

h2. Solution

# *Fix PortalServiceImpl.java:963*: Read configuration property instead of hardcoded limit
# *Activate default.sakai.properties:68*: Uncomment the property
# *Enhanced cleanup*: Handle users with existing 50+ recent sites by cleaning up excess entries

h2. Testing

All existing tests pass with mocked {{ServerConfigurationService}} returning 3.

summary: Add an "open submission preview in new tab" link in the Assignments grading UI
description:
The grading UI in Assignments has been improved to allow for side by side view on desktop. However, the mobile view breakpoints are still a little awkward at certain sizes, particularly the “tablet” size in between phone and desktop sizes. For Word or PDF files, which are by far the most common format, the document preview area tends to get scrunched down to an unreadable size given the width limitations in between the course/tool nav on the left and the grader panel on the right. 

Since it is so difficult to anticipate what size and resolution users will have when grading, the T&L/UX group thought that the best thing to do is to add a link so that the instructor can choose to open the student submission preview in a new tab so they can view it at full screen width. This would be a read-only view (even for inline submissions) so there would not be added complications with entering grades in multiple tabs.

I’m attaching a couple of mockups of what the “open in new tab” link might look like. We could either spell it out as a text link (so people know what it is), or if folks think it is obvious enough without the text label, we could just have the icon next to each submission. A tooltip could spell out the “open submission preview in new tab” part.

option 1 - spell out as a text link

!open-submission-preview-new-tab1.png|width=91.66666666666666%,alt="open-submission-preview-new-tab1.png"!



option 2 - icon only, tooltip to convey purpose of link

!open-submission-preview-new-tab2.png|width=91.66666666666666%,alt="open-submission-preview-new-tab2.png"!

Personally, I like option 2 better. It is cleaner and less cluttered, and takes up a lot less space. It would also work for assignments with multiple submission items (i.e. inline text plus attachments).

Note: The new tab should include the assignment title and student’s name at the top.

summary: Gradebook: Export file with Example items has a bad example
description:
If you export a Gradebook with no GB items, the file includes four sample columns:

# Example Assignment With Points [100]
# Example Assignment With No Points
# * Example Assignment with Points And Comments [50]
# # This column will be ignored.

I think column 3 is supposed to be an example of how to include comments, but since the item name doesn’t match 1 or 2, it does nothing. This makes it a pretty poor example. Honestly, when I saw this column, I was trying to figure out if this was comments, points, or both.

The Example items in a blank gradebook export should be functional examples, so if a user exported the blank gradebook, looked at these examples, added some values to each cell, and imported it back in, it would process things correctly. Column 3 should be comments for either Example Assignment With Points or Example Assignment With No Points.

summary: Enhance push notifications for iOS Safari and Android browsers
description:
Enhanced push notification support for iOS Safari and Android browsers to improve cross-platform compatibility and user experience.

h2. Changes Made

h3. 1. Enhanced Documentation

* Added comprehensive push notification documentation to CLAUDE.md
* Documented platform-specific requirements (iOS Safari, Android Chrome/Firefox, Desktop)
* Included implementation architecture details and development guidelines

h3. 2. Enhanced Browser Detection

Updated sakai-push-utils.js with new functions:

* isIOSSafari() - Detects iOS Safari specifically
* isAndroid() - Detects Android devices
* getBrowserInfo() - Comprehensive browser/platform detection
* canRequestPushPermission() - Checks if push permissions can be requested
* getOptimalPermissionTiming() - Suggests best timing for permission requests
* getPWAInstallationMessage() - Provides user-friendly PWA installation instructions
* shouldShowPWAPrompt() - Determines if PWA prompt should be shown

h3. 3. Improved User Experience

* Platform-specific permission handling
* Better error messages and logging
* PWA requirement checks for iOS Safari
* Optimal timing recommendations for different platforms
* Created web app manifest (manifest.json) for PWA support
* Added manifest link to portal header template

h2. Platform-Specific Requirements

h3. iOS Safari (iOS 16.4+)

* Requires PWA installation (add to home screen) before push notifications work
* Uses standard Web Push Protocol (no APNs certificate needed)
* Existing backend code works without changes

h3. Android Chrome/Firefox

* Works immediately with existing VAPID-based implementation
* No additional backend changes needed
* Enhanced UX provides better timing for permission requests

h2. Technical Details

* Backend UserMessagingServiceImpl.java already handles both platforms correctly
* No changes needed to Java implementation
* Enhanced browser detection improves UX across all platforms
* Maintains compatibility with existing infrastructure

h2. Files Modified

* CLAUDE.md - Added push notification documentation
* webcomponents/tool/src/main/frontend/packages/sakai-push-utils/src/sakai-push-utils.js - Enhanced browser detection and UX
* portal/portal-render-engine-impl/pack/src/webapp/manifest.json - New PWA manifest
* portal/portal-render-engine-impl/impl/src/webapp/vm/morpheus/includeStandardHead.vm - Added manifest link

summary: Assignments Date Picker: Enable datetime pasting

By focusing solely on the current behavior of the sakai-date-picker, which is deployed in only a few places in Sakai (e.g., Assignments), this jira addresses only a subset of the concerns raised in [https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-50002|https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-50002|smart-link]. (E.g., Firefox does not seem to register any paste events with this input, nor does it currently support a time picker.)

The test plan evinces a modest UX improvement for paste events with the sakai-date-picker when using Chrome or Edge. (Safari may need to be tested.)

summary: Date Manager: CSV Export needs to work in the US
description:
See the comments in [https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-50733|https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-50733|smart-link] 

Currently, the delimiter is “;” (European style), which does not work correctly in the US. We need the csv to have a comma as the delimiter, (or a tab), in order to view the csv file correctly with columns instead of one long string per line.

Comment from *Matthew Jones:*

{quote}It looks like this line sets the default to be the semi-colon?

[https://github.com/sakaiproject/sakai/blame/dc22c44f93880c4c73aa79fced773aa4c876365b/site-manage/datemanager/tool/src/main/java/org/sakaiproject/datemanager/tool/MainController.java#L296|https://github.com/sakaiproject/sakai/blame/dc22c44f93880c4c73aa79fced773aa4c876365b/site-manage/datemanager/tool/src/main/java/org/sakaiproject/datemanager/tool/MainController.java#L296|smart-link]

I’d either make that a {{,}} or make it configurable either in the UI or property if {{;}} is a more common separator for some countries. TSV (Tab separated) and CSV (Comma separated) are the more popular US formats.

It might also be useful if this did use POI to process actual Excel files (like Polls) to avoid these issues but that would be a larger feature.{quote}

*Co-pilot suggestions:*

Uncaught TypeError: $.handleError is not a function



means that the {{jquery.form-2.43.js}} script is trying to call a jQuery function named {{handleError}}, but that function does not exist or has not been defined when it’s being called.

This happens at line 339 in that script when the {{cb}} function executes—possibly during an {{iframe.onload}} event.

*Possible Causes* Here’s why this could be happening:

* *Missing Function Definition*: The script expects {{$.handleError}} to exist—either defined by a plugin or elsewhere in your code—but it’s not available.
* *jQuery Version Mismatch*: Older plugins (like jQuery Form v2.43) may rely on custom extensions or legacy behavior not supported in newer versions of jQuery.
* *Script Load Order*: {{handleError}} might be defined in another script that hasn’t loaded yet when this code runs.

*How to Fix It* Here are a few possible fixes:

# *Define* {{$.handleError}} *Yourself* If you don’t need advanced error handling, you could define a simple fallback:

$.handleError = function (s, xhr, status, e) {

    console.error("jQuery Form plugin error:", status, e);

};



# *Check Plugin Compatibility* Make sure the jQuery Form plugin version is compatible with the version of jQuery you’re using. If you're on a newer jQuery version, consider upgrading to a modern form plugin or updating {{jquery.form.js}}.
# *Review Script Order* Ensure any script that defines or extends jQuery with {{handleError}} is loaded before {{jquery.form-2.43.js}}.

summary: Lessons Checklist edit link icon alignment issue after linking item on page
description:
h2. Problem

When editing a checklist in Lessons and linking checklist items to page content, odd horizontal spacing occurs that affects the visual alignment of the edit interface.

h2. Steps to Reproduce

# Create a site with Lessons and Resources tools
# On the Lessons page, create a checklist with at least two items
# Verify no changes have been made by uploading a default.css file
# On the Lessons page, create one linkable item (content link, assignment, quiz, etc.)
# On the Lessons page, edit the checklist and link one of the checklist items to the linkable item
# Once the item is linked, observe the odd horizontal spacing that occurs in the edit interface

h2. Expected Result

The checklist edit interface should maintain consistent spacing and alignment regardless of whether items are linked or not.

h2. Actual Result

After linking a checklist item to page content, odd horizontal spacing occurs in the edit interface, disrupting the visual alignment.

h2. Environment

* Sakai version: Latest trunk
* Browser: Multiple (Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge)
* Device: Desktop

h2. Additional Notes

This issue appears to be CSS-related, affecting the visual presentation of the checklist edit interface specifically after items have been linked to page content.

summary: Single Instance Store in Content Hosting: replaced content served instead of original
description:
After implementing [https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-48238|https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-48238|smart-link], if a file that was previously uploaded and later replaced in one site is uploaded again (with its original content) in a different site, the system may serve the replaced version instead of the newly uploaded one. This means that instructors uploading what they believe is their own file may unknowingly expose content uploaded by someone else. Also, the browser console shows a {{net::ERR_HTTP2_PROTOCOL_ERROR}} and the image preview fails to load, although downloading the file returns the replaced version, not the file the instructor just uploaded.

This is a critical issue, as it results in file content leaks across sites, potentially exposing private or inappropriate material without the instructor's knowledge.

summary: Allow samigo Tests&Quizzes access to "Total Scores" also for submission count = 0

summary: Improve Canvas CC import into Sakai

Canvas Syllabus Import

* Detection: Enhanced identifyCanvasEntityFiles() to detect resources with intendeduse="syllabus"
* Import Logic: Added syllabus import handler that:
** Extracts HTML content from Canvas syllabus files
** Creates syllabus entries using Sakai's SyllabusManager

* Entity Exclusion: Canvas syllabus files are excluded from generic resource processing

  Canvas Discussion Import

* Detection: Enhanced Canvas entity detection for imsdt_xmlv1p1 resource types
* Import Logic: Added discussion import handler that:
** Parses Canvas discussion XML files for title and HTML content
** Uses Sakai's ForumInterface to create forum topics
** Adds discussion topics to lesson pages as forum items
* Entity Exclusion: Canvas discussion files are excluded from generic resource processing

  Technical Implementation

* Dependencies: Added sakai-syllabus-api dependency to lessonbuilder tool
* Service Integration: Initialized SyllabusManager and MessageForumsForumManager services
* Error Handling: Added comprehensive exception handling and logging
* Variable Naming: Fixed compilation conflicts with proper variable scoping

  The implementation follows the established pattern of detecting Canvas entities early in the import process and processing them as their intended Sakai objects rather than generic resources. This
  ensures a clean import experience where Canvas syllabi appear in the Syllabus tool and discussions appear as forum topics, rather than creating resource folders with XML files.

description:
If the instructor creates an assignment with a resubmission allowed and a student saves their initial attempt but does not submit:

* *Before* the due/late/resubmission date, the instructor should not see the draft text/file upload and be able to “Allow Extension”
** This is working currently
* *After* the due/late/resubmission date, if no submission has been made, the instructor should be able to see the draft text/file upload, be able to grade, and “Allow Resubmission”
** {color:#ff5630}Classic Grader: No indicator that this was a draft and the option is still “Allow Extension”{color}
** Sakai Grader: Draft label and text “*Still a draft - not submitted.*” {color:#ff5630}Option is still “Allow Extension”{color}
