* Student: Assignment shows as returned (when fixed, this should be “Allow Resubmission”)

summary: Assignments: Resubmission allowed, student submits, then saves draft (but not resubmitting) - instructor should see initial submission only before and after due/resubmission dates
description:
If the instructor creates an assignment with a resubmission allowed and a student submits the assignment, then reopens the assignment and adds text/file upload, and saves this second attempt as a draft:

* *Before* the due/late/resubmission date, the instructor should be able to see the student’s submission, but not the draft, and be able to “Allow Resubmission”
* *After* the due/late/resubmission date, the instructor should only see the student’s actual submission, not the draft (see [user] comment in [Assignments: Resubmission and Extensions|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1TkIZ3wDdhr65S9Lgk3KsQplAPTYxp-dmjUgflAfMYTA/edit?tab=t.0#heading=h.denp24ytois8] - red text)
** _Yes, if the student submitted prior to the due date and then started a new draft submission, the first submission should be available to the instructor. However, the draft submission would not be available._
** _After the due/late/resubmission date passes, the draft should only display if there were no actual submissions._
* Instructor grades, “Allows Resubmission”, saves and releases to student
* Student: Assignment shows as returned (when fixed, this should be “Allow Resubmission”)

summary: Reset password doesn't honour the configured site language
description:
Every multi-language organization must offer an internationalized experience for their users. This includes a gateway in every supported language. This is critical in countries with more than one official language, pretty common in Europe.

Reset password tool is internationalized so it loads the user’s preferred language, but this is a very dumb behavior because when somebody is trying to reset his password obviously he is not logged in yet. When there is no user, the tool loads the server’s language.

A mechanism for forcing a language in a site has been present in Sakai for years (see [https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-10393|https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-10393|smart-link] ) but Reset Password tool doesn’t honor this setting in Gateway sites.

description: If using anonymous grading for a group submitted assignment the Grade Overrides feature in the Legacy grading interface reveals the student identities. summary: Resources: Add optional Notification for file creation or modification
description: Resources has a drop-down notification option for new files or updating files. In discussing Notification in the QA meeting, I suggested that it could be convenient if Resources also had an optional Bullhorn/Notification for new files or file changes. This should be no notification by default, just like the email notification is, but allow instructors to send students a notification when there is new files available. Since this would just have binary option - Notification / No Notification, a checkbox may work.

summary: Assignments: Add an option for 'silent' modification with no student notification
description:
When an open assignment is modified, there is a notification that appears for students.

There are times when an instructor or administrator needs to make a change to an assignment that they do not want broadcast to the class. I would like to suggest an option when editing an assignment to not post a notification. This would allow minor changes for fixing problems not be announced to the entire class. 

It’s especially useful for admins or IDs who may be helping with troubleshooting. I don’t need students wondering who Christina is and why she’s updating their assignments when the instructor just needed some help with sending the assignment scores to Gradebook.

summary: Use Sonatype's new Central Portal to publish Sakai artifacts
description:
The [OSSRH service|https://central.sonatype.org/publish/publish-guide/] will reach end-of-life on June 30th, 2025. This coincides with the [end-of-life date of the underlying technology, Sonatype's Nexus Repository Manager v2|https://help.sonatype.com/en/sonatype-nexus-repository-2-sunsetting-information.html].

h2. What Does This Mean[⚓︎|https://central.sonatype.org/news/20250326_ossrh_sunset/#what-does-this-mean]

If you have been holding off migrating to the [Central Publisher Portal|https://central.sonatype.org/publish/publish-portal-guide/], now is the time to start your preparations. Please reach out to support if you encounter any issues with migration or require specific functionality that is present in OSSRH but not yet available in the Portal or listed below on our roadmap.

Going forward, we are prioritizing our development and support efforts significantly in the direction of the Portal. We will do our best to keep OSSRH operational and respond to OSSRH-related support tickets in a timely manner, however you may experience increased delays as we approach the end-of-life date.

h2. Roadmap[⚓︎|https://central.sonatype.org/news/20250326_ossrh_sunset/#roadmap]

In order to provide transparency on what the Central team will be working on between now and the above date, we wanted to share a high-level view of our upcoming roadmap.

h3. Support for Gradle and Other Publishers[⚓︎|https://central.sonatype.org/news/20250326_ossrh_sunset/#support-for-gradle-and-other-publishers]

Gradle support and support for other build tool plugins are two of the biggest feature requests we have received. [Third-party support|https://central.sonatype.org/publish/publish-portal-gradle/] has grown to meet the needs of many Gradle publishers. We'd like to specifically thank JReleaser for being an early-adopter of the Portal and working with us to improve the API design.

In order to fill in the remaining gaps and to provide support for more obscure tools, we have rolled out an [OSSRH Staging API service|https://central.sonatype.org/publish/publish-portal-ossrh-staging-api/] service that translates a subset of the Nexus Repository Manager 2 API into the API that the Portal provides. We will iterate on this service as we receive feedback from the community, so we encourage publishers to test it and let us know how it can be improved.

If you are a third-party plugin author that provides publishing capabilities to Maven Central via OSSRH, we would request that you provide equivalent capabilities for publishing via the Portal. [Version 1 of the API|https://central.sonatype.org/publish/publish-portal-api/] has been stabilized and will not receive any backwards-incompatible changes. Any incompatible changes would be a {{v2}} API version.

Once OSSRH is sunset, we will have more roadmap capacity to begin working on a first-party Gradle plugin. We are working with Sonatype's legal department to streamline the process of open sourcing Central-related plugins. This discussion is currently focused on our Maven plugin, but we intend to launch a first-party Gradle plugin as open source from day one.

h3. Organization Support[⚓︎|https://central.sonatype.org/news/20250326_ossrh_sunset/#organization-support]

Support for self-service management of publishing permissions is another of the most common feature requests we've received. In the coming months, we will roll out new organization and namespace management capabilities. Organization administrators will be able to invite users to their organizations, add/remove them from namespaces, and view an audit trail of actions taken related to the organization. This functionality will only be available to publishers that are entirely on the Portal.

h3. User Token Enhancements[⚓︎|https://central.sonatype.org/news/20250326_ossrh_sunset/#user-token-enhancements]

Improvements to the tokens used for publishing are another frequently requested feature. Over the next few months, we plan to roll out the following enhancements:

* Publishers can have multiple, named tokens
* Tokens can be scoped to specific namespaces, {{groupId}}s, or {{groupId}} and {{artifactId}} combinations
* Tokens can have defined expiration dates

We believe that these enhancements are a step towards providing a more secure experience for publishers.

h2. Questions[⚓︎|https://central.sonatype.org/news/20250326_ossrh_sunset/#questions]

If you have any questions, please contact [Central Support|mailto:[email]]. We expect to have a significant volume of support requests over the next several months as more projects migrate ahead of the sunset date, so please bear with us as we process the requests. We will work to ensure that this migration involves as little friction as possible. We appreciate your efforts to migrate to the new publishing method early and we look forward to supporting your publishing to Maven Central for many years to come.

summary: Test & Quizzes: strange calculation of total blank (unanswered) questions
description:
Currently, the calculation of blank (unanswered) responses in TotalScoresBean depends on the existence of ItemGradingData records with publishedAnswerId set to null. However, if a student does not reach all the questions (for example, due to time expiration or early submission), there may be no ItemGradingData record for those unvisited questions.

As a result, the sum of correct, incorrect, and blank answers may be less than the total number of questions, leading to inconsistent and confusing statistics.

I am not sure whether this is the expected behavior or a bug, since for different students who have visited the same number of questions, answered the same number, and never opened the same number, the calculation differs depending on how the exam ends.

summary: Assignments: assignment title for email reminders cut off
description:
When a student receives the reminder email that an assignment is due in 24 hours, the title of the assignment is cut off. Yet, if a student submits the assignment, the full title displays.

!image-20250827-161744.png|width=663,height=714,alt="image-20250827-161744.png"!

summary: Lessons: Student Content peer review rubric not imported
description:
When Lessons pages containing a Student Content component with a peer review rubric are imported to another site, the rubric is not included in the new site. The instructor would have to re-enable peer review and create a new rubric in each site. 

In 22.x, the rubric imports but isn’t selected. Instructors can check the box to add a peer review rubric, then select the radio button for their rubric.

summary: Lessons: Embedded announcements include draft announcements for instructor
description:
This is not a problem on 22.x or 23.x

The Embedded Announcements component on Lessons is including Draft announcements for the instructor (without showing the draft label). This would make it confusing for instructors who may think that the announcement is visible to the class. Students can not see these announcements in the widget. Date locked annnouncements do not have this problem.

summary: Lessons: Imported links to assignments remain pointed to original site
description:
When there is a link in Lessons to an assignment, and both tools are imported to a new site, the link has the original site name behind the link and is not visible to students.



I’m not seeing this in 25.x or earlier

summary: Assignments: ELFinder links are not correct after import
description:
This is working on 25.x

If an instructor creates a link to an assignment using the ELFinder in the CKEditor (say in Lessons) and the Assignments and link are imported into another site, the link should direct users to the assignment in that class, after it is republished. Instead, it continues to link to the original assignment and students get a 403 - Forbidden error.

summary: CKEditor: ELFinder links to Assignments, Discussions have square braces on import
description:
On import, ELFinder links to Assignments and Discussions have square braces added. 

In 22.x and 23.x, it is a single brace - [link]

In 23.x and 25.x it is a double brace - [ [link] ]

This looks ugly, especially as links to Resources or Samigo don’t get the braces added on import

!image-20250827-183717.png|width=369,height=350,alt="image-20250827-183717.png"!

summary: Roster: Profile always displays silhouette instead of profile pic
description: When viewing someone’s profile via the Roster tool, the image displayed is always the graduate silhouette instead of a profile pic or the user’s initials as expected. Perhaps this behavior may have been reverted sometime after [https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-50638|https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-50638|smart-link].

summary: Lessons: Imported, unvisited pages are listed as not in use
description:
When Lessons are newly imported, if there are multiple pages, any unvisited pages are listed as not in use on the Index of Pages.

This does not happen on 23.x.

summary: Sakai Profile: Defined email & pronouns not displayed
description:
The sakai-profile web component (a popover displayed when clicking the sakai-user-photo web component) no longer displays a user’s email address like it did in Sakai 23.

Furthermore, the sakai-profile can display pronouns but these are never passed to the component even when roster.display.pronouns is set to true in sakai.properties, allowing for the display of pronouns in the Roster.

The first part of this jira is a regression. The second part currently requires dev qa in order to set {{roster.display.user.pronouns=true}}, which is not set in sakai.properties on nightly.

summary: Lessons: Test & Discussion links do not restore description after changing item
description:
If Lessons and the linked tools are imported separately, the links in Lessons to tests, assignments, and discussions show “This item was copied from another site. It won't work until you do "Edit" and "Change ___" to pick a(n) ____ that is valid in this site.” This also happens if a test is deleted and republished or an assignment is duplicated and the original removed.

If the instructor follows those steps to change the linked item, Assignments restores any description that was originally in Lessons for that link. Links to Discussions or Tests & Quizzes lose their descriptions.

summary: Update Apache HttpCore 5.3.5 GA
description:
{noformat}Release 5.3.5
------------------

This maintenance release fixes several corner cases in the H2 protocol handler that could have been
potentially exploited to make H2 endpoints allocate extra resources and lead to Denial-of-Service
conditions. This release also improves handling of H2 stream abnormal termination.


Change Log
-------------------

* Improved H2 connection termination in case of the opposite endpoint failing to send GOAWAY
  frame.
  Contributed by Oleg Kalnichevski <olegk at apache.org>

* Bug fix: Corrected abnormal termination of H2 streams
  Contributed by Oleg Kalnichevski <olegk at apache.org>

* Use RequestNotExecutedException instead of ConnectionClosedException when failing enqueued
  requests that never got executed.
  Contributed by Oleg Kalnichevski <olegk at apache.org>

* H2 protocol handler to enforce a max limit on number of CONTINUATION frames.
  Contributed by Oleg Kalnichevski <olegk at apache.org>

* Bug fix: Fixed a potential 'End Stream Headers' vulnerability and adds test coverage for
  various HTTP/2 stream reset exploits.
  Contributed by Oleg Kalnichevski <olegk at apache.org>

* Improved ContentType Javadoc.
  Contributed Winfried Gerlach <Winfried.Gerlach at draeger.com>

* HTTPCORE-782: Non-blocking TLS session can end up in an endless loop in case of a protocol
  negotiation.
  Contributed by Oleg Kalnichevski <olegk at apache.org>

* Slightly better and efficient #toHexString method.
  Contributed by Oleg Kalnichevski <olegk at apache.org>{noformat}

summary: Assignments: Unable to edit an assignment due to Oracle treating empty strings as NULL
description:
We have found in production that some assignments, for some reason, end up with the property *prop_new_assignment_add_to_gradebook* set to *null*. This is unexpected behavior for Assignments and prevents these assignments from being saved. The number of cases is increasing over time, but we haven’t found a way to reproduce it.

The cases can be detected with the following query:

{noformat}select a.context,a.assignment_id,a.title,a.created_date,ap.name,to_char(ap.value) 
from asn_assignment_properties ap,
asn_assignment a
where ap.assignment_id=a.assignment_id
and ap.name in ('prop_new_assignment_add_to_gradebook')
and ap.value is null 
order by a.title,ap.name  {noformat}

summary: Migrate jclouds to minIO
description:
jclouds is in Apache attic.



h2. Key Gains

* remove length counting: streams unknown-length uploads using multipart (stream(in, -1, partSize)).
*  lower memory: no mark/reset read; memory bounded by part size/HTTP buffers.
*  faster uploads: single pass; no pre-read or temp copies unless you choose to dedupe first.
*  simpler deps: drop jclouds APIs and OSGi registries; one small SDK.
*  clearer errors/retries: MinIO client surfaces S3 errors and supports multipart retries.

Proposed Architecture

*  Keep FileSystemHandler: implement MinioFileSystemHandler alongside existing handlers.
*  Uploads: compute SHA-256 and count bytes inline while streaming to S3/MinIO; set hash/length post-upload.
*  Direct links: use MinIO getPresignedObjectUrl for signed GETs.
*  Downloads: stream object; optionally spill to temp file above a size threshold (same as today).
*  Metadata: keep id and path user metadata if needed for parity.

h3. Migration Plan

# Add MinIO dependency
#* io.minio:minio (8.x) to cloud-content/impl.
#* Remove jclouds deps from the S3 path; keep Swift temporarily (see deprecation).
# Implement MinioFileSystemHandler
    - Bold saveInputStream: wrap incoming stream with DigestInputStream + CountingInputStream, then:
     - {{putObject(PutObjectArgs.builder().bucket(bucket).object(key).stream(cis, -1, partSize).contentType(ct).build())}}
     - After upload: {{bytes = cis.getCount()}}, {{sha256Hex = bytesToHex(digest.digest())}}; set properties on the resource.

*  getInputStream: getObject streaming; temp-file spill threshold optional.
*  getAssetDirectLink: getPresignedObjectUrl with configurable expiry.
*  delete: removeObject.

# Wire Spring config
#* New bean: org.sakaiproject.content.api.FileSystemHandler.minio.
#* Update sakai-configuration.xml alias to point to minio handler.
#* New props: endpoint, accessKey, secretKey, baseContainer (bucket), useIdForPath, signedUrl.expirySeconds, optional partSizeMB.
#* New props: endpoint, accessKey, secretKey, baseContainer (bucket), useIdForPath, signedUrl.expirySeconds, optional partSizeMB.
# Eliminate content-length counting
    - Remove markableInputStream() + markableStreamLength() usage from S3 path.
    - Keep temp-file hashing only if you must dedupe by SHA-256 before upload; otherwise compute while streaming.
5. Deprecate jclouds
    -  S3 BlobStore: mark deprecated now; remove next major release after one cycle.
    -  Swift: mark deprecated now; remove next major release unless you identify active users.
    - Provide migration notes and property mapping.
6. Backward compatibility
    - Maintain old property keys but ignore them (emit warnings) when MinIO is active.
    - Provide opt-in flag to continue old handlers for one release if needed.

summary: Import From Site: Lessons allows selection of removed/not in use pages
description:
Might be related to [https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-51712|https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-51712|smart-link], as I noticed this while verifying. 

In Lessons, pages may be removed but are still available to re-add. The Index of Pages shows them as not in use. When going to Site Info → Import From Site, if a user expands the list of Lessons pages to only import a subset, the not in use pages are listed too, but they don’t appear to be importable. I would expect that unused / removed pages would not appear in this list. 

We have several cases where an instructor removes an old page and replaces it with a new one with the same name, with updated content. Both would be listed on the Import From Site list, but there’s no indication which one is the new / active page.

summary: Assignments anonymous grading setting removed when editing assignment after due date
description:
If an instructor goes in to check the “Hide submitters' identities (e.g. for anonymous grading)” setting for an assignment after the due date for that assignment, the check is removed when the user receives the message about editing an assignment after the due date. 

The use case for this is when an assignment is set for anonymous grading, but after the fact, an instructor has a need to enter a score for an individual student. Changing the assignment setting from anonymous to non-anonymous and back again is the easiest way to do this, but the removal of the check mark makes this frustrating for the instructor, since they may not notice that the check has been removed before saving again.

summary: Lessons: Show indication of top-level pages being required, not released until prerequisites are completed
description:
Currently, there is no indication if a top-level Lessons page is set to be required and/or set to not be released until prerequisites are completed. Hidden Lessons pages have the padlock and eye icons appearing next to the page name on the left. Date locked pages have a message for instructors at the top of the page - Note: This page will not be available to standard users until <date>. You can change this in the Settings window.

I feel it would be beneficial to include the other potential messages based on the settings:

Note: Completion of this page may be required for standard users to access other pages. You can change this in the Settings window.

Note: This page will not be available to standard users until prior required pages are completed. You can change this in the Settings window.

summary: Dashboard course cards: fix image sizing/cropping by using background-image (preserve cover/center/no-repeat)
description:
* Problem: On Home Dashboard, course card images are inconsistently cropped or appear as black squares. The inline background: shorthand on the .info-block resets background-size, background-position, and background-repeat,
overriding stylesheet longhands.
** User impact: Course images display random portions or look black, reducing visual fidelity and causing confusion.
** Root cause: Inline style="background: linear-gradient(...), url(...)" resets background sub-properties defined in SCSS.
** Regression introduced: a73bad699a4e4c1bb409de12a5c709e644c203ab (SAK-48986 “Dashboard add course list to home dashboard”) on 2024-06-05.
** Fix:
*** Change inline style to only set background-image so SCSS background-size: cover; background-position: center; background-repeat: no-repeat; apply.
*** Correct SCSS to explicitly set background-repeat: no-repeat.
** Files touched:
*** webcomponents/tool/src/main/frontend/packages/sakai-course-card/src/SakaiCourseCard.js (use background-image)
*** library/src/skins/default/src/sass/webcomponents/course-card/_course-card.scss (use background-repeat: no-repeat)
** Notes:
*** Keeps gradient via CSS variables (--sakai-course-card-gradient-start/end).
*** No behavioral change when a course has no image; no-background link style still applies.
*** Optional enhancement (separate ticket): allow --sakai-course-card-background-size to switch between cover|contain.

summary: Update Lombok 1.18.40
description:
h3. v1.18.40 (September 4th, 2025)

* PLATFORM: JDK25 support added [#3859|https://github.com/[user]/lombok/issues/3859].
* BUGFIX: Recent versions of eclipse (or the eclipse-based java lang server for VSCode) caused {{java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: Document does not match the AST}}. [Issue #3886|https://github.com/[user]/lombok/issues/3886].

* IMPROBABLE BREAKING CHANGE: From versions 1.18.16 to 1.18.38, lombok automatically copies certain Jackson annotations (e.g., {{[user]}}) from fields to the corresponding accessors (getters/setters). summary: Site Info: Display expand/collapse only for tools supporting granular import
description:
For the granular import feature introduced with [https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-49673|https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-49673|smart-link], expand/collapse buttons are displayed for all tools regardless of whether or not they have entities that can be imported piecemeal. 

This is especially problematic for Gradebook where all its content is copied even if the user only selects one of its entities to be copied. Also, external gradebook items (e.g., items sourced from Assignments or Test & Quizzes) are currently listed under Gradebook via this feature when they shouldn’t be. Because of these reasons and given that Gradebook is not mentioned in [https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-49673|https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-49673|smart-link], I assume that granular import was not intended to support Gradebook.

I propose fixing this by applying server-side logic to only display the expand/collapse button for tools that have entities that can be granularly copied. This also means that such a button will not display for Gradebook.

summary: Implement copy in FileSystemHandler
description:
Today, copying Resources typically streams file bytes through the Sakai app server. This is slow and wasteful when using filesystem/S3-compatible storage.

  This change introduces two complementary optimizations:

* Reference copy during site copy (“Import from Site”): new resources reuse the source blob (same filePath) without duplicating bytes.
* Server-side/object-store copy for explicit resource copies: when a physical duplicate is required (Resources “Copy”), bytes are copied within the storage backend via API, not through Sakai.

  Both paths preserve metadata (length, SHA-256, MIME type) and events. No configuration flags are added.



h1. Technical Design

* Reference copy (site copy):
** Modify BaseContentService.transferCopyEntities(...) to create the destination resource as a reference copy when filesystem/object storage is in use and the source has a blob:
*** set referenceCopy to source id
*** reuse source m_filePath
*** set contentLength and contentSha256 from source
** Fall back to the existing stream path when reference copy is not applicable.
* Server-side copy (resource copy):
** Extend FileSystemHandler with copy(sourceId, sourceRoot, sourcePath, destId, destRoot, destPath) → long size.
** Implement copy(...) in:
*** DefaultFileSystemHandler: local Files.copy (replace existing).
*** BlobStoreFileSystemHandler (jclouds): BlobStore.copyBlob(...), with stream fallback when provider lacks server-side copy.
** Override DbContentService.copyResource(...) to:
*** use reference copy when requested
*** else call fileSystemHandler.copy(...) to create a distinct object without streaming; set length/SHA-256; commit metadata
*** on error, fall back to the prior stream-based copy
* Eventing and scanning:
** Site copy path continues to commit via storage and post add/new-version events as before.
** Resource copy override commits via commitResourceEdit(...): events and virus scan queue still occur; Tika re-detection is skipped since bytes are identical.

summary: Assignments: Additional Item attachment closes the Add dialog
description: When an instructor creates an assignment and adds an additional item - model answer or all purpose item, adding an attachment to this closes the additional item editor, which may be problematic if the instructor was still entering information or wanted to add another attachment from a different location.

summary: Assignments: Model Answer, All Purpose Items shouldn't require text
description: In Assignments, the model answer and all purpose item have the option for attachments and text, and text is required. I feel that there are cases when an attachment is sufficient. Forcing the instructor to enter text for these feels unnecessary.

summary: Date picker reset dates when editing because it receives an incorrect ISO format
description:
After [https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-51931|https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-51931|smart-link] was fixed the date picker works, but when an evaluation is created and is edited later, the date picker resets to current date and time, losing saved values.

This happens because the date picker receives the values in an incorrect ISO format. A little change for correcting the format fixes it.

summary: Content remove legacy XML ORMs and legacy conversion pipeline
description:
If you look at DbContentService.java

[https://github.com/sakaiproject/sakai/blob/master/kernel/kernel-impl/src/main/java/org/sakaiproject/content/impl/DbContentService.java#L723|https://github.com/sakaiproject/sakai/blob/master/kernel/kernel-impl/src/main/java/org/sakaiproject/content/impl/DbContentService.java#L723|smart-link] 

The pre-fix code in this method is (a) doing some optional conversion from XML to binary and then (b) looking at the schema through a series of queries to determine of metadata in the content, collection, and deleted content tables is serialized in XML, Binary, or both.

The reality is that for many years now, all the metadata has been binary serialized except for first time a Sakai server is started with an empty database.  The {{sakai_content.sql}} bootstraps essential top level collections into the {{CONTENT_COLLECTION}} table using the XML field.  Given that there is a binary serialization field, once the table is created and bootstrapped the {{DbStorage}} method re-serializes the {{XML}} column into {{BINARY_ENTITY}} and forever and ever the {{XML}} in all columns will be {{NULL}} and only {{BINARY_ENTITY}} is the only column that will be used.

You might think that just changing the  {{sakai_content.sql}} to generate the {{BINARY_ENTITY}} column during setup and dispense with XML forever.  I have tried that and it is horrible.  The binary serialization in Sakai is horribly complex and not conducive to working for anything other than intricate Java code.  It is like Python’s {{pickle}} capability but harder to understand - for a fun time take a look at {{Type1BaseContentResourceSerializer}} - it is over the top in unnecessary complexity and super fragile to change - so we should leave it alone for now.

So ultimately the {{XML}} column is only used in the first server start after fresh database so at runtime, once we have started once (including later in the first startup) we can pretend that XML does not exist.  So we can always use {{BaseDbBinarySingleStorage}} as the ORM class for content resources, content collections, and deleted resources.

So the logic in {{DbStorage()}} can be reduced to (a) if there are any non-null XML fields re-serialize them as binary. (b) use {{BaseDbBinarySingleStorage}} at runtime.  As a side effect, this removes the last use of the {{BaseDbDualSingleStorage}} ORM class which can be removed.

While this in many ways is not changing any run-time behavior, it does mean that if a future developer decides to move from {{BINARY_ENTITY}} to a data model with fully realized columns (i.e. like JPA) the starting point will be much clearer.  It will be clear that there is one and only one data model in the Content service.  And as we work on and extend the Content service we don’t have to look at {{DbStorage()}} and wonder which ORM class is in use and try to do things that work across three different ORM classes.  Also, AI will be able to better understand how the service code and ORM code work together if there are no more run-time decisions being made.

summary: Site import is overwriting all tool permissions during import
description:
*Scenario:* An instructor is in the middle of the academic term and they’ve configured their course site’s permissions in various tools to accommodate one or more teaching assistants who have various TA tasks and/or prohibitions across those tools. Using the granular import feature introduced with [https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-49673|https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-49673|smart-link], the instructor then decides (for example) to copy one assignment (as opposed to everything from the Assignments tool) from a course site used long ago. Furthermore, that source site’s and tool’s set of permissions differ from those set in the current (target) course site. Sometime after importing that one assignment, the TA seems to all-of-a-sudden hit a roadblock in their task (or have access to something they shouldn’t). 

*Root issue:* The above scenario typifies one of possibly many other kinds where the copying of tool permissions from one site to another needs to be uniquely distinguished from copying discrete items (referred to as entities in the server logic) from a particular tool.

*One approach (but not sufficient):* Investigating this code, I observe that one approach that could resolve many such scenarios would be to revise several methods in SiteManageServiceImpl.java, to attach a FunctionManager to this bean, and add a new method to EntityTransferrer like “getToolPermissionsPrefix” to query the function manager for tool specific properties to exclude from copying (in SiteManageServiceImpl.copyToolPermissions) from one site to another.

Even with such an approach implemented, there are still gaps to address for clarifying the user’s intent about copying permissions vis-a-vis checkbox interaction. See below. 

*Open UI/UX issues:* Should an explicit checkbox labeled “{tool name} permission” be introduced (when a tool has entities that might be copied) to disambiguate whether a tool’s permissions are desired to be copied? Something like this might be needed or at least determined before addressing inconsistencies in automated checking/unchecking checkboxes as demonstrated in the attached screencast: DoWeNeedGranularPermissionsCheckbox-20250916.mp4. (For what it’s worth, the screencast exhibits an adoption of a proposed fix for [https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-51934|https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-51934|smart-link].

summary: System-wide bullhorns (like MOTD) cause system slowness and 504 html errors so they should be configurable
description:
In [https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-49298|https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-49298|smart-link] the MOTD messages were added to portal bullhorns. The idea is really nice, but we are having performance issues in our production environment. The admin user receives a timeout error message.

Having that system-wide notifications are a heavy load for the platform, we think that they should be configurable with a property so in case of issues they could be disabled.

Of course, if the performance issues are fixed will be even better, but a property would be also useful.

PD: We have also found that the notifications are sent only to local users (in SAKAI_USER table) but not to external LDAP users. So this issue could have been even worse.

summary: Tests & Quizzes: Anonymous grading regression - student names exposed in submission navigation dropdown
description:
h2. Problem

SAK-36952 was supposedly fixed in 2012, but the bug has regressed. In anonymous grading mode, the submission navigation dropdown in the instructor grading view exposes student names and IDs, completely defeating the purpose of anonymous grading.

h2. Steps to Reproduce

# Create a quiz with anonymous grading enabled
# Have students submit the quiz
# As instructor, go to grade submissions
# Click on a student submission to view individual submission
# Observe the navigation dropdown shows "Albertson, Albert (student0011)" instead of anonymous ID

h2. Current Behavior

Navigation dropdown exposes student names even in anonymous grading mode

h2. Expected Behavior

Dropdown should show anonymous identifiers like "Submission ID: 23"

h2. Root Cause

SubmissionNavBean.populate() method always displays student names regardless of anonymous grading setting

h2. Privacy Impact

Critical privacy violation that completely undermines anonymous grading functionality

h2. Related Issues

Regression of SAK-36952 (marked as Fixed in 2012).

The breaking commit was 033ca645e7b from July 21, 2023, as part of S2U-15 (Tests & Quizzes: Improve navigation when grading). This was a new feature that introduced the navigation dropdown but didn't account for anonymous grading.

summary: Granular import will not instantiate tools
description:
This jira is similar to [https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-49898|https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-49898|smart-link] but distinct in at least two ways:

# The focus of this jira is the act of importing select contents from a tool (as opposed to everything from that tool)
# I am no longer able to reproduce the conditions per the test plan for SAK-49898 (as in that jira might be deemed resolved.)

*Root concern:* If a user seeks to select only a few assignments from the Assignments tool in Site A (i.e., not everything in Assignments) to copy to Site B and Site B does not have the Assignments tool, the user would expect that the Assignments tool would appear in Site B after the import. This is currently not happening, and this condition holds for most if not all such tools (e.g,, Syllabus, Tests & Quizzes, etc.)

The above should hold provided that site.setup.import.addmissingtools is set to true in sakai.properties.

summary: Out-of-order criterion causes rubrics failure for instructor
description:
* In rubrics/impl/src/main/java/org/sakaiproject/rubrics/impl/RubricsServiceImpl.java:385-394, the reorder handler builds sorted with sortedCriterionIds.stream().map(current::get) without checking for missing IDs. When the client sends an ID that no longer exists (stale drag-and-drop data or a concurrent delete), current::get returns null, that null is reinserted into the JPA-managed list, and Hibernate still advances the [user] position for that slot. The next real criterion is written with the following index, leaving a gap such as 1,2,4,5.
** The same pattern appears for ratings in rubrics/impl/src/main/java/org/sakaiproject/rubrics/impl/RubricsServiceImpl.java:397-404, so the symptom can also occur for rbc_rating.order_index.



h2. Fix Ideas

Filter or reject missing IDs before re-adding the list, for example {{sortedCriterionIds.stream().map(current::get).filter(Objects::nonNull)}} (and log/abort if any were missing). Do the equivalent for ratings.

Optionally harden the API by validating that the client sent exactly the current set of IDs, so stale requests fail fast instead of corrupting the ordering.

summary: Assignment-created gradebook item can select a different rubric than the assignment
description:
If you create an assignment that uses a rubric, and create a gradebook item when you save the assignment, the user is still able to go to the gradebook item and change the rubric association in the gradebook. However, this does not update the rubric association in the assignment. Instead, it results in two different rubrics being shown as attached to the item - one in the assignment settings, and a different one in the gradebook. Changing the assignment rubric selection after creation does not seem to update the rubric shown in the gradebook either. 

The rubric setting should not be able to be changed for the gradebook item independently of the assignment. It should either be disabled in Gradebook (as the grade entry options are) or it should update the assignment settings if it is changed in Gradebook. While the item can only be graded from Assignments (and therefore the rubric selected in Assignments is the only you can actually use to grade), it is still very confusing to the instructor to see two different rubric selections for the same item in two different tools.

summary: Add TransferBean style objects to the LTI API
description:
This work will add simple POJO transfer beans to the LTI API.  The implementations will be built so that there is a lossless transfer between the Map<String, Object> represented preferred by FOORM and the POJOs representing the same objects.   Also a number of the loading methods will be overloaded to allow client code to receive its results as POJOs as an alternative to Map<String, Object>.

This will allow the code that uses services to start retrieving tools and content items as POJOs if they like.  The code that will be easiest to convert from Map<> to POJO will be code that simply retrieves objects and looks at them.  Updating and storing objects will be a little trickier.

This will introduce the POJOs, the conversion utilities, and service implementations and choose one area to actually convert to using the POJOs.

This Jira will convert the LTI13Service servlet to using POJOs - these are the API endpoints for LTI 1.3 for line items, etc.   Future JIRAs will make changes to switch from  Map objects to POJO objects one at a time so each area can be individually tested.

This will be applied to various areas of LTI but also to other services that make use of LTIService like Assignments and Lessons.

summary: Update Apache httpcore 5.3.6
description:
{noformat}Release 5.3.6
------------------

This maintenance release fixes a regression introduced by the previous release that can cause
a temporary I/O spin during HTTP/2 connection shutdown in case the opposite endpoint fails
to send a GOAWAY frame, and also fixes several bugs related to abnormal termination of HTTP/2
connections found since the last release.


Change Log
-------------------

* Bug fix: #disconnected method of protocol handlers is to be called only once
  the underlying I/O session has been fully closed out.
  Contributed by Oleg Kalnichevski <olegk at apache.org>

* Bug fix: Fixed a race between async I/O session termination and command submission.
  Contributed by Oleg Kalnichevski <olegk at apache.org>

* Bug fix: Async I/O sessions to explicitly close the I/O channel for output in GRACEFUL
  close mode.
  Contributed by Oleg Kalnichevski <olegk at apache.org>

* Bug fix: Classic HTTP server to keep RequestListener thread running when an exception
  occurs during initialization of the incoming connection.
  Contributed by Christian de Waal <christian at de.waal.name>

* Regression: Improved HTTP/2 connection termination in case of the opposite endpoint
  failing to send a GOAWAY frame (correction).
  Contributed by Oleg Kalnichevski <olegk at apache.org>{noformat}

summary: Content: Custom FileSystemHandler injection is broken
description: There are multiple implementations of {{FileSystemHandler}} that handle persistence of Sakai resources. By default, the {{DefaultFileSystemHandler}} is active which handles interactions with the file system. Sakai allows the configuration of other implementations that enable storage in AWS S3 or Swift object storage. But the configuration of other implementations is broken since [https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-49808|https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-49808|smart-link].

summary: Webcomponents: Run tests in test phase so they respect the -DskipTests flag
description: The tests in {{webcomponents}} always run, even if the {{-DskipTests}} flag is provided. This is causing the build to take way longer then it has to in situations where the test don’t need to run. Unfortunately, the tests sometimes fail for unexpected reasons - even if the developer is not touching {{webcomponents}}, which can make Sakai deployment frustrating. This also adds the requirement to install packages for running playwright just to compile Sakai. The test execution can be added configured for the {{test}} phase, then the {{-DskipTests}} is respected.

summary: Library: Bootstrap classes bg-primary and text-primary don't apply the correct skin-styles
description: The Bootstap classes {{bg-primary}} and {{text-primary}} don’t assign the Sakai skin variables correctly. They are defined in one rule, applying both {{color}} and {{background-color}}, though they are overridden by the default style as they use !important. I intent to separate those styles, applying Sakai brand color to both {{color}} and {{background-color}} properties respectively, also adding !important to actually override the bootstrap defaults.

summary: Add legacy-UTF8 protection around notification titles
description:
Added legacy-UTF8 protection around notification titles to handle supplementary Unicode code points (like emojis) that may cause issues in legacy systems.

h2. Changes Made:

* *When* {{content.cleaner.filter.utf8=true}}, notification titles are now scanned before persistence
* Supplementary code points are either:
** Converted to HTML decimal entities (default behavior)
** Replaced with the configured {{content.cleaner.filter.utf8.replacement}} string
* *Notification titles are decoded back to display form* when read so the UI/push payload still shows emojis on modern browsers
* *Brought in the emoji helper* used elsewhere in kernel to keep behavior consistent (HTML decimal encoding only when an actual emoji is detected)

h2. Technical Details:

* Affects: {{UserMessagingServiceImpl.java}}
* Ensures backward compatibility with legacy systems while maintaining modern emoji display
* Uses existing kernel emoji detection utilities for consistency

summary: LTI Remove unused lti13_setting field from tool and content and lti13 flag from content
description:
The {{lti13_settings}}field is actually a hold over from LTI 2.0 - and I left it in for a while hoping that LTI 1.3 would re-add a settings service (which I felt was a good feature).  But time passed, and the feature was not added to LTI 1.3 - it was superseded by the much more complex link service so it is not likely to come back.  We removed the support for the (never used) settings service to set and get the settings some time ago and it is time to remove the columns from the database and model as well.

Also there is an {{lti13}} flag in content that needs to be removed.  The {{lti13}} flag in the tool is what is used.  Back in the day, I thought as part of the LTI 1.1 → 1.3 transition it might be nice to back to have one content item use 1.1 while all the rest used 1.3.  The LTI 1.1 to 1.3 transition across all LMS’s was weird and spotty and few LTI tools really were prepared from a content item level flexibility of launch type.  The {{lti13}} flag in _content_ is not read or written anywhere in the code base so it should be removed.  

The {{lti13}} flag in the tool is essential and will remain the signal to launch code as to which protocol to use.

summary: Update Apache HttpComponents Client 5.5.1 GA
description:
{noformat}Release 5.5.1
------------------

This is a maintenance release that fixes several defects in the connection management
code and a regression in the DIGEST authentication reported since the previous release.
It also upgrades HttpCore to version 5.3.6.


Change Log
-------------------

* HTTPCLIENT-2391: Improved GRACEGUL shutdown of ExecutorService used internally by async
  clients.
  Contributed by Oleg Kalnichevski <olegk at apache.org>

* Bug fix: Use a 1 second timeout when closing out connections inside a connection pool lock.
  Contributed by Oleg Kalnichevski <olegk at apache.org>

* Clarified the behavior of the protocol-level responseTimeout and the connection management
  level socketTimeout and their interrelation.
  Contributed by ChangYong <lcy9002 at naver.com>

* Bug fix: Connection managers to ensure open connections have a socket timeout set based on
  ConnectionConfig upon lease.
  Contributed by Oleg Kalnichevski <olegk at apache.org>

* HTTPCLIENT-2393: Remove `rspauth` attribute from `Authorization` DIGEST header (#716)
  RFC 7616 compliance: rspauth is server-side (Authentication-Info 3.5) only.
  Contributed by Arturo Bernal <abernal at apache.org>

* HTTPCLIENT-2386: Classic transport to use the connect timeout as a default if the TLS timeout has
  not been explicitly set.
  Contributed by Oleg Kalnichevski <olegk at apache.org>

* HTTPCLIENT-2384: Socket options related to TcpKeepAlive are ignored.
  Contributed by Oleg Kalnichevski <olegk at apache.org>

* HTTPCLIENT-2371: Logging of request re-execution at INFO priority.
  Contributed by Oleg Kalnichevski <olegk at apache.org>

* HTTPCLIENT-2379: Fixed a defect in H2SharingConnPool causing an IllegalStateException
  when releasing the same connection from multiple threads. (#663)
  Contributed by Arturo Bernal <[email]>

* Fixed the behavior of the `validateAfterInactivity` connection setting by the async
  connection manager.
  Contributed by Ryan Schmitt <rschmitt at apache.org>

* HTTPCLIENT-2376: Fixed the problem with ContentCompressionExec not taking `acceptEncoding`
  parameter into account.
  Contributed by Oleg Kalnichevski <olegk at apache.org>

* HTTPCLIENT-2372: Normalize HttpHost port comparison to treat implicit default ports as
  equal (#643).
  Contributed by Arturo Bernal <[email]>

* Maven wrapper
  Contributed by Ryan Schmitt <rschmitt at apache.org>

* Bump org.junit:junit-bom from 5.12.2 to 5.13.0 #639.
  Contributed by Gary Gregory <garydgregory at gmail.com>

* Bump testcontainers.version from 1.20.6 to 1.21.1 #638.
  Contributed by Gary Gregory <garydgregory at gmail.com>{noformat}

summary: Upgrade to JDK 21
description:
*Upgrade Critical Frameworks and Libraries*

* *Spring Framework core (LOE: High · Priority: P0):* move from Spring Framework 5.3.x (OSS EOL: June 2023) to 6.2.x+ so the platform stays on a supported line with native Java 21 runtime support. This re
quires adopting Jakarta EE 9+ namespaces across tools and aligning Spring Data, Web, and integration starters with the new baseline.
* *Spring Security platform (LOE: High · Priority: P0):* upgrade the security stack to Spring Security 6.2+ so authentication/authorization layers are certified on Java 21, and so the project inherits the
Spring Framework 6.1/6.2 baselines. Plan for method-security annotation refactors, new defaults (deferred {{SecurityContext}} saving), and Project Reactor alignment for reactive modules.
* *Authentication & SAML (LOE: High · Priority: P0):* replace end-of-life {{spring-security-saml2-core}} 1.0.10.RELEASE and CAS 3.6.x usage in {{login/login-tool}} with Spring Security’s supported SAML 2.1+ s
ervice-provider features (OpenSAML 4 baseline). Expect to rework XML metadata handling, bootstrapping, and certificate rollover, and to refit any custom filters around the new APIs.
* *Hibernate / persistence (LOE: High · Priority: P0):* migrate from Hibernate ORM 5.6.x (limited support, only certified through Java 18) to Hibernate 6.5+ for official Java 21 compatibility, new SQL gen
eration, and updated Jakarta Persistence APIs. Account for query syntax differences, identifier handling, and batch fetching changes.
* *Jakarta Faces / JSF stack (LOE: Medium · Priority: P1):* inventory JSF 2.3-era code (Mojarra/MyFaces, OmniFaces) still on {{javax.*}}. Target Jakarta Faces 4.1 (Java 17+ minimum, validated on Java 21) an
d refresh component libraries to Jakarta EE 10+ so templated tools (e.g., legacy JSF portlets) continue to run after the JDK uplift. This will require updating to Tomcat 10.
* *Wicket modules (LOE: Medium · Priority: P1):* converge the mix of Wicket 6/8/9 modules on Apache Wicket 10.x, which is built for Java 17+ and tested on Java 21. Use the OpenRewrite migration recipes to
modernize component packages and remove legacy servlet dependencies before the JDK switch.
* *Velocity templating (LOE: Medium · Priority: P1):* retire Apache Velocity 1.6.4 (impacted by CVE-2020-13936) and move templated code to Velocity 2.3+ or alternate templating engines compatible with Jav
a 21. Review any sandbox customizations and ensure template inputs remain validated after the upgrade.
* *Legacy XML toolchain (LOE: Medium · Priority: P1):* inventory modules tied to {{simple-xml}} 2.7.x (e.g., {{kernel/api}}, {{kernel/kernel-impl}}, {{userauditservice}}) and Apache XMLBeans 4.0.0 ({{samigo/samlit e-impl}}). {{simple-xml}} has been unmaintained since 2014 and only targets Java 8-era APIs, while XMLBeans 5.3.1 (released March 2024) is actively maintained and runs on JDK 8+. Immediate playbook:
*# Generate a full usage report ({{rg "simple-xml"}} and {{rg "xmlbeans"}}) and capture deserialization entry points plus tests that guard them.
*# Prototype migrating one representative {{simple-xml}} consumer (e.g., {{kernel/api/src/main/java/org/sakaiproject/util/FormattedText.java}}) to Jackson data-binding; measure serialization diffs and add re
gression fixtures.
*# Document why XMLBeans exists: {{samigo/samlite-impl}} uses XMLBeans-generated IMS QTI 1.2 bindings ({{org.imsglobal.xsd.imsQtiasiv1P2.*}}) to parse Samigo Lite assessment uploads. Capture the schema sourc
e, generation script (if any), and the parser entry points ({{SamLiteServiceImpl.parse}}).
*# Upgrade XMLBeans to 5.3.1 in {{samigo/samlite-impl/pom.xml}}, regenerate the IMS QTI bindings, and run {{mvn -pl samigo/samlite-impl test}} plus a Samigo Lite import smoke test to verify compatibility.
*# Draft a rollout checklist (schema regeneration scripts, regression test suites, QA sign-off) so remaining modules can follow the same pattern without blocking the wider JDK migration.
* *Application container & shared services (LOE: Medium · Priority: P1):* confirm the Tomcat baseline supports the latest Jakarta Servlet APIs required by upgraded frameworks (Tomcat 10.1+/11 for Java 21)
and update shared services (email, content hosting, job scheduler) that rely on container-specific APIs.
* *Security-adjacent libraries (LOE: Medium · Priority: P2):* modernize Nimbus JOSE, jjwt, BouncyCastle, Apache Commons, and other cryptography/IO packages to releases tested on Java 21, coordinating with
platform security reviews.
* *GenericDAO abstraction (LOE: High · Priority: P1):* audit usages of {{org.sakaiproject.genericdao}} across hierarchy, signup, polls, entitybroker, and other tools to ensure compatibility with Hibernate 6
.x. The custom DAO layer relies on Hibernate 5-era session APIs; plan either to adapt it to Hibernate 6.5 or to migrate high-value modules onto Spring Data repositories. Document extension points and identify modules that can be retired to reduce maintenance surface. A solution could be simply to remove Generic DAO as it is really not needed anymore.
* *Modernize Test Tooling*
** Update Mockito (≥5.x), JUnit (vintage vs. Jupiter), and other test libraries to versions certified on Java 21.
** Replace or refactor usages of PowerMock 2.0.9 and outdated bytecode instrumentation that break under the new JVM.
** Confirm integration/e2e harnesses (e.g., Selenium, Playwright) and service test containers build on JDK 21 images.

description:
rwiki has all sorts of custom XSL transformations for outdated things like RSS 1.0, RSS 2.0, Atom, print to PDF.

Note that Print to PDF is a decent feature, and if there is demand for it, we can re-implement it using modern technologies (e.g., openPDF).

But we are supporting tons of old XML transformations in this old code. And removing it allows us to upgrade core dependencies.

summary: Calculated Question warning on edit if formulas, variables not changed
description:
Tests & Quizzes calculated question has a warning on edit “You have not changed variables, global variables or formulas.  Are you sure that you want to Save?” if the instructor has not modified one of these fields. 

This appears at times that feel annoying - 

* Editing other question settings (Extra credit, point value)
* Editing text in the question that isn’t a variable
* After editing formulas/variables if they clicked Check Forumulas and did not make any changes to the variables after

For the first two situations, the warning is annoying. For the third, it is incorrect - we did make changes to the forumlas/variables/calculations, but apparently the Check Forumlas button changes whatever status that warning is based on

I don’t see other question types giving a warning on save unless required information isn’t present. Is this one necessary?

summary: SakaiAccount component makes duplicate API calls to /api/users/{userId}/profile on initialization
description:
The SakaiAccount LIT web component makes duplicate API calls to /api/users/{userId}/profile when it initializes. This occurs because _loadUser() is called in both connectedCallback() at line 54 and attributeChangedCallback() at line 62 when the user-id attribute is set. Both callbacks fire during component initialization, resulting in two identical network requests.

h2. Fix

Add a guard in connectedCallback() to only call _loadUser() if userId exists. This ensures _loadUser() only fires once via attributeChangedCallback when the user-id attribute is set.

h2. File Location

webcomponents/tool/src/main/frontend/packages/sakai-account/src/SakaiAccount.js

summary: Fill in the Blank questions custom markers doesn't allow forward slash
description:
This appears to work in 25. 

[https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-34477|https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-34477|smart-link] added a custom marker field for the fill-in questions that allow different characters to be used to mark the correct answer, so curly braces can be used in the question text. 

The instructions for the custom field give the reserved characters as “ ' . , & < > | * and space. 
For a test, I was attempting to use \ and / as the custom markers. The backslash \ was accepted with another character, the forward slash is not. 

Including the forward slash / gives an error: Please make sure your answer markers match and answers must contain at least one non-space character. 

Since the forward slash is accepted on 25, it should remain functional on 26. If this isn’t possible, then it should be included in the reserved characters and give an error that is more accurate.

summary: SakaiNotifications component fetches notifications on every page load
description:
The SakaiNotifications component fetches /api/users/me/notifications on every page load, even if notifications were just fetched seconds ago on a previous page. This creates unnecessary network traffic and server load.

h2. Solution

Implement localStorage caching with 5-minute TTL:

* Check cache before fetching
* Store notifications with timestamp
* Invalidate cache when notifications are cleared/marked as viewed
* Show cache age in console for debugging

This way, if a user navigates between pages within 5 minutes, cached notifications are used instead of making redundant API calls.

h2. File Location

webcomponents/tool/src/main/frontend/packages/sakai-notifications/src/SakaiNotifications.js

summary: Custom CSS selection lost when sites are created from a template
description:
{noformat}  - Problem: Sites created from a template lose the Lessons “Custom CSS” selection. The CSS file is copied to Resources (LB-CSS) but the page’s cssSheet field no longer points to the copied file.
  - Steps to Reproduce:
      1. In a template site, upload a CSS to Resources > LB-CSS and select it in Lessons > Settings.
      2. Create a new site from that template (manual or bulk).
      3. Open the Lessons page in the new site.
  - Expected: The selected custom CSS remains selected and applied.
  - Actual: The CSS selection is unset or falls back to default while the file exists in Resources.
  - Diagnosis: During transferCopyEntities/merge, Lessons only rewrote the siteId segment in cssSheet and didn’t use the traversal map. If Resources renamed the file (e.g., my.css → my-1.css) or if the path used /content/… instead of /group/…, the stored cssSheet no longer matched the new resource.
      - Proposed Fix: Remap page cssSheet using the traversal map and normalize /content vs /group IDs.
          - Files changed: lessonbuilder/tool/src/java/org/sakaiproject/lessonbuildertool/service/LessonBuilderEntityProducer.java:1686, 2191
      - Risk: Low; metadata-only update to page records.{noformat}

summary: Remove genericdao library entirely from Sakai
description:
h2. Overview

Remove the legacy {{genericdao}} helper library from Sakai in favor of standard Spring + Hibernate/JPA patterns available in modern Java.

h2. Why Remove genericdao

* *Maintainability*: {{genericdao}} re-implements DAO patterns that Spring and Hibernate/JPA already solve better with clearer APIs and less bespoke code
* *Modern Java*: The library predates Java 8 streams, JPA Criteria, and stronger generics. Using standard APIs simplifies onboarding and reduces technical debt
* *Tooling/Performance*: First-class Hibernate/JPA integration enables better diagnostics (SQL logs, stats), standard transaction management, and easier caching
* *Risk Reduction*: Fewer custom abstractions lowers the surface area for subtle ClassLoader and proxy issues

h2. Migration Approach

# Define explicit repositories/DAOs per aggregate with clear domain methods (no generic search DSL)
# Implement with Hibernate SessionFactory or JPA EntityManager
# Use {{[user]}} annotations on services
# Remove {{genericdao}} dependencies from module POMs

h2. Tools Requiring Migration

* Polls (POC already completed)
* Hierarchy
* EntityBroker
* Signup
* RSF

h2. Reference

See {{docs/genericdao-migration.md}} for detailed migration guide and Polls POC examples.

summary: Merge new Tags service with existing Unicon Tags
description:
The Tags Service was originally created by Unicon and seemed to have a much different purpose in mind than the more recent S2U work on the Tags Service. For example, Samigo Tags are enabled by a whole different set of sakai.properties than the newer Tags for Assignments and Messages. 

The T&L/UX group reviewed the tag functionality in several tools, and determined that they currently exist within tool silos, with the inability to manage tags centrally as an admin. The S2U work seems to primarily be focused on using tags within specific tools in sites for sorting purposes. However, the Unicon tag work seemed to have a more global perspective where tags could be created and managed at the system level and could be used in any tools that support tags (even though Samigo was the only tool to support tags until recently). T&L/UX likes the global approach because it can facilitate the tracking of competencies and learning objectives, something which is currently lacking in the available Sakai analytics.

We would like to see the Tags service be merged so that it can enable sorting within tools, but also work globally and with the tool silos removed. Essentially, we want admins to be able to manage tags for the system, as well as individual instructors, and we would like any tags created in the system to be available to all tools that use tags. 

The key functionality we would like to see:

* Tags Service should be in Admin Workspace by default

* Tag Collection creation/editing should be available to admins in Admin Workspace as well as instructors within sites they own

* Administratively created tags should  display / be available for selection in individual sites, but not editable by instructors
* Instructor-created tags and collections should only be available within the site where they were created
* All tools which use tags should be able to select from any existing tags and collections within the site and shared globally from Admin Workspace



For reference, here are the original Jiras regarding tags:

* *Origial Tags Jira:*  [https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-32083|https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-32083|smart-link]  - link new feature requests to this Jira

* Jira from EDF to filter assignments: [https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/S2U-32|https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/S2U-32|smart-link]

summary: Bootstrap 5.2: form-check-input checkboxes render incorrectly without form-check wrapper
description:
h3. Summary
After the Bootstrap 5.2 upgrade, several checkboxes and switches that use {{.form-check-input}} are no longer styled correctly. The markup is still using {{.form-group}} wrappers (or inline {{<label>}} wrappers) instead of the Bootstrap 5.2 {{.form-check}} structure, so the inputs lose their expected padding and alignment.

h3. Steps to Reproduce

h1. Log in to Sakai trunk (commit a49151634f03fe856bf1f096433ff6f6f6637b33) as a user with access to the Plus tool.

h1. Go to _Plus > Tenants_ and open an existing tenant.

h1. Scroll to the _Trust email_ and _Verbose_ toggles.

h1. Note that the checkbox/switch inputs are flush against the container edge and no longer align with their labels.

h3. Expected Behaviour
Checkboxes and switches that use Bootstrap 5.2 classes should render with the spacing, alignment, and focus states provided by the {{.form-check}} component.

h3. Actual Behaviour
Inputs with the {{.form-check-input}} class appear unstyled or misaligned because the surrounding markup still uses legacy {{.form-group}} containers or wraps the input directly in a {{<label>}}. Without the {{.form-check}} wrapper and {{.form-check-label}}, the Bootstrap 5.2 CSS no longer applies the positioning offsets.

h3. Notes

* Example markup in {{plus/tool/src/main/webapp/WEB-INF/templates/form.html}} uses {{<div class="form-group form-switch">}} instead of {{<div class="form-check form-switch">}}.
* Similar patterns exist in {{site-manage/site-group-manager}} templates, {{lessonbuilder}} checklist templates, and other areas that rely on {{.form-check-input}}.
* Bootstrap 5.2 relies on the {{.form-check}} wrapper to set {{position: relative}} and to add the left padding spacing for {{.form-check-input}}.

h3. Environment

* Sakai trunk, Bootstrap 5.2
* Observed in Chrome 124 on macOS Sonoma

h3. Proposed Fix
Audit usage of {{.form-check-input}} across the codebase and update the surrounding markup to match the Bootstrap 5.2 examples, i.e. wrap inputs in {{.form-check}} (and {{.form-switch}} for toggles) and use {{.form-check-label}} for the associated labels. This will restore the expected spacing and visual treatment.

summary: Remove the remnants of the long deprecated LinkTool from LTI
description:
Back in 2005, before LTI was widespread, Chuck Hedrick of Rutgers developed a tool that was called {{LinkTool}}.  It solved the use case of launching an external tool and sharing user information with that tool.  The problem is that it solved problems using session sharing which was dangerous.  Since LTI came along about the same time, there was little use of LinkTool outside of Rutgers and it was effectively deprecated in 2005.  In order to help folks make

Note that the External LTI 1.1 Tool only supports LTI 1.1 and pre-dates the modern External Tools feature in the admin tool. summary: Remove the long deprecated "paste XML" feature from the LTI 1.1 "External Tool"

When a stealthed tool is deployed to a site, (26 & 25), instructions are needed for the admin on the Manual Tool Deploy page and possibly on the Tool Links page, unless there is a better way to handle this.

If the admin adds a stealthed tool to a site, it then becomes available for the instructor to add to the navigation, Lessons, etc, wherever the admin made the placement available. In the example, the tool is added to the navigation, so when the instructor goes to site info > manage tools, they will see the stealthed tool and can add it to the navigation.

If the admin decides later to remove the site from the stealthed tool, the admin can click on the # under the Deployment column for that tool on the External Tools page.

summary: Signup permissions API blocks instructor updates in web component UI
description:
Summary: Site maintainers using the web component permissions UI for Signup receive a 403 when saving because the Signup service registers its permissions without marking them user-mutable.

Impact: Non-superuser instructors cannot adjust Signup permissions after the REST-based workflow was introduced; the legacy helper masked the issue so it went unnoticed until the web component was adopted.

Reproduction:

# Log in as an instructor (maintain role) and open Signup in a site that uses the SakaiPermissions web component.
# Change any permission toggle and click Save.
# Observe the network response: POST /api/sites/{siteId}/permissions returns 403 Forbidden and the UI shows a generic failure banner.

Root cause: Signup registers its permissions with functionManager.registerFunction(permission) (userMutable = false). The REST controller only allows non-superusers to mutate functions that were registered as user-mutable, so every write attempt is rejected.

Fix: Register all Signup permissions with userMutable = true and improve logging/UI messaging so the 403 surfaces meaningful information.

summary: Safe Exam Browser - Issues in timed assessments
description:
After some time with Safe Exam Browser in our production environment, we have had several issues with timed assessments. These issues only happens with SEB, not in regular assessments without kiosk mode.

We don't have a deterministic test plan to reproduce this. It has happened with a lot of different settings (with or without late submission date, with a one page assessment and with navigation between questions...). The only important setting is that the assessment must be timed and must have a good amount of time. Not sure if it matters but we have the server autosave feature running (samigo.autoSave.repeat.milliseconds=60000).

The issues happen when the time is near to finish, i.e. in a 42 minutes assessment everything seems to work well until the last 2-3 minutes.

The issues that we have experienced include:

* The "Save" and "Submit" buttons are unresponsive, so it’s not possible to finish and exit SEB.
* Some radio buttons are resetted after clicking on "Save".
* After time runs out, autosubmission of test is not inmediate and is done 1-2 minutes later.
* After time runs out, timer shows random values for a while before autosubmitting. These values change and sometimes they are negative values.

Autosubmit works well AFAIK and answers aren't lost but these issues cause anxiety and fear in students and teachers.

summary: Date-picker rolls over to next month for months with fewer than 31 days
description:
When selecting, in Samigo, a available or due date in a month with fewer than 31 days, the system automatically changes the month to the following one after saving.

For example, if the user selects February 10, it is saved or displayed as March 10 instead.

The issue occurs with the date-picker when configuring dates in February, April, June, September, and November (months with fewer than 31 days). This behavior has been observed in forums, test & quizzes, gradebook and lessons, while assignments appear to behave correctly. Maybe more tools.

summary: Add information text on screen for LTI "Transfer" option
description:
The purpose for the new “Transfer” option in the Admin External Tools UI is not obvious to users. The use case is very rare. Lets say you have an LTI 1.1 tool for MyMathLab with tons of links and content items scattered across many sites and you need to install an LTI 1.3 MyMathlab tool and you want *all* those links to the LTI 1.1 Pearson tool to be switched to the LTI 1.3 tool. The Transfer tool is intended to update all those links and save the admin a lot of work. However, since the links remain titled as they were originally in each of the affected sites, it does not really work for any other scenario.

We would like to add some informational text to the UI to explain the intended use for this feature, so that admins are not confused by it or attempt to use it for the wrong thing. We would like the message to read: “The Transfer option is meant to update all of the existing tool links from one tool to another tool. However, the tool link title is not changed. This is usually done when an existing LTI tool with many tool links is being replaced with a newer version of the same tool.”

summary: Tests & Quizzes / Gradebook : Cancel Question allows unequal points possible items in Keep/Drop category
description:
When using Keep (or Drop) Highest/Lowest all items in the category must have the same point total (unless the equal weighting option is selected - since that option’s purpose is to account for category items with differing point totals). 


By using the new Cancel Question feature, a category item that does match its cohort’s points possible can be triggered.

Also, I contend this should be considered a distortion of the gradebook category involved.  Ex. (as seen via executing the test plan):  

Cancelling question 1 in Quiz 1 leads to a score of 80% ( 1/2 + 3/3 = 4/5). When using Keep/Drop items must maintain equal points possible. So without errantly allowing the cancellations of the question the score would have been 2/3 for Quiz 1 and 3/3 for Quiz 2 for a category score of 83.33% or if the question was answered wrong 1/3 for Quiz 1 and 3/3 for Quiz 2 = 66.66%

summary: Support markdown in lessons
description:
It would be nice to have support for markdown format in lessons tool.

I guess [https://github.com/[user]/commonmark-java|https://github.com/[user]/commonmark-java|smart-link]  could be used for implementing such a feature.

Currently we have lectors hosting markdown in GitHub Pages and embedding them into Sakai. This is a creative way to be able to use that common format, but comes with the burden of external hosting the content.

Thus it would be favorable to have this support natively in sakai.

summary: Samigo: Duplicated group quizzes with unexpected release setting
description:
The fix introduced by [https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-51762|https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-51762|smart-link] resolves one regression (vis-a-vis Sakai 23 & 22) where a duplicate for an assessment released to groups will not display in the Assessments tab. Due to that fix, the duplicated assessment now displays. However, for assessments released to groups, the duplicated assessment in Sakai 23/22 would display a helpful error message in the For column, alerting the instructor that settings would need to be adjusted for it to be released:

*Expected error message in For column:* “Students are not able to take this assessment because the groups it was released to have been deleted. You must publish a new copy of this assessment.”

Furthermore, the duplicate’s release to ‘Entire Site’ is unexpected (or at least not intuitive). The current behavior in Sakai 26/25 is especially problematic for course sites where two (or more) distinct groups represent different lecture meeting times (e.g., MWF vs Tues. & Thurs.) and thus different deadlines for assessments, assignments, etc. For such sites, assessments released to ‘Entire site’ should never (or only rarely) occur.

summary: Lessons: Extraneous SimplePageItem created for page
description:
This jira intends to prevent cases which yield warnings in catalina.out like the following:

{{07-Oct-2025 11:08:54.964 WARN [ajp-nio-0:0:0:0:0:0:0:1-8009-exec-5] o.s.l.m.}}*SimplePageToolDaoImpl*{{.lambda$}}*findTopLevelPageItem*{{$1 query found more than one SimplePageItem where sakaiId=13750 and type=2}}

The type refers to an item that also represents a page. The sakaiId is also in this case a page ID.

The test plan reliably creates such cases for Sakai 26 and 25.

summary: Assignments: Gradebook category should persist in new assignments (configurable via Sakai property)
description: When editing or creating an assignment, the selected Gradebook category is currently set as the default for the next assignment created (after reverting [https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-51785|https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-51785|smart-link]). It should be possible to configure in sakai.properties ({{gradebookng.category.reset}}) that the selection is reset after each edit.

summary: Assignments: Download All translates some files into Spanish and Catalan
description:
The Download All Submissions option downloads files like timestamp, feedbackText, and comments, among many others. Only these three are translated into Spanish and Catalan. However, the instructions for export and import do not use the translated names, and imports sometimes fail because of this.

Since this feature is not being used in other languages, it should be reverted. If desired, a new Jira can be created to implement it correctly.

summary: Assignments: Job to auto-submit assignments
description:
For Test & Quizzes, there is already a job called Auto Submit Assessments. It is proposed to add a similar job called Auto Submit Assignments.

Currently, assignment drafts are visible, but since they are not actually submitted, certain actions that normally occur upon student submission (such as Turnitin checks or peer review assignments) are never triggered.

It is proposed to add this functionality using the following properties:

{noformat}# Auto Submit assignments feature
# See assignment/docs/auto_submit/README.autoSubmit.txt for instructions.
# DEFAULT: false
# assignment.autoSubmit.enabled=true

# Auto-submit assignments default checkbox option
# DEFAULT: false (checkbox will be unchecked by default)
# assignment.autoSubmit.defaultCheckbox=true

# Enable or disable email notifications for assignments auto submit failures
# DEFAULT: false (no emails will be sent by default)
# assignment.email.autoSubmit.errorNotification.enabled=true

# Set the address to which auto submit assignments failure emails will be sent
# DEFAULT: the current value of the 'mail.support' sakai.property
# DEFAULT: if 'mail.support' is not set, the current value of 'setup.request' sakai.property is used
# DEFAULT: if 'setup.request' is not set, property value falls back to "no-reply@" + serverConfigurationService.getServerName()
# assignment.email.autoSubmit.errorNotification.toAddress=[email]
{noformat}

Students are notified that the assignment will be automatically submitted after the due date.

summary: SCORM: Number of attempts allowed not honored
description:
This will affect 25x once all the SCORM Jiras are merged. SCORM configure has an option to allow unlimited or 1-10 attempts. Setting this to allow only 1 attempt does not work. The student can take the module/quiz multiple times and if the grade is sent to the GB, it updates to the latest score. This would allow a student to keep trying until they get a perfect score.

In the results page, the instructor only sees 1 attempt made even though there were multiple. (When unlimited attempts are made, it does now show for the golf packages the number of attempts.)

The instructor would incorrectly believe that the student only made 1 attempt and got a perfect score.

My student received a 73 on the first attempt and then 100 on the second attempt. The instructor saw only 1 attempt with a perfect score and the GB had a 100.

description:
