Reset the variable inside the first loop each time.

summary: Linked quizzes with prerequisites lose their initial access in T&Q
description:
When an assessment is linked as a quiz in Lessons and it’s configured with prerequisites, some things happen:

* A group with name "Access: <assessment name>" is created for the prerequisite, though teacher doesn't notice this.
* The assessment is changed in Test & Quizzes to be available only for that group, again without teacher knowledge.
* The group contains only the students that have submitted the assessment.
* The teacher goes to the Scores and see only the students that have submitted the assessment. But he wants to grade all the students and he thinks that this is some bug.

Not sure if this is a bug or a feature, but we think that the assessment should remain available to the entire site and all students should be gradable, no matter if they have submitted the test or not.

summary: Resubmission due date in Assignments should be respected
description:
Currently, in Assignments, if you allow resubmissions for an assignment, and select a due date for the resubmissions, the due date is overridden by the Accept Until date for the assignment. T&L/UX discussed this behavior on our call today (Nov 19, 2025) and the group felt that the resubmission due date should be respected. Otherwise, what is the point of having a resubmission date field at all? You could simply select the number of resubmissions allowed and let the overall Accept Until date control the submission window.

The use case that was discussed was as follows. An instructor has an assignment with resubmissions allowed. However, he only wants to accept resubmissions until the resubmission due date. If students miss the resubmission due date, they are not allowed to resubmit. Submissions after the due date, up until the Accept Until date, are marked late and are only allowed for the first submission attempt (not for resubmission attempts).

summary: Resubmission dates in Assignments should be included in the Date Manager
description:
Currently, the Assignments items in Date Manager only display the Open Date, Due Date, and Accept Until Date columns. However, some assignment may allow resubmissions and have a separate Resubmission Due Date specified in the item Settings. These resubmission dates are not visible to be batch updated in Date Manager, which means that they may be missed when instructors update their sites for a new term. 

The T&L/UX group discussed this issue, and the consensus was that we would like an additional column for Resubmission Due Date added to the Assignments section of the Date Manager. Similarly to Tests & Quizzes, if resubmissions are not allowed, then the Resubmission Due Date field would be disabled. However, if resubmissions are allowed, then the Resubmission Due Date would be populated into that field.

Note: This is for resubmissions allowed at the assignment level (not individual resubmissions that are set on a per-student basis during grading).

See proposed mockup below:

summary: "What if" calculator for grades
description:
This feature request was suggested by a student at a Sakai institution.

It would be a nice enhancement to have a “what if” calculator for grades, so that the student could enter the desired/anticipated grade for future gradebook items and see what the effect would be on their course average. This would help them determine the minimum grade they need to make on specific items to receive a particular letter grade in the course. 

While students can certainly do this manually by plugging in their scores and calculating their anticipated average based on the overall grading formula for the course, it would be much easier to accomplish this task if there were an online UI that automatically sets up the calculation for them based on the course gradebook.

description:

summary: New option in Gradebook to "set score for empty cells" on assessments and assignments
description:
Currently, when you have an assignment or assessment being sent to the gradebook the item in the gradebook is locked. Instructors can add comments but are unable to enter a score via the gradebook - they must go to the Assignments or Tests & Quizzes tool to enter or modify scores. This presents a problem if the instructor needs to assign a zero grade for an item that has been selectively released.

Consider the following scenario: The assignment or assessment is selectively released to students via Lessons. Lessons uses “access” groups to release items, so students are only added to the group once they complete the access requirement. When an instructor goes into the grading interface of the tool (both Assignments and Tests & Quizzes) they only see the members of the group to which the item has been released - in this case, it is the “access” group created by Lessons. Students who are not in the access group, i.e. students who have not completed the requirement, are not shown. Therefore, the instructor has no way to enter a zero score for those students who fail to complete the assignment/assessment. The gradebook allows instructors to enter zeros for all ungraded items across the entire gradebook at one time, but there is no way to do this per-gradebook item for locked items. 

T&L/UX would like to propose that we add the option to “Set score for empty cells” for locked items, similar to the way that you can do this for gradebook-created items.

See mockups below: 

!gb-set-scores-quiz.png|width=671,alt="gb-set-scores-quiz.png"!

!gb-set-scores-assignment.png|width=671,alt="gb-set-scores-assignment.png"!

summary: New option to view non-group members in Assignment submissions screen
description:
In the related Jira [https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-52213|https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-52213|smart-link]  T&L/UX proposed a new feature to set scores for empty cells on locked assignment items in the gradebook. The rationale for this feature request to view non-group members is the same as the one for the gradebook option. Instructors are unable to enter zero scores for students who have not completed assignments selectively released in Lessons, since they are not part of the “access” group and do not appear in the submission list. In this case, the feature is being requested within the Assignments grading UI, since that it the most likely place instructors will go to look for such a feature, particularly if they are accustomed to entering all scores for assignments via the Assignments tool.

T&L/UX would like to propose the following changes to the View drop-down menu in the assignment submission screen:

# Add a “Released Sections/Groups” option to promote consistency with Tests & Quizzes view options. This should be the default display option, which is essentially the same view of released-group-members-only which is the current view.
# Modify the “Entire site” option (which doesn’t actually seem to display the entire site now) to say “Entire site (including Non-members of Released Sections/Groups)” and ensure that it actually does display all enrolled site participants, regardless of group. This would allow instructors to view students who have not completed the Lessons “access” group requirement and enter zero scores for them as needed.

See mockup below:

summary: Update unboundid-ldapsdk 7.0.4
description:
h1. UnboundID LDAP SDK for Java 7.0.4

[*Latest*|https://github.com/[user]/ldapsdk/releases/latest]

[dirmgr|https://github.com/[user]] released this 2 days ago

· [1 commit |https://github.com/[user]/ldapsdk/compare/7.0.4...master]to master since this release

[7.0.4|https://github.com/[user]/ldapsdk/tree/7.0.4]

{{2b16a37}}

We have just released version 7.0.4 of the [+UnboundID LDAP SDK for Java+|https://github.com/[user]/ldapsdk]. It is available for download from [+GitHub+|https://github.com/[user]/ldapsdk/releases] and [+SourceForge+|https://sourceforge.net/projects/ldap-sdk/files/], and it is available in the [+Maven Central Repository+|https://central.sonatype.com/artifact/com.unboundid/unboundid-ldapsdk/7.0.4]. You can find the release notes for this release (and all previous versions) at [https://docs.ldap.com/ldap-sdk/docs/release-notes.html|https://docs.ldap.com/ldap-sdk/docs/release-notes.html|smart-link] , but here’s a summary of the changes:

* We added a “discard results” search result listener that can be used in cases where a search should be performed, but the actual matching entries and references aren’t needed (for example, if you only need to know the number of matching entries).
* We added client-side support for a W3C trace context request control that can be included in requests sent to the latest versions of the Ping Identity Directory Server or ForgeRock Directory Services. This can be used to convey information for use in distributed tracing (e.g., via OpenTelemetry).
* We improved debug logging when adding or removing servers from the blacklist used to temporarily avoid creating connections to a server when using the round robin and fewest connections server set.
* We updated the {{PropertyManager}} class to make it possible to cache property values for faster access with less contention. Caching is disabled by default, although you can enable it by specifying a maximum cache duration. You can also programmatically clear the cache and pre-populate the cache based on currently defined system properties and environment variables.
* We improved performance and reduced contention when retrieving the values of environment variables from the JVM process.
* We updated the documentation to include the latest revisions of draft-bouchez-scram-mcf and draft-codere-ldapsyntax in the set of LDAP-related specifications.

summary: Syllabus: sanitizer warning blocks publish after AntiSamy strips align attribute
description:
When instructors paste HTML with disallowed attributes into a new syllabus item, AntiSamy cleans the markup but the JSF flow treats the warning as a blocking validation error. The page reloads and nothing is saved even though the content has already been sanitized. * Example: adding a new item with

Sam Test

1

shows a red error banner and Publish just reloads the page without saving. The align attribute is removed, but the item is never persisted. * Expected: AntiSamy should sanitize quietly and proceed with save/publish so instructors aren’t blocked or shown scary HTML errors. * Fix implemented: treat AntiSamy warnings as informational; keep the sanitized content and continue the JSF flow instead of setting alertMessage/returning to edit. Log the sanitizer notes for admins.

summary: Changes in Section Info options are not well synchronized by Ignite between servers.

description:
[ANNOUNCEMENT] HttpComponents Core 5.4 GA released
The Apache HttpComponents project is pleased to announce 5.4 GA release
of HttpComponents Core.

This is the first GA release in the 5.4 release series that improves
HTTP/2 protocol support by ensuring conformance to the latest HTTP
specification (RFC 9113) and adds support for Unix domain sockets.

Notable changes and features included in the 5.4 series:

* Experimental OFFLOCK (lock-free) connection pool.
* Conformance to RFC 9218 (Extensible Prioritization Scheme for HTTP).
* Improved conformance to RFC 9113 (Hypertext Transfer Protocol Version
2).
* Five-second TCP keep-alive enabled by default.
* Unix domain socket support by the classic and async transports.
* Redesign of classic over async API bridge.
* Improved URI encoding per RFC 3986.
* QUERY method support.
* Improved idle connection validation in the async transport.

summary: Date Manager: if the top of the page is not visible when the instructor clicks to save changes, they never see the success/failure message
description:
The Date Manager does display success/failure messages when updating, but if the instructor is updating something and the top of the page does not display, when the enter modified dates and click Save Changes, they do not see the success message because the focus does not go to the top of the page after submitting changes.

If there is a failure, the message does display for that date field, but the message at the top of the page does not display because the focus is on the failed date field.

With a failure it makes sense that the focus remains on the failed date field since there is a message indicating the problem, but with a success message, it is only displayed for a few seconds and the instructor never sees it if the top of the page is not displayed and receiving focus.

With the failure there is an issue if the instructor is updating several items and the “failed” date is not the one that the instructor worked with last. See [https://drive.google.com/file/d/1pFcaxm78SLSm5gy6wuNXQLNnv9MJpRq1/view?usp=sharing|https://drive.google.com/file/d/1pFcaxm78SLSm5gy6wuNXQLNnv9MJpRq1/view?usp=sharing|smart-link]

summary: Assignments PeerReview: Schedule a retry after detecting an error in reviewer allocation

The job responsible for allocating reviewers for peer-review assignments runs when the review period opens. We have detected that, in some cases, the reviewer allocation is not performed. In addition, this process currently has very limited logging, which is insufficient to detect malfunctions.

summary: LTI local-network-access issue with Chrome 142 and iframes
description:
Chrome 142 turned on restrictions about public servers accessing things on the local network: [New permission prompt for Local Network Access  |  Blog  |  Chrome for Developers|https://developer.chrome.com/blog/local-network-access]

This is fixed by fixing support for the already-existing {{browser.feature.allow}} property in the Sakai LTI iframe web component and add “local-network-access *” to the default in the kernel default properties.

Sites that have already customized {{browser.feature.allow }}in sakai.properties should add: {{browser.feature.allow.6=local-network-access *}} and update their {{browser.feature.allow.count}} accordingly.

The following is from Moodle addressing this issue:

Copied from [https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-87258|https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-87258|smart-link] 

For use this broke the LTI for Turn It In, when Launch container = Embed. This shouldn’t be specific to Turn It In though, any embedded LTI that authenticates with a Moodle server with a private IP address will fail on Chrome 142 and later. The iframe loads these URLs:

# {{https://moodle-server/mod/lti/launch.php?id=4&triggerview=0}}
# {{https://lti.int.turnitin.com/oidc/login/xxx}}
# {{https://moodle-server/mod/lti/auth.php}} (fails with LocalNetworkAccessPermissionDenied)

Our {{moodle-server}} has split-horizon DNS, on campus users get a 10.x.x.x IP, Internet users get a public IP. [+lti.int.turnitin.com+|http://lti.int.turnitin.com/] has public IPs.

I added “local-network-access *” in mod/lti/view.php where it builds the <iframe allow="">attribute. Now Chrome prompts for local network access permissions and then loads the LTI. Other LTIs that don’t redirect back don’t prompt for local network access.

It feels Chrome is wrong, but the sane fix is in Moodle.  And the only fix is in Moodle code. Or changing our network.

summary: Calendar: only allow items to be edited through the Calendar that were actually created in the Calendar

summary: Date Manager > Gradebook: Associated Internal gradebook items allow editing under Date Manager > Gradebook, but include note about not syncing with tool
description:
This was discussed on the Core call and the T&L meeting. If an item is created in the Gradebook, then another tool is associated (linked) with that GB item, that item appears in the Date Manager twice. Once in the tool section, and again in the Gradebook section.

!image-20260122-160156.png|width=671,alt="image-20260122-160156.png"!

These items associated with a GB item have open/close/due dates in the tool itself and display under the Date Manager > tool with their dates. It would cause confusion if the instructor were to add a due date to the GB item that does not match the tool date. However, upon discussion in T&L, it was pointed out that some instructors prefer to add dates in either the GB or the Tool for specific use cases.

We did not want to disrupt the current workflow by changing the behavior and forcing it to sync. So instead, we would like to add a note about the dates in the GB section to inform users that changing the date in the GB section is only informational and will not affect the actual tool dates or access: "Changing the date in the Gradebook section will only affect the date displayed in the Gradebook."

We also thought that adding some text noting the linked/associated items would further clarify the relationship for items listed more than once.

See mockup:

Tools in Sakai have their own search textboxes and are very inconsistent. This is an umbrella Jira to bring consistency between all the tools and their search textboxes.

The preferred search textbox:

!image-20260123-160313.png|width=263,alt="image-20260123-160313.png"!

* The x in the textbox appears after a user starts to enter text
* As the user starts to enter text, results will start filtering
* If the user hits the ‘Enter’ key, the textbox is *not* cleared, but continues to show filtered results
* When the user clicks the ‘x’, the textbox is cleared and all results will be listed

Document with tools checked: [https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1zLL_UlZ8RjVurXSTyr9AqXB5usvlaAdU3BgKDTFsY50/edit?usp=sharing|https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1zLL_UlZ8RjVurXSTyr9AqXB5usvlaAdU3BgKDTFsY50/edit?usp=sharing|smart-link]

summary: Samigo bulk delete of many assessments can destabilize node (Hibernate/OpenSearch storm)
description:
Bulk deleting a large number of Samigo assessments (reproduced with ~200 selected at once) can overwhelm request-thread and backend processing, leading to node instability and cluster-side failures.

  In production, a single bulk delete triggered:

* HikariCP thread starvation / clock leap warnings
* Long JVM pause warnings (~22 seconds)
* Ignite SYSTEM_WORKER_BLOCKED critical failure in TcpCommunicationSpi
* Discovery/communication failures (Broken pipe) and node-failure handling

  Expected behavior:
  Bulk delete should complete without destabilizing the JVM or cluster services, and should avoid heavy per-assessment/per-item synchronous work in the request path.

  Actual behavior:
  Delete processing cascades into expensive operations (ORM-heavy delete path + synchronous side effects such as search unindex/event fan-out), causing pause amplification and communication thread blockage severe enough to destabilize the instance.

summary: Discussions: Anonymous posting note is misleading about identity visibility when “Reveal identities” is unchecked
description:
In Discussions topic settings, enabling Allow anonymous postings shows helper text that implies owner-level users can identify anonymous authors by default.
  However, in actual behavior, identities remain hidden for all users (including admins/instructors) unless Reveal identities to roles with the "Identify Anonymous Authors" permission is also checked.

  This creates admin/instructor confusion and support noise, because the first checkbox note suggests the second checkbox is optional for owners when it is not.

  *Actual result*
  With Allow anonymous postings checked and Reveal identities... unchecked, everyone sees anonymous IDs only.

  *Expected result*
  UI text should clearly state that identities are revealed only when Reveal identities... is enabled, and then only for users with Identify Anonymous Authors permission (Owner includes this by default unless
  permissions were customized).

summary: copyAllAssessments triggers pathological Hibernate auto-flush/cascade loop and can run for hours
description:
When importing Tests & Quizzes (Samigo) during Site Import, the import thread can appear to never finish while consuming high CPU.

  Observed behavior:

* Import thread remains RUNNABLE for long periods.
* CPU time continuously increases.
* Thread dumps show repeated Hibernate flush/cascade traversal, including:
** SessionImpl.persistOnFlush
** Cascade.cascade*
** AbstractPersistentCollection.getOrphans
** call path through:
*** SiteManageServiceImpl.transferCopyEntities
*** AssessmentEntityProducer.transferCopyEntities
*** AssessmentFacadeQueries.copyAllAssessments
*** AuthzQueriesFacade.getAuthorizationByFunctionAndQualifier

  *Root cause:*

* In AssessmentFacadeQueries.copyAllAssessments, deep copied assessment graphs are saveOrUpdate’d, then group-release authz is queried (getReleaseToGroups) inside the same transaction loop.
* Those read queries trigger Hibernate auto-flush, which repeatedly cascades/dirty-checks large Samigo object graphs (sections/items/itemText/answers/attachments/tags), causing extreme slowdown.

summary: Messages Search
description:
T&L/UX discussed the look and feel of Search across tools and we would like more consistency across tools. (Currently, it is very inconsistent.) However, the Search in Messages is a little different from other tools because it also includes an Advanced Search option.

Ideally, we would like Search in Messages to look and work more like the Search in Gmail. This is very similar to the preferred Search defined for other Sakai tools (see SAK-52292 for more details), but also incorporates the functionality of Advanced Search without having a separate button and dated/clunky interface for the advanced search options. 

I’m including screenshots below from Gmail. We would like Sakai Messages Search to follow that model. 

The search box does not have separate Search or Advanced Search buttons. 

!search-box-gmail-empty.png|width=671,alt="search-box-gmail-empty.png"!

Users can begin typing and will see results as they type. Or, they can hit Enter to see the complete search results below.

If the user wants to filter the search results, they can either select the “filter” icon located in the right corner of the Search text field, or enter the filter term followed by a colon in the search field.

Selecting the filter icon displays a list of filter items available for the user, as shown below:

!search-box-gmail-filters.png|width=671,alt="search-box-gmail-filters.png"!

Or, the user can enter the filter term followed by a colon in the text field and then select Enter to search, as shown below:

!search-box-gmail-textpluscolon.png|width=671,alt="search-box-gmail-textpluscolon.png"!

The T&L/UX group thinks that modeling the Search in Messages after Gmail would be a much more modern and clean approach.

summary: Samigo backfill failing due to JPA positional parameter queries
description:
Samigo item hash backfill job could fail due to JPA/Hibernate positional parameter handling in the underlying queries. Updated the backfill implementation to avoid positional-parameter query issues by switching to Criteria-based queries and using {{SessionFactory.getCurrentSession()}} under Spring-managed transactions. {{ItemHashUtilTransactionTemplate}}

Also updated Spring wiring to inject the additional dependencies and to run each batch in its own *REQUIRES_NEW* transaction for safer, more reliable long-running backfills.

summary: Update Apache HttpComponents Core 5.4.1 GA
description:
{noformat}Release 5.4.1
------------------

This maintenance release fixes a latency regression in the async transport
caused by TCP_NODELAY failing to be set. Several other bugs have also been
fixed affecting connection management, HTTP/2 exception handling and
propagation, and so forth.


Change Log
-------------------

* Regression: Ensure TCP-specific socket options are set correctly in the async
  transport.
  Contributed by Ryan Schmitt <rschmitt at apache.org>

* Bug fix: Prevent integer overflow in LaxConnPool so that negative numbers are
  not reported in the thread pool statistics.
  Contributed by Ryan Schmitt <rschmitt at apache.org>

* Bug fix: Loop over and close expired connections in LaxConnPool instead of
  returning them.
  Contributed by Ryan Schmitt <rschmitt at apache.org>

* Bug fix: Respect the PoolReusePolicy.FIFO in StrictConnPool.
  Contributed by Ryan Schmitt <rschmitt at apache.org>

* Bug fix: Corrected exception propagation in protocol negotiators' exception
  handling code.
  Contributed by Oleg Kalnichevski <olegk at apache.org>

* Bug fix: Fix SOCKS handshake to fail on EOF. (#604)
  Contributed by Arturo Bernal <abernal at apache.org>

* Bug fix: Handle CancelledKeyException thrown by abort method of the H2 stream.
  Contributed by Oleg Kalnichevski <olegk at apache.org>

* Bug fix: Fix race condition in ComplexCancellable.
  Contributed by Ryan Schmitt <rschmitt at apache.org>

* Bug fix: In MonitoringResponseOutOfOrderStrategy, always perform a blocking
  read to check for data.
  Contributed by Ryan Schmitt <rschmitt at apache.org>

* Bug fix: Corrected exception propagation to individual H2 streams in case of
  an unexpected error with the H2 connection.
  Contributed by Oleg Kalnichevski <olegk at apache.org>

* Regression: Restored SocketSupport and marked it deprecated.
  Contributed by Oleg Kalnichevski <olegk at apache.org>
{noformat}

summary: Resize SAKAI.SAKAI_SITE.TITLE to 255 characters
description:
Most common systems (Moodle, Canvas, Blackboard) as well as our custom data-leading system do use a length of 255 charachters when limiting textual data in databases, which does conflict with the current limit of 99 characters for *sakai.sakai_site.TITLE* field.

We are tempted to customize it, by altering the length of the database field *sakai.sakai_site.TITLE*, but are worried to break things else-where.

Our custom approach of simply truncating incoming title-strings leads to important text being cut-off at the end. Imposing that historical limit of 99 characters onto our data-leading system is also not possible.

So, if there isn’t a good reason to keep that limit, it would be super-cool to make that field 255 characters. 🙂

summary: LTI Convert most calls to LTIService to return and use beans instead of maps
description:
We are in the middle of migrating from Map-based APIs to Bean-based APIs in Sakai’s LTI.  This step continued that process - so  far we already did the following:

[https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-51970|https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-51970|smart-link] 

[https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-52045|https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-52045|smart-link] 

Our next step is to flip bean covers and map implementations in SakaiLTIUtil to be  map covers and bean implementations.  The lays the ground work for eventually removing support for Maps.

After this is complete, we will move on to beanifying the UI bits and then the persistance bits.

summary: Upgrade OpenSearch to 2.19.4
description:
Upgrade OpenSearch from 2.16.0 to 2.19.4 (currently latest 2.x version) Lucene updated to 9.12.3
[https://github.com/[user]/opensearch-build/tree/main/release-notes|https://github.com/[user]/opensearch-build/tree/main/release-notes|smart-link] 

OpenSearch 2.19 includes a number of updates that help you build machine learning (ML)-powered applications, increase performance and stability, and improve the way you and your teams collaborate using OpenSearch.

h4. NEW AND UPDATED FEATURES

* OpenSearch Flow helps developers build ML-powered applications, including generative AI applications, more quickly using OpenSearch Dashboards. Custom flows can be composed to support a range of use cases, such as retrieval-augmented generation and vector search applications.
* Binary vector functionality offers an efficient alternative to FP32 vectors, delivering a more than 90% reduction in memory and storage requirements while maintaining performance. This release adds support for Lucene binary vectors, complementing existing Faiss engine binary vector support.
* Cosine similarity support in the Faiss engine for k-NN and radial search eliminates the need for manual data normalization, offering benefits for use cases such as recommendation systems, fraud detection, and content-based search applications.
* Enhanced hybrid search introduces the {{pagination_depth }}parameter for improved management of large result sets.
* Reciprocal rank fusion provides an alternative approach to result combination that uses the positions or ranks of the documents rather than relying on their scores.
* The new {{hybrid_score_explanation}} processor offers debugging and troubleshooting capabilities for hybrid search operations, offering insights into score normalization and combination processes for search responses.
* A new version of the Faiss library adds advanced AVX-512 Single Instruction Multiple Data (SIMD) instructions for newer-generation processors, available on public clouds such as AWS for c/m/r 7i or newer instances. These SIMD instructions improve the query performance of binary vectors.
* The expanding library of search pipeline processors can make it challenging to track data through processors. A {{verbose_pipeline}} parameter for search pipelines provides a new tool for visualizing the flow of data across these processors, supporting troubleshooting, optimizing pipeline configurations, and providing transparency for search requests and responses.
* ML inference search request extensions allow you to pass additional input fields during search queries, making search requests more adaptable to different ML models and enhancing prediction capabilities during search operations.
* Feature-level anomaly detection now enables precise configuration of spike or dip detection for individual metrics, providing more targeted monitoring of specific data patterns across system resources.
* A new structured index architecture for anomaly detection results transforms values such as entity values and arrays into flattened formats, improving dashboard visualizations and query efficiency.
* Query insights dashboards introduces a new interface for monitoring and analyzing top N queries, with visualizations for historical data integration, detailed drill-down analysis, and streamlined retention management with configurable data expiration.
* A new mechanism used by plugins to access metadata simplifies system index access, offering stronger security controls for privileged operations.
* New concurrency optimizations enable OpenSearch to download graph files in parallel so that they are ready to be loaded into the native memory cache. This enhances performance for remote-backed storage and searchable snapshot workloads, where the data is not readily available on disk.
* Filter performance is improved with the addition of a simple check in the {{searchLeaf}} query method that identifies whether the filters match all of the doc IDs in the segment. If confirmed, OpenSearch will proceed directly with ANN search and avoid unnecessary steps.
* Script scoring for k-NN binary vectors in Hamming space is optimized by eliminating unnecessary type conversions between {{byte}} and {{float}} arrays.
* Further performance optimizations include constant-time privilege evaluation and cost-based bitmap filtering selection, delivering improvements in query efficiency and cost.
* Users are no longer able to specify both the model ID and dimension in an index creation request. When the model ID is provided, k-NN search will refer to the dimension from the training index instead of the user-defined dimension in the mapping request body.
* The {{fields}} parameter is now supported for searches on knn_vector fields so that users will no longer experience failures when running searches using the {{fields}} parameter on indexes with a knn_vector field.
* A fix to the {{rescore}} parameter enables users to disable the rescore step when setting this parameter to {{false}} for searches of knn_vector fields.
* Updates to the index.knn setting fixed an issue whereby users could update the setting after an index had been created.
* Updates provide more detailed error messaging/validation for Faiss training than was previously available, which made it difficult to debug product quantization (PQ) and inverted file system (IVF). The enhancement provides improved error messages by adding explicit checks for the most common errors that cover 90% of training failures that occur.
* Updates to k-NN functionality ensure consistent results across filter queries that previously provided incorrect results.
* OpenSearch plugins traditionally store metadata in system indexes, which can lead to challenges related to version compatibility, resource constraints, and single-tenant limitations. This release introduces a repository wrapper that transitions plugin metadata from system indexes to stateless OpenSearch nodes using external storage like remote OpenSearch clusters or cloud providers.
* Multi-tenancy is available for key plugins like ML Commons and Flow Framework, enabling logical resource separation by tenant ID. This enables cloud providers to conceptualize plugins as a service to support delivery of scalable multi-tenant solutions.
* A built-in multimodal preprocessor function for Cohere lets users create a connector by providing a function name, simplifying development and avoiding complex Painless scripts.
* An enhancement to the conversational agent allows users to build tools using large language model (LLM)-generated inputs as search parameters.
* A new Learning to Rank plugin enhances search relevance by incorporating ML and behavioral data. It leverages lightweight ML models like XGBoost and RankLib to rescore search results, considering multiple factors in the ranking process to significantly improve the accuracy and relevance of results.
* A new {{template}} query type introduces placeholder variables in search queries that remain unresolved until a search request processor assigns their value, enabling more dynamic and secure search operations.

h4. EXPERIMENTAL FEATURES

OpenSearch 2.19 includes the following experimental functionality. Experimental features are disabled by default. For instructions on how to enable them, refer to the documentation for the feature.

* The experimental Discover view now supports the SQL and Piped Processing Language (PPL) query languages in addition to Dashboards Query Language (DQL) and Lucene, along with new autocomplete functionality and improved data selection to provide a more flexible and efficient query experience.
* Star-tree aggregation adds support for metric aggregations and date histograms with metric aggregations, delivering up to 100x query reduction and 30x lower cache utilization, with optimized binary search for multiple {{terms}} queries.
* Improvements to disk-tiered request cache performance divide the cache into multiple partitions, each protected by its own read/write lock, enabling multiple concurrent readers to access data without contention and multiple writers to operate simultaneously, providing higher write throughput.
* Experimental derived source functionality for k-NN vectors optimizes storage by removing vectors from the JSON source and dynamically injecting them when needed, supporting flat vector mappings, object fields, and single-level nested fields.

h4. DEPRECATION NOTICES

*Deprecating support for Ubuntu Linux 20.04* Please note that OpenSearch and OpenSearch Dashboards will deprecate support for Ubuntu Linux 20.04 as a continuous integration build image and supported operating system in an upcoming version, as Ubuntu Linux 20.04 will reach end-of-life with standard support as of April 2025 (refer to [+this notice+|https://ubuntu.com/blog/ubuntu-20-04-lts-end-of-life-standard-support-is-coming-to-an-end-heres-how-to-prepare] from Canonical Ubuntu). For a list of the compatible operating systems, [+visit here+|https://opensearch.org/docs/latest/install-and-configure/os-comp/].

*Deprecating support for Amazon Linux 2 on OpenSearch Dashboards* Please note that OpenSearch Dashboards will deprecate support for Amazon Linux 2 as a continuous integration build image and supported operating system in an upcoming version, as Node.js 18 will reach end-of-life with support as of April 2025 (refer to [+this notice+|https://nodejs.org/en/blog/announcements/v18-release-announce] from [http://nodejs.org|http://nodejs.org|smart-link] ) and newer version of Node.js LTS version (20+) will not support runtime on Amazon Linux 2. For a list of the compatible operating systems, [+visit here+|https://opensearch.org/docs/latest/install-and-configure/os-comp/].

----

OpenSearch 2.18 includes a number of updates that help you build machine learning (ML)-powered applications, increase performance and stability, and improve the way you and your teams collaborate using OpenSearch.

h3. NEW AND UPDATED FEATURES

* Enhancements to the ML inference search response processor improve the integration of ML models in search pipelines, enabling more sophisticated and context-aware document ranking and result augmentation.
* A new reranker type, ByField, has been added to the rerank processor, allowing you to perform a second-level rerank on search results, based on a specified target field, to achieve greater search relevance.
* New performance updates for vector search applications include optimizations for better memory and cache management for native libraries, an updated approach to creating vector data structures to accelerate index creation, and the integration of AVX512 SIMD support for the Faiss engine.
* You can now define the search pipeline parameter directly within the Multi-search API request body when building search pipelines, offering greater flexibility and control over search pipeline deployments.
* New paginated APIs for _cat/indices and _cat/shards let you take advantage of _cat APIs for troubleshooting at scale in larger clusters, avoiding performance constraints.
* Grouping top N queries by similarity now supports field names and data types, allowing you to group queries at a finer level of detail so that you can better identify and analyze resource-intensive query patterns across query types.
* Workspaces provide a new multi-tenant environment to increase team collaboration. Granular access controls let you manage or remove collaborators and control their access at the workspace level with role-based permissions.
* A redesigned homepage and navigation structure provide a centralized toolkit for accessing and creating Workspaces, with a more cleanly organized navigation bar that adapts to the selected workspace and supports tailored workflows
* Two new analyzers, {{phone}}[ +and+ |https://opensearch.org/docs/latest/analyzers/supported-analyzers/phone-analyzers/]{{phone-search}}, have been added as an optional plugin to simplify the complex task of parsing global phone numbers.

h3. EXPERIMENTAL FEATURES

OpenSearch 2.18 includes the following experimental functionality. Experimental features are disabled by default. For instructions on how to enable them, refer to the documentation for the feature.

* An updated Discover interface enhances the query experience and offers greater customization options. This release adds PPL and SQL as query options in Discover alongside Dashboards Query Language (DQL) and Lucene, and improvements to the data selector and the addition of autocomplete functionality further enhance usability.

----

OpenSearch 2.17 includes new and updated features to help you build and optimize your search applications, improve stability, availability, and resiliency, enhance ease of use, and more.

h3. NEW AND UPDATED FEATURES

* Introduced as an experimental feature in OpenSearch 2.15, remote cluster state publication is now generally available in 2.17.
* To help users benefit from concurrent segment search for the right requests, OpenSearch 2.17 adds a new setting both at index and cluster level. These settings along with pluggable “decider” logic will give more granular control on the requests that will be executed using concurrent search.
* Adds support for encoding numeric term values as a Roaring bitmap. By encoding the values more efficiently, a search request can use a stored filter that matches over a million documents, with lower retrieval latency and less memory used.
* Introduces disk optimized vector search feature which significantly reduces the operational costs for vector workloads.
* Vector search introduces byte vector support to its Faiss engine. Faiss Byte vector is a memory-efficient encoding technique that reduces memory requirements by up to 75% with a minimal drop in recall, making it suitable for large-scale workloads.
* Introduces ML inference search processors, enabling users to run model predictions while conducting search queries.
* Introduces batch asynchronous ingestion, allowing users to trigger batch inference jobs, monitor job status, and ingest results once batch processing is complete.
* Flow Framework plugin now supports advanced user level security in 2.17. Users can now use backend roles to configure fine-grained access to individual workflows based on roles.
* ML inference search processors has now enhanced search response processors by allowing users to specify running model prediction for all documents in one request or running model prediction for each document.

h3. EXPERIMENTAL FEATURES

OpenSearch 2.17.0 includes the following experimental features. Experimental features are disabled by default. For instructions on how to enable them, refer to the documentation for the feature.

* OpenSearch 2.17 introduces application-based configuration templates. When enabled, this feature provides your cluster with a set of pre-defined component templates, streamlining the creation of indexes and index templates tailored to your specific needs.
* Introduces experimental mechanisms to achieve indexing and search isolation within a cluster by adding a new replica shard type that is intended only to serve search traffic.
* Improves performance of expensive queries using the approximation framework that brings new techniques to short-circuit long running queries by only scoring relevant documents in the query.
* Introduces a custom trace source that is based on the open telemetry schema and includes a redesigned overview page for traces and services.

summary: LTI 1.3 JWKS rotates every 120 minutes because Ignite cache expiry
description:
*Problem*
  KIDs are changing far too frequently (about every 120 minutes), which is not expected for LMS signing keys.

  *Impact*

* Tool launches intermittently fail when tool-side JWKS cache or KID lookup doesn’t match rapidly changing Sakai keys.
* Seen as “invalid signature / key not found” behavior by vendors.

  *Root Cause*

* Ignite default cache expiry is 120 minutes.
* SakaiKeySetUtil_cache was not configured as eternal, so key material can expire and be regenerated, replacing all KIDs unexpectedly.

  *Expected Behavior*

* Keyset should remain stable and rotate only on intended schedule.
* Rotation should be monthly

  *Proposed Fix*

# Configure org.sakaiproject.basiclti.util.SakaiKeySetUtil_cache as an eternal Ignite cache.

summary: Notifications: Accordions change order when deleting notifications
description:
Several users have reported that when notifications are deleted from a section, the order of the sections keeps changing. From what we've observed, the order follows the sequence in which notifications first appear. I propose that the order be based on the title instead. This way, sections keep a fixed order, are easier to locate, and don’t move when notifications are deleted.

summary: LTI / IFrame / Flashing Dark to Light as LTI as iframes switch from internal to external sources
description: The fix to [https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-52376|https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-52376|smart-link] introduced an issue where the iframes are marked as “block dark mode” too early that led to light dark flashes as the iframe progresses through a series of internal / external urls.  The solution is to leave the iframes that will launch internal content that progresses to external content as “propagate dark mode” then at the last minute when the frame is about to be redirected to an external url, add the “force light” class via JavaScript.

summary: LTI / Lessons Iframes do not resize when the lti.frameResize message is received
description:
*TL;DR* Fix LTI Frame Resize without breaking Samigo frame resize in Lessons.

LTI tools launched in an iframe have the option to send a “lti.frameResize” windows.postMessage to dynamically ask for a frame resize as the tools frame height changes.  Samigo expects Lessons to auto-resize the iframe 1 second after the question content is loaded and there is JavaScript in ShowItem.html that waits one second and resizes the frame based on the size of the loaded content.  As part of [https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-52276|https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-52276|smart-link] an unrelated switch of the iframe tag to the Sakai web component - which fixed the LTI resize problem but broke the Samigo resize feature.  This part of the fix was reverted in [https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-52374|https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-52374|smart-link] to get Samigo working again but re-breaking the LTI iframe resize.   This Jira will fix the LTI reframe feature in Lessons but keep Samigo working.

Here is the comment from [user] in [https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-52276|https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-52276|smart-link] 🙂 ;

_I think the changes made to ShowItem.html, namely stripping out those blocks of iframe related Javascript may have introduced some UX regressions vis-a-vis the embedding of T&Q in Lessons (if not also for Assignments & Discussions). For instance, the iframe height for embedded T&Q is seemingly now fixed to 350px._

_Without the_ {{onload="resizeiframe1()"}} _attribute (or something analogous) that calls that resize function, the iframe height remains static when a student is navigating through a quiz or through an assignments whereas the the contents of that iframe often vary widely as the student proceeds through the quiz, assignment, etc._

Here is the portion of the patch that broke Samigo inlining itself and adjusting its fame height:

summary: Enforce a hard cap on persisted pinned sites during auto-pin sync
description:
{{syncUserSitesWithPortalNav}} currently auto-pins all accessible sites and saves them via {{savePinnedSites}} with no hard cap. Over time, users (especially test/automation accounts) can accumulate hundreds of pinned sites. This makes left navigation noisy and can degrade UX/performance.


{{portal.default.tabs}} only seems to have an effect in MoreSitesView

Implement a hard limit for persisted pinned sites (configurable, e.g. portal.pinned.max, default 20) and enforce it in backend pinning logic.

summary: Kernel Change the Default citationsAdmin.autocreate to be false
description:
Back in 2004 we invented a thing called *CitationsAdmin* which auto-created site to manage lists of Citations.  Back in 2009 we made it optional in [SAK-15887|https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-15887] with a sakai.property {{citationsAdmin.autocreate=true}} - now in 2025, we are going to “fix the glitch” (Office Space movie reference) and set the default to {{false}}.


This site is created by the {{init()}} method of the citations.BaseConfigurationService when Sakai starts up - if the feature was off when the Sakai database was created, and the admin wants the site to exist, simply add {{citationsAdmin.autocreate=true}} to {{sakai.properties}} and restart Sakai.

Once the site is created, it remains regardless of the setting of this parameter.   If the site is deleted and the parameter is {{true}} it will be re-created on the next boot (so it can be tough to delete because it recreates itself on every boot).

The citations feature continues to work in Resources.

summary: Add full gradebook matrix export endpoint to Sakai webapi
description:
Implemented a new first-class gradebook export API in webapi:

* GET /api/sites/{siteId}/grading/full-gradebook
* GET /api/sites/{siteId}/grading/full-gradebook/{gradebookUid}
* Optional query param: includeComments=true|false (default false)

  The endpoint returns a single integration-friendly payload with:

* Gradebook settings (gradeType, category mode, course-grade display flags)
* Categories (weights/drop-keep config)
* Assignment columns (points, weight, category, released/counted, external linkage)
* Students
* Per-student per-assignment grades
* Per-student course grade (calculatedGrade, mappedGrade, points earned/possible)

summary: LTI: allow pop-up to be changed not working as expected
description:
This seems to be inconsistent and I need to keep an eye on 25 and 23 to see if it inconsistently there also. 

This morning I added the LTI 1.1 Test Tool to trunk with a height set of 600 and checked allow popup to be changed. When I added the tool to the navigation, it opened in a new tab. Clicking on Edit, I expected the checkbox to launch in popup to be checked, and it was. I unchecked the it and the tool then loaded in the iframe. This worked as expected.

This evening I added the tool to a different site, and it loaded in a new tab. When I went to edit it, the checkbox was not checked and I was not able to get it to load in the iframe at all. Checking and unchecking the box did not make any difference, it just kept loading in a new tab.

Adding the same tool to a third site, it launched in a new tab and when editing, the checkbox for launch in popup was checked. I was able to uncheck it and it loaded in the iframe. This worked as expected.

I have seen this before when the option on the server is allow popup to be changed that sometimes, even though the checkbox is not checked, the tool launches in a new tab.

summary: Profile: enabling upload and official profile picture does not work
description:
In file *default.sakai.properties* there are the following information regarding profile image:


{noformat}# Allow users to change their profile picture? (true/false)
# DEFAULT: true
# profile2.picture.change.enabled=true {noformat}

{noformat}# Can users upload an image or just link to an existing one? (upload/url/official)
# *NOTE: If using official, see below.
# DEFAULT: upload
# profile2.picture.type=upload{noformat}

{noformat}# Official Image Support - to enable support for using official images, set to true
# DEFAULT: false
# profile2.official.image.enabled=false{noformat}

{noformat}# If enabled, where should Profile2 look for the officially provided images?
# If 'url', you need to add a URL for each user to the PROFILE_IMAGES_OFFICIAL_T table in the database.
# If 'provider', you need your UserDirectoryProvider implementation to add a BASE64 encoded image to a property
# on the User object. This is already in place for the LDAP provider, just setup the jpegPhoto attribute.
# See http://jira.sakaiproject.org/browse/SAK-17816.
# profile2.official.image.source=url{noformat}

{noformat}# If enabled and you set the source to 'provider' above you also need to specify the attribute, if different to this value.
# Used when profile2.official.image.source=provider is configured. Attributre should match the value your provider populates in the properties for a User.
# see SAK-17816
# DEFAULT: jpegPhoto
# profile2.official.image.attribute=jpegPhoto{noformat}

{noformat}# Note that if you want to use *only* officially provided images you also should set
# profile2.picture.type=official
# If you want to allow a user to choose either the official image or an uploaded/url one of their choice,
# do not set type=official and rather set profile2.picture.type=url/upload. They will then be able to choose
# to use either the official image, or one they select.
# Remember, you can always disable changes altogether via profile2.picture.change.enabled=false{noformat}



we have set 

* profile2.picture.change.enabled=true
* profile2.picture.type=upload
* profile2.official.image.enabled=true
* profile2.official.image.source=provider
* profile2.official.image.attribute=jpegPhoto


as provider we have configured LDAP.



With this setup, there is no option for the user to change between an uploaded image and the official one.

Changing the prop to 

* profile2.picture.type=official

does use the official one, but  does not allow to change profile image (as specified in default.sakai.properties)


Note: With Sakai 23 this setup works and the user can choose between official and an uploaded one. I have noticed that the tab *preferences* is missing in sakai 25, where you could (sakai 23) switch between official and uploaded.

I could not test this with master branch.

summary: Assignments group submissions can drift between groupId and submitter roster, causing wrong group ownership, student status, and Gradebook updates
description:
For group assignments, Sakai persists both {{ASN_SUBMISSION.GROUP_ID}} and {{ASN_SUBMISSION_SUBMITTER}} rows, but different code paths use different ownership signals. Group grading resolves submissions by {{groupId}}, Assignments by Student and some student lookups resolve by persisted submitter rows, and Gradebook-by-group derives target groups from current live membership of those submitter ids. In addition, the group submission edit flow can change {{submission.groupId}} without rebuilding the submitter roster.
  

As a result, one group submission can appear under the wrong group in grading, students in the apparent owning group can see “not started,” and Gradebook scores can be written for a different group than the one owning the submission in Assignments.

summary: Group submission lookup can delete the wrong submission when stale group rosters overlap
description:
For group assignments, the submitter list stored on a submission is a persisted snapshot, not a live view of current group membership.

If a student remains on an older group submission’s persisted submitter roster, but their current assignment group resolves to a different group, a later lookup by user id can mis-handle the situation. The group lookup path ends up treating the two group submissions as duplicate user submissions. The repository duplicate-cleanup logic then deletes one submission row during a read/lookup.

  This causes two visible problems:

* the wrong group submission can be returned/displayed
* the valid current group submission can be deleted from {{ASN_SUBMISSION}}

  The delete happens in repository cleanup, so it does not emit the normal {{asn.delete.submission}} event.

summary: LTI: Issues with sakai-lti-admin-iframe
description:
In collaboration with Turnitin, two outstanding issues were identified with sakai-lti-admin-iframe:

* Need to allow for local network access (same issue addressed by [+SAK-52276+|https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-52276])
* The height is not responsive, defined with both a height attribute and as css within a style attribute.

This issue is evident within an LTI popup/modal when configuring an external tool to be a submission type for an assignment in the Assignments tool.

Cursorily, the overarching fix seems to be to supplant the replace the element that is nested within external-modal-iframe-div (in the Add/Edit Assignment view) with the sakai-lti-iframe webcomponent where both concerns are (mostly?) encapsulated. Presumably, other adjustments in JS, templates, and elsewhere may need to be made.

All that said, so far I’m not able to reproduce the local network access problem (Chrome view with sad face) using tsugi tools, but barring reproducing that, the “local-network-access *” string set within the allow attribute for the webcomponent’s iframe ‘should’ resolve the reported problem. Testing this without that specific case (e.g., the specific external tool with its host) might prove difficult/elusive.

summary: Refactor Sakai's Kernel Spring XML configuration
description:
Modernize bean wiring patterns and resolve deep-seated startup failures caused by legacy Spring 1.x/2.x factory bean patterns that were incompatible with modern Spring initialization semantics.

The refactor eliminated all TransactionProxyFactoryBean, ProxyFactoryBean, CurrentClassLoaderTxProxyFactoryBean, MethodInvokingFactoryBean, and lookup-method usages from the kernel, replacing them with [user], <aop:config> with interface-based pointcuts, and direct setter injection. In doing so, the refactor also exposed and fixed several long-standing dead dependencies and circular initialization chains that had been masked by the old patterns.

Dead code removed:
    → SessionManager from ServerConfigurationService
    → UsageSessionService from SqlService
    → Transaction proxies from DBHelper
    → SecurityService roleswap code

Architecture corrected:
    → All AOP pointcuts target interfaces ✓
    → JDK proxy used everywhere ✓
    → No CGLIB across ClassLoader boundaries ✓

Spring modernized:
    → TransactionProxyFactoryBean gone ✓
    → CurrentClassLoaderTxProxyFactoryBean gone ✓
    → MethodInvokingFactoryBean gone ✓
    → lookup-method gone ✓
    → [user] where appropriate ✓
    → [aop:config|aop:config] with interface pointcuts ✓

summary: In-progress assessments use stale published answer hashes after regrade/republish
description:
When an instructor edits and republished a published assessment, student submissions can still be graded against the old published answer key if the student opened the assessment before the instructor does the regrade/republish.

*Root cause:*

* Student submit grading uses DeliveryBean cached publishedAssessment, publishedItemHash, publishedItemTextHash, and publishedAnswerHash rather than forcing a fresh reload from the DB at submit time.
* If a student begins the assessment before republish, submits after republish, and their session still holds the old published answer metadata, the submission is graded against the old answer key.

  *Expected*:

* After republish/regrade, any student submission should be graded against the latest published assessment data.

If the instructor edits the settings for the topic or forum, the grading is not set and saving the settings makes the rubric icon disappear. 

It’s linking to the rubric in the original site - editing the rubric in the original site after the import changes the rubric that appears in the destination site.

summary: SCORM: Xerte file not passing correct values to the results page and nothing to the Gradebook
description:
Files from [scorm.com|http://scorm.com] (Rustici Software), Articulate Storyline 360 and Camtasia all return a 1, completion status of “completed” and a success status of “passed” if a user completes the SCORM package and passes. If the student completed but failed, a score is also passed, with completion status of “completed” and  success status of “failed” or “incomplete”. If the student exited the package without completing it, the {color:#ff5630}*score is -1*{color}, completion status = incomplete. The results can be seen here: [https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/12uUFxJpYdRqcZJfL3EufbHrJ1KDbtID8xAu7OaCcG5A/edit?usp=sharing|https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/12uUFxJpYdRqcZJfL3EufbHrJ1KDbtID8xAu7OaCcG5A/edit?usp=sharing|smart-link] 

Xerte is different because the {color:#ff5630}*score seems to be -1* {color}whether the student completed/failed/exited, sometimes a completion status, other times no completion status. Not all of the Xerte packages are set to be graded, but I would still expect something to be returned, if the student completed the package, and when applicable, a score if there are correct/incorrect answers, (% correct, for example).

The Underwater Basket Weaving Quiz by Xerte contains 4 questions. I had 3 students launch the package:

Student 149439329 completed the quiz and scored 4/4. SCORM results show a score of -1, no completion or success status, and nothing passed to the Gradebook:

!image-20260408-131134.png|width=671,alt="image-20260408-131134.png"!

Student 917877426 completed the package, and scored 2/4. SCORM results show a score of -1, no completion or success status, and nothing passed to the Gradebook:

!image-20260408-131452.png|width=671,alt="image-20260408-131452.png"!

Student 232534623 answered 1 question, then exited the SCORM player. Sore is -1, completion status is “incomplete”. Nothing is passed to the Gradebook.

!image-20260408-131635.png|width=671,alt="image-20260408-131635.png"!

For student 1, I would have expected the SCORM results to show they completed the package and 100% passed to the Gradebook.

For student2, I would have expected the SCORM results to show they completed the package and 50% passed to the Gradebook.

For student3, the SCORM results already show the completion status as “incomplete” and no score in the Gradebook. This is the only result that seems to meet expectations.

summary: LTI: Handle Turnitin Line Item PUT requests
description:
Scenario: An instructor creates an assignment in the Assignments tool configured to use Turnitin LTI 1.3, which inherently has a submission type of External Tool (LTI). The instructor uses the default gradebook association which creates a Gradebook item to be managed by the Assignments tool.

Later, one of the following scenarios breaks the assignment’s gradebook association:

# The instructor clicks the title of the assignment and then the button ‘Go to External Tool’.
# A student clicks the title of the assignment (presumably to submit work) and then the button ‘Go to External Tool’.

When Turnitin loads via the LTI integration, it sends a PUT request to Sakai to update the line item. Currently, this act overwrites the gradebook association. The assignment’s gradebook association should remain intact, and remain controlled by the Assignments tool.

summary: Turnitin: Clicking 'Refresh inbox data' soon after Sakai restarts
description:
This bug is contingent upon the shutdown and restart of Sakai. During Sakai’s restart, Sakai's public-private key pair for validating JWTs is renewed. Thus, old tokens used prior to Sakai’s shutdown are invalidated. That said, Sakai transparently communicates this by responding with HTTP codes of 403 and reports the specific problem with {{retval={"error":"signature_error"}}}, from which external tools can respond by fetching a new token and then re-invoking the failed request. (Or at least that’s my understanding.)

Some good news is that so far, I've not seen other invalid signature stack traces invoked for other Turnitin requests. Hopefully, the bug described further below is relatively isolated.

Also, fortunately, this bug’s operative window is an hour or less, due to the external tool’s need to fetch a new token a given token expires. (The lifetime for such tokens is generally 3600 seconds.) 

Of course, Sakai and other developers who need to restart Sakai more frequently when doing development work would be far more sensitized to this particular bug. Nevertheless, an instructor encountering this problem within an hour of Sakai’s startup is a reasonable scenario.

Refer to [+this screencast+|https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_7GN7ViW1ytl4T4D-LISgRHzeDrCcK-Q/view?usp=sharing] to see this bug in action.

summary: DateManager add bulk date setter controls
description:
Managing dates in Date Manager is still tedious when the goal is not to shift everything by a relative amount, but to set specific target dates across many items. The existing date shifter works for “move everything forward/backward by X days,” but it is awkward for
common instructor workflows like “set all open dates to Monday at 8:00 AM” or “set all due dates to Friday at 11:59 PM.” In those cases, users have to edit many rows manually, which is slow and error-prone, especially when working across multiple expanded sections.

This change adds bulk date setter controls to Date Manager so users can enter one or more specific dates once and apply them across all items or only the currently expanded sections. It supports the main date fields used in the tool, validates that at least one bulk
date was entered before applying changes, and keeps the existing “Save Changes” flow intact. The result is faster setup, fewer repetitive edits, and a better fit for real course date-management workflows.

Codex with GPT 5.4 high was used in creating this. I did manually test it myself also.



* Introduced a bulk date setter feature enabling users to enter and apply multiple date values simultaneously across calendar items.
* Added flexible application options: apply dates to all items or restrict to only visible and expanded sections.
* Implemented input validation with clear error messaging when attempting to apply without entering required dates.

summary: Assignments / LTI Provide the $ResourceLink.available.startDateTime LTI 1.3 substitution parameter
description:
The {{$ResourceLink.available.startDateTime}} is not properly substituted with the actual “Open Date” for the assignment. 

in lti 1.3 - there are four dates 

{noformat}ResourceLink.available.startDateTime # when students can open/access the link
ResourceLink.available.endDateTime # when students can no longer open/access it

ResourceLink.submission.startDateTime # when the tool should start accepting submissions
ResourceLink.submission.endDateTime # when the tool should stop accepting submissions{noformat}

In Sakai we have open date, due date and accept until date.

According to ChatGPT:

Sakai’s model is actually cleaner than LTI’s once you line them up conceptually. The trick is: *Sakai splits “submission end” into two semantic phases (due vs accept-until), while LTI only has one hard submission end.*

Here’s the clean mapping:

----

h3. Sakai → LTI 1.3 mapping

{noformat}Sakai.openDate        → ResourceLink.available.startDateTime
                        ResourceLink.submission.startDateTime

Sakai.dueDate         → (NO direct LTI field — tool must interpret)

Sakai.acceptUntilDate → ResourceLink.submission.endDateTime
                        ResourceLink.available.endDateTime   (optional){noformat}

----

summary: Setting portal.notifications.push.enabled=false should not show "Push is not enabled - <Enable>" in UI
description:
This issue [https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-51526|https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-51526|smart-link] describes the exact issue, and it got resolved.
However implementation of this issue [https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-51709|https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-51709|smart-link]  breaks the original fix.

The mistake seems to be to have turned the variable {{this.pushEnabled}} in {{SakaiNotifications.js}} from a Backend-Variable coming from {{UserMessagingServiceImpl.java}} into a local-state variable {{this._pushEnabled}} with completely different meaning.

Proposed fix:
Separate the actual meaning of the two concerns cleanly, using two variables:
- {{pushServerFeatureEnabled}} - coming from backend and telling us whether the sysadmin has activated that feature via {{sakai.properties}}
- {{_pushClientReady}} - solely front-end-state telling us whether setting up push notifications in the front-end has been done or is still open

*Note:* I was able to get the original functionality of hiding the UI-Message in case of setting the property to false, when reverting the single file {{SakaiNotifications.js}} back to {{78faa0bc72e74bddf0eae8ea2bb43c5d3e98af71}}

I’d be willing to make a pull request next week, if there is interest in that.

# If a gradebook item created in Gradebook is an LTI line item, check first to see if that gradebook item is associated with an assignment in the Assignments tool. If so, treat the line item like other assignments (as a rule of thumb). (Note, however that such gb items can be associated with multiple assignments. summary: LTI Allow Tools to use LTI Bearer Tokens to Access WebAPI  and Direct
description:
Sakai has an OAuth 1.0 authentication to access direct web services that is out of date, broken and scheduled for removal - [https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-52541|https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-52541|smart-link]

In its place we need to add a feature to Sakai to allow LTI tools to get Tokens to access /api and /direct without a per-user log in - it is more of a per-tool login.

The External Tools UI will add an API Setup option to each tool where a tool can be granted any number of Sakai authorization functions (like content.read).  A tool can discover which functions it has been granted as well as the /direct and /api endpoints using LTI 1.3 custom substitution parameters.

The tool can request an API token that contains scopes that represent Sakai functions it is allowed to use.  These LTI JWTs can be presented to /direct or /api to give access to those services.

summary: LTI Add a checkbox giving an LTI tool readonly access to non-owned lineitems
description:
This adds a feature to allow a tool to have readonly access to all the columns and student data in the gradebook.  The tool still has read-write access in the columns the tool owns - but can view any column in the gradebook.  The feature is documented here:

[https://github.com/[user]/sakai/blob/SAK-52583/lti/docs/LTI13_EXTENSIONS.md|https://github.com/[user]/sakai/blob/SAK-52583/lti/docs/LTI13_EXTENSIONS.md|smart-link] 

The primary use case is to enable the building of a full-featured badging system that can plug into Sakai using only LTI NRPS and AGS - with this extension.  A badging tool needs all the grades and needs to let the admin / instructor then decide wat achievements warrant what badges in the course.

This is pretty simple and reuses all the existing AGS tooling in Sakai and tools.  When enabled, the tool can list all lieitems and those that the tool does not own have an extension in the returned JSON:

{noformat}{
  "id": "https://lms.example.edu/imsblis/lti13/lineitems/site-id/12345",
  "scoreMaximum": 100,
  "label": "Midterm",
  "https://www.sakailms.org/spec/lti-ags/v2p0/readOnly": true
}{noformat}

The tool can retrieve line item detail and then the student grades.  Student names come from the NRPS service.

With AGS+Extension and NRPS a full featured LTI installable bading system can be supported in Sakai.

description:
See [https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-52582|https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-52582|smart-link] 

We talked about this in the QA meeting. The behavior for invalid scores should be consistent.

In 23, the invalid score is removed from the cell if the instructor does not correct it.

The fix in SAK-52582: 

* US GB with decimal point: the invalid grade drops the comma and any number that follows the comma if the instructor does not fix it - preference is that the score be removed as in 23 and in the Spanish GB
* Spanish GB with commas: the invalid grade is removed if the instructor doesn’t fix it - this is consistent with 23 behavior and preferred behavior

summary: Locale-aware sorting: global use of UserSortNameComparator with preferred locale
description:
Across multiple Sakai tools, user lists were not sorted correctly for names with accented or special characters (e.g. Martínez, Peña) because sorting did not respect the site/user preferred locale.

Root cause: various tools used Collator.getInstance() without a locale, Collator.PRIMARY (which ignores diacritics), or plain String.compareTo() with no collator at all.

Fix (PR #14630 by ottenhoff): UserSortNameComparator has been updated to accept the preferred locale and is now used consistently across the platform.

Origin: the issue was first identified in the Section Tool roster view (EnrollmentDecorator) and addressed in PR #14619, which served as the starting point for this broader improvement.

summary: Assignments: Adjust Mapping of LTI Dates to Assignments Dates
description:
So there are for LTI 1.3 variable affecting assignment availability and due dates in the LTI protocols.  Sadly these variables don’t map perfectly to Sakai’s Assignment variables and they similarly do not map to TII’s sense of the variables.  So we are iterating on the right way to map these variables between Sakai and LTI 1.3 tools like TII - hopefully each iteration gets closer.  And hopefully we will end up with a mapping that is good for any LTI tool not just TII.

This PR also changes the PUT request to only change due date and leave {{Available date}} alone.

Here is the latest proposed external to internal mapping:

||Substitution variable||How Sakai sets it||
|ResourceLink.available.startDateTime|Earliest non-null of visible date and open date (omitted if both are unset). Visible date is rarely set in practice because the Assignments UI does not expose it by default.|
|ResourceLink.submission.startDateTime|open date|
|ResourceLink.submission.endDateTime|due date|
|ResourceLink.available.endDateTime|Latest non-null of close date, due date, and resubmission accept-until (omitted if all are unset)|

In IMS Global Learning Consortium LTI 1.3 / LTI Advantage, the {{ResourceLink.submission.*}} variables are part of the *LTI Names and Role Provisioning / launch substitution variable model* used to communicate assignment timing semantics from the LMS to the tool.

The key thing is:

* {{available.*}} → when the activity is visible / accessible
* {{submission.*}} → when submissions are expected / accepted

The {{submission.*}} values are intended to describe the _assessment workflow_, not merely page visibility.

Submission map pretty cleanly.  Sakai has multiple values that might impact “available” so we take the earliest of Sakai’s “start access” values and the latest of the “end access” values.

Note that Sakai has {{visible date}} pre-configured not to show in the UI and will always be null.  So normally there are only four values (a) open, (b) due, (c) close, and (d) resubmit that can be set in the Sakai UI.

I have update Tsugi to request more of the custom values for easy debugging - it also asks for the Sakai specific  custom parameters as well - all this should make debugging and validation easier.

I also updated the internal dev doc:

[https://github.com/[user]/sakai/blob/SAK-52600/lti/docs/ASSIGNMENTS.md|https://github.com/[user]/sakai/blob/SAK-52600/lti/docs/ASSIGNMENTS.md|smart-link] 

This points to my branch but should be updated to master when the PR is merged.

summary: Announcements tool hides future announcements from instructors who can edit them
description: The Announcements tool currently retrieves messages through the normal view-filtered channel path. Since SAK-49544, that path applies release/retract visibility via PrivacyFilter, so an instructor who did not create a future-dated announcement  may not see it in the Announcements tool even if they have permission to edit all announcements in the site. This is correct for Dashboard/synoptic/API view surfaces, but incorrect for the Announcements management tool.

summary: Subsites: Remove the sakai.properties configuration
description:
Currently, we have 2 properties that affect (1) how the list of subsites is displayed in the tools menu and (2) whether it is displayed at all.

{noformat}# Whether or not to include subsites in the portal. If set to never, subsites will never be included. 
# If set to false, subsites may be included depending on the site preferences. 
# If set to any other value, subsites will always be included. 
# DEFAULT= none (null) = always include
# portal.includesubsites=never{noformat}

{noformat}## SAK-22703 - Optionally group subsites into flyout menu
## Default changed to true in SAK-32499
# The flyout subsites menu is off by default. Grouping the subsites into a flyout menu can be very 
# useful if you have a wide and shallow site hierarchy. To turn it on, set the following property to true. 
# DEFAULT: true
# portal.showSubsitesAsFlyout=false{noformat}

On one hand, {{portal.includesubsites}} has a default value of an empty string, or any value except false or never, for it to work. However, it does not work if you leave it empty (which is the default value). On the other hand, I am not sure how, if I set it to false, I can make the subsites menu appear in the tools menu for a specific site [user] .

{{portal.showSubsitesAsFlyout}}. The default option is true (subsites are grouped), but the description says: "The flyout subsites menu is off by default".

In addition, the items are not well integrated with the rest of the interface elements.

My proposal is that {{portal.includesubsites}} should only accept true and never (and if false is no longer in use, remove it).

{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
Update
{panel}

The sakai.properties configuration for subsite behavior has been completely removed. The only available behavior is now the previous default: an always-visible list with a flyout menu, visually aligned with the Lessons subpages navigation for greater consistency across the site menu.
