summary: Fix feedback dates upon assessment import so that they are not before the due/accept until date
description:
This issue is related to [https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-34476|https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-34476|smart-link] 

The majority of assessments experiencing the date issue in [https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-34476|https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-34476|smart-link] are created when instructors import assessments from a prior term, but forgot to go back and update the feedback displayed to student dates, resulting in the dates being before the due/late date, and the feedback being visible to students while taking the exam.

To avoid this problem when importing, we would like to propose that the “feedback available” dates be updated upon import, so that no imported assessment can introduce old feedback dates that are prior to due/late dates.

If we do this, we would need to:

* Set the “show feedback date” to be the same as the due date or accept until date (whichever is later).
* If there is a “hide feedback date” there should be a calculation to determine the number of days between the original show/hide dates and set the “hide feedback date” to a similar interval after the updated show date (which has been set to the same as the retract date).
* If there is no due date or accept until date set for an imported assessment, the show/hide feedback dates should be removed and reset the assessment to the default option “No, do not display any feedback to the student”

summary: Prevent new assessments from selecting feedback dates prior to the due/late dates
description:
This issue is related to [https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-34476|https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-34476|smart-link] and [https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-52615|https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-52615|smart-link] 

The T&L/UX group consensus is that saving feedback dates prior to due/late dates should not be allowed. There is already an immediate feedback option labeled “Yes, show the student feedback while they are taking the assessment. They can change their answers accordingly.” Since this immediate option already exists without using the feedback dates fields, we don’t see any use case where entering feedback dates prior to the due/end date, or in absence of the due date, would be desired.

The T&L/UX group recommends that this be strictly enforced, and should prevent the user from saving until the feedback dates are corrected or removed. 

If we prevent saving in Samigo, then it needs to also be enforced in Date Manager, during import, and anywhere else feedback dates would be edited.

summary: Allow Sakai-to-Sakai iCal calendar subscriptions with circular loop detection
description:
h2. Problem

Sakai rejects all ICS requests originating from another Sakai instance by checking the User-Agent header for the string "Sakai". This was an intentional workaround (introduced as SAK-21718) to prevent infinite subscription loops between sites, but it also blocks legitimate cross-site subscriptions with no circular dependency.

h2. Solution

Replace the User-Agent heuristic with proper circular-dependency detection using a custom HTTP header X-Sakai-Calendar-Chain that carries the comma-separated siteId path accumulated so far. If the destination site finds its own siteId already in the chain, a circular subscription exists and the request is rejected with HTTP 500 and a WARN log entry. Otherwise the site appends its own siteId and continues normally.

Additional changes:

* generateICal only exports primary events (not re-exported subscription events) to avoid cascading duplicates across multi-hop subscription chains.
* A custom ICS property X-SAKAI-SITE-NAME is added to each exported event so that subscribers display the originating site name in the event title (e.g. "Staff meeting (Site B)").
* Duplicate subscription events (same name + start time) arriving via multiple subscription paths are deduplicated in getEvents().

h2. Files changed

* calendar/calendar-impl/impl/src/java/org/sakaiproject/calendar/impl/BaseCalendarService.java
* calendar/calendar-impl/impl/src/java/org/sakaiproject/calendar/impl/BaseExternalCalendarSubscriptionService.java
* calendar/calendar-impl/impl/src/java/org/sakaiproject/calendar/impl/readers/IcalendarReader.java
* config/configuration/bundles/src/bundle/org/sakaiproject/config/bundle/default.sakai.properties

h2. Feature flag

All new behaviour is gated behind calendar.subscription.sakai.enabled (default: false). When disabled, the original User-Agent blocking is preserved exactly and no existing behaviour is affected. Set to true in sakai.properties to activate the new chain-based detection and site attribution.

summary: Test & Quizzes: AutoSubmit Assessments Job does not process submissions after the closing date
description:
When an assessment has the auto-submit option enabled ("Automatically submit any saved student work after the Due Date or Late Submission Deadline"), the current process only auto-submits submissions made before the closing date. Therefore, if a student takes the assessment after that date (for example, due to a time exception), their submission will never be processed if it remains in draft status.

The following query can be used to detect in-progress submissions that have not been processed by the job.

{noformat}select *
from sam_assessmentgrading_t sag,
    sam_publishedaccesscontrol_t pua
where pua.assessmentid=sag.publishedassessmentid
    and ((pua.latehandling=1 and pua.retractdate<sysdate) or (pua.latehandling=2 and pua.duedate<sysdate))
    and sag.status not in (-1,5) and (sag.hasAutoSubmissionRun = 0 or sag.hasAutoSubmissionRun is null) and pua.autoSubmit = 1
    and sag.attemptDate is not null;{noformat}

summary: Video Training Tool
description:
Sponsored by WESTACO EXPRESS ([westaco.com|http://westaco.com]), developed by Entornos de Formación ([edf.global|https://www.edf.global/]).

Currently, other LMS platforms offer native video processing capabilities. In Sakai, you currently need to rely on costly third-party LTI integrations (such as Kaltura or Panopto) to achieve adaptive streaming and detailed tracking.

The Video Training Module (VTM) closes this gap by providing a highly advanced video ecosystem. The key competitive advantage of this module compared to the closed solutions offered by other LMS platforms is its hybrid storage approach: it allows institutions to process and host videos locally, or to externalize storage by synchronizing them with private channels on platforms such as YouTube. This flexibility enables institutions to dramatically reduce storage and bandwidth costs on their own servers while maintaining a centralized user experience where students never leave Sakai.

* Zero interruptions for students: Support for adaptive bitrate HLS uploads, ensuring smooth playback on any connection.
* Deep Pedagogical Integration: Native “Video Training Picker” embedded directly into the Lessons page authoring interface, without disrupting the instructor’s workflow.
* Actionable Analytics: Tracking of total views and unique viewers per video to measure actual student engagement.
* Visibility and Scope Management:
** Global: Centralized institutional repository accessible to any authenticated user. Ideal for cross-disciplinary training content.
** Course: Strict privacy; videos are only visible to students enrolled in the course.
** Lessons: Isolation within dedicated folders for videos uploaded “on the fly” from a lesson unit, preventing the general library from becoming cluttered.

Main Features:

* Infrastructure Savings (Multi-Source): Native video uploads or transparent linking through the YouTube API. The system embeds the player without exposing students to the external platform.
* Automated HLS Transcoding: Background jobs using FFmpeg to automatically generate multiple resolutions.
* Custom “Favorites” and “Watch Later” lists for students.
* Advanced Organization: Hierarchical category trees for managing large video libraries.
* Publishing Workflow: Draft and published states, plus temporary access control (releaseDate / retractDate).
* Metadata Synchronization: Asynchronous updates of titles/descriptions from external sources and email alerts in case of broken or lost access.

The VTM architecture lays a strong foundation for future extensions:

* Accessibility and automatic subtitles.
* Expanded external storage support: native integration with the Vimeo API, for example.
* Tag integration.
* As a native tool rather than an LTI, it enables integration with other tools such as assignments or grading systems.

summary: Gradebook NG: course grade sort ignores decimals in non-English locales due to parseFloat with comma decimal separator
description:
When sorting by course grade in descending order, students with the same letter grade (e.g. "Sobresaliente") are not correctly ordered by their percentage. Instead, they remain in their original order (alphabetical by name), because the decimal part of the percentage is ignored.

Root cause: in gradebook-gbgrade-table.js, the sorter function for the course grade column uses parseFloat(a[1]) to parse the percentage value. In non-English locales (e.g. Spanish), the percentage is formatted with a comma as the decimal separator (e.g. "98,08"). JavaScript's parseFloat() stops parsing at the comma and returns only the integer part (98), making all values within the same grade band appear equal and leaving them unsorted.

Fix: replace the comma with a period before parsing: parseFloat(a[1].replace(',', '.')).

summary: Migrate hierarchy recursive-CTE native queries to the Hibernate 6 Criteria CTE API (Oracle WITH RECURSIVE incompatibility)
description:
This issue was created because Hibernate 5 doesn’t have support for CTE queries and Hibernate 6 does so am thinking it would be best to solve this when we move to Hibernate 6 before the next major version of Sakai. If were still on H5 then I will implement native CTE queries for Oracle just as I did for MySQL/MariaDB.

----

  Related to: SAK-52040 (Hierarchy migrate from genericdao to JPA)

  Background

  SAK-52040 migrated the Hierarchy service from the legacy generic-dao layer to JPA/Hibernate. Almost all data access in HierarchyNodeRepository was expressed with the JPA Criteria API. The exception is ancestor/descendant closure traversal, which
  requires recursive common table expressions (CTEs). Hibernate 5's Criteria API cannot express recursive CTEs, so these four queries were intentionally left as native SQL as accepted, documented tech debt (see the TODO in
  HierarchyNodeRepositoryImpl).

  Current behavior / problem

  The following constants in
  hierarchy/impl/src/main/java/org/sakaiproject/hierarchy/impl/repository/HierarchyNodeRepositoryImpl.java
  are native SQL using WITH RECURSIVE:

* ANCESTORS_IDS_CTE → findAllAncestors(Long)
* DESCENDANTS_IDS_CTE → findAllDescendants(Long)
* ANCESTOR_IDS_BATCH_CTE → findAncestorIdsByNodeIds(Collection<Long>)
* DESCENDANT_IDS_BATCH_CTE → findDescendantIdsByNodeIds(Collection<Long>)

  These are the only native SQL statements in the repository. The WITH RECURSIVE syntax is valid on MySQL/MariaDB but invalid on Oracle, whose recursive subquery factoring omits the RECURSIVE keyword. As written, these queries will fail at runtime on
  Oracle, affecting any caller of the non-direct (transitive) hierarchy operations — e.g. HierarchyService.getChildNodes(..., directOnly=false), getParentNodes(..., false), getChildNodeIds, getParentNodeIds — which back the Delegated Access tree
  building, among others.

  ▎ Note: this is distinct from the one-time upgrade scripts in db/migration/oracle.sql, which already use Oracle-native CONNECT BY and are not affected. This ticket concerns only the runtime repository queries.

  Why this is deferred to the Hibernate 6 upgrade

  Hibernate 6 adds first-class CTE support to HQL and the Criteria API (JpaCriteriaQuery#with(...) / CteCriteria, and the HQL with clause), including recursive CTEs. This lets us express the ancestor/descendant traversals portably through the ORM and
  remove the last native SQL from the repository — resolving the Oracle incompatibility as a side effect rather than maintaining dialect-specific SQL by hand. Doing this work now (pre-Hibernate 6) would mean writing and testing per-dialect native SQL
  that we'd then throw away.

  Scope

* Replace the four native recursive-CTE queries with equivalent Hibernate 6 Criteria/HQL CTE constructs.
* Remove the now-obsolete native SQL constants and the TODO note.
* Keep the existing batch/“origin-tracking” semantics (each row maps an origin node id to a related id) so findAncestorIdsByNodeIds / findDescendantIdsByNodeIds continue resolving many origins in one query.
* Preserve the queryIdPairs parameter-chunking behavior (or its CTE-API equivalent) for large id lists.

  Acceptance criteria

* No native SQL remains in HierarchyNodeRepositoryImpl; all traversal goes through the Criteria/HQL CTE API.
* Ancestor/descendant and batch id-set results are identical to the current implementation (covered by existing HierarchyServiceTest cases).
* The hierarchy traversal queries execute correctly on both MySQL/MariaDB and Oracle.
* TODO comment regarding the Hibernate 6 CTE migration is removed.

  Dependencies / risks

* Blocked by: the Kernel/Hibernate 6 upgrade (link the umbrella ticket once it exists).
* Risk to flag: until this lands, Oracle deployments cannot use the transitive hierarchy operations. If any Oracle installs need these before the Hibernate 6 upgrade ships, we should reconsider deferral and add an interim Oracle-dialect query (e.g.
CONNECT BY / recursive WITH without the keyword) as a stopgap.

  References

* hierarchy/impl/src/main/java/org/sakaiproject/hierarchy/impl/repository/HierarchyNodeRepositoryImpl.java (CTE constants ~L51–L83; consumers findAllAncestors/findAllDescendants/findAncestorIdsByNodeIds/findDescendantIdsByNodeIds)
* SAK-52040

summary: Calendar iCal export should use RRULE for recurring events instead of expanding individual occurrences
description:
When exporting the Schedule/Calendar as an iCal feed (.ics), recurring events are expanded into individual VEVENT occurrences instead of being exported with a standard RRULE property. This has been acknowledged in the source code since at least Sakai 2.x with a TBD comment:

BaseCalendarService.java, generateICal():

/* TBD: add to VEvent: recurring schedule, ...
RecurenceRUle x = event.getRecurrenceRule();
*/

h3. Impact

* A class meeting every Monday/Wednesday/Friday for a semester generates ~50 individual VEVENTs instead of a single VEVENT with RRULE:FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=MO,WE,FR.
* External calendar clients (Google Calendar, Outlook, Apple Calendar) cannot recognise these events as a recurring series, so users cannot edit or manage the whole series.
* The exported ICS file is unnecessarily large for calendars with many recurring events.
* Sakai-to-Sakai subscriptions (SAK-52617) also benefit: fewer events to process and store on the subscribing side.

h3. Proposed fix

Modify generateICal() in BaseCalendarService to retrieve base (non-expanded) events by calling calendar.getEvents(null, null), then:

* For events with a RecurrenceRule: emit a single VEVENT with an RRULE property built from the rule's frequency, interval, count/until.
* For one-time events: emit as individual VEVENT (current behaviour), filtered to the export time window.

Sakai frequency to RRULE mapping:

* Daily → FREQ=DAILY
* Weekly → FREQ=WEEKLY
* MWF → FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=MO,WE,FR
* TTh → FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=TU,TH
* MW → FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=MO,WE
* SMW → FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=SU,MO,WE
* SMTW → FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=SU,MO,TU,WE
* STT → FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=SU,TU,TH
* Monthly → FREQ=MONTHLY
* Yearly → FREQ=YEARLY

INTERVAL is added when > 1. UNTIL or COUNT is added when the rule has a defined end.

summary: User Audit Log timestamps are overwritten on MySQL during user_audits_log migrations
description:
The MySQL DDL for user_audits_log.audit_stamp allows MySQL to create the column as:

{code:sql}timestamp NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP ON UPDATE CURRENT_TIMESTAMP{code}

    This causes audit log timestamps to be rewritten when rows are later updated. In practice, institutions can see thousands of historical User Audit Log entries collapsed onto the same second after migration SQL touches the table.

  The likely trigger is SAK-48106 in docs/conversion/sakai_25_mysql_conversion.sql, which updates existing audit rows to convert stored EIDs to internal user IDs:

{code:sql}  UPDATE user_audits_log AS audits
  INNER JOIN SAKAI_USER_ID_MAP AS idmap ON audits.user_id = idmap.eid
  SET audits.user_id = idmap.user_id;

  UPDATE user_audits_log AS audits
  INNER JOIN SAKAI_USER_ID_MAP AS idmap ON audits.action_user_id = idmap.eid
  SET audits.action_user_id = idmap.user_id;{code}



  Because audit_stamp has ON UPDATE CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, these data migration updates overwrite the original audit timestamps. The audit log then incorrectly reports old events as occurring at the migration runtime.

summary: Calendar: UX improvements for the calendar grid view (navigation, quick event creation, visual cues, collapsible toolbar)
description:
h2. Summary

This ticket bundles a set of UX improvements to the FullCalendar-based calendar grid view (calendar/calendar-tool), implemented and verified in the browser. They improve navigation and event-creation discoverability, free up vertical space above the grid, and fix a pre-existing scrollTime configuration bug.

h2. Changes

* *Day navigation:* clicking a day cell in Month view now switches to the Day view for that date.
* *Quick event creation:* double-clicking a time slot in Day/Week view opens the "New Event" form pre-filled with the clicked date and time (rounded to the half-hour).
* *Half-hour slot shading:* the second half of each hour slot in Day/Week view is subtly shaded, so users can tell that double-clicking can target either the :00 or :30 half.
* *Hover affordance:* day cells (Month view) and time-slot rows (Day/Week view) are shaded on mouse hover with a pointer cursor, indicating they are clickable.
* *Event tooltips:* events now show a native tooltip with the full title, schedule, type and originating site - useful since long titles get truncated in Month view cells.
* *Month view auto height:* Month view rows now size to their content ('auto' height) instead of using a fixed aspect ratio, avoiding excessive empty space or cramped rows on weeks with many events. Other views (Week/Day/List) keep the previous aspect ratio and scroll-to-time behavior.
* *Collapsible toolbar:* a new "Calendar options" toggle next to the tool title shows/hides the tool menu, the view selector (By Calendar/List + default view) and the "Printable Version" link, which are now collapsed by default to bring the calendar grid closer to the top. The expanded/collapsed state is remembered per browser via localStorage.
* *Bug fix - scrollTime reset:* fixed the calendar.fullCalendar.scrollTime sakai.properties setting being reset to its default (06:00) after switching views. FullCalendar's internal ScrollResponder is recreated on a deferred remount (e.g. triggered by aspectRatio/height changes), which reapplies the original scrollTime option. The fix also updates that option (not just issuing a one-off scrollToTime call) whenever the scroll time is set.

summary: Modernize Statistics: Widget-based analytics platform for courses, students, and institutional insights. Umbrella
description:
The current Statistics tool has remained largely unchanged for many years and no longer meets the expectations of modern learning analytics. Institutions increasingly request richer insights into course activity, student engagement, adoption metrics, and early identification of at-risk learners.

This umbrella issue proposes a phased modernization of the Statistics tool, transforming it into a flexible analytics platform built around reusable Web Component widgets.

h3. Goals

* Modernize and refactor the existing Statistics tool.
* Enable widget reuse across Statistics and Dashboard.
* Improve performance through asynchronous widget loading.
* Allow users to customize which analytics are displayed.
* Expand analytics capabilities for instructors, students, and administrators.
* Provide exportable reports and data.
* Establish a foundation for future learning analytics and student success initiatives.

summary: Statistics: Modernization Effort
description:
Refactor and modernize the Statistics tool architecture to establish the foundation for future analytics enhancements.

This phase will focus on replacing legacy rendering technologies with Thymeleaf and introducing a reusable Web Component-based widget architecture.

Key objectives:

* Migrate Statistics views to Thymeleaf (SAK-52731)
* Convert existing statistics reports into reusable widgets.
* Implement asynchronous widget loading.
* Allow widgets to be shown, hidden, and configured by users.
* Enable widget reuse between Statistics and Dashboard.
* Support role-aware rendering for instructors, students, and administrators.
* Modernize the Administration Workspace statistics experience.
* Improve maintainability, extensibility, and performance.

The result of this phase should preserve existing functionality while providing a modern and extensible analytics framework.

summary: Statistics: New Analytics
description:
Expand Statistics beyond its current reporting capabilities by introducing new analytics designed around current institutional and instructor needs.

This phase will be driven by community feedback and stakeholder requirements gathered from Sakai institutions.

Key objectives:

* Define and prioritize new analytics requirements.
* Introduce new instructor-focused engagement and activity metrics.
* Introduce student-facing analytics and progress indicators.
* Add institutional analytics and platform adoption metrics.
* Provide richer visualizations and reporting capabilities.
* Continue expanding the catalog of reusable analytics widgets.

The result of this phase should provide actionable insights for instructors, students, and administrators while promoting data-informed decision making.

summary: Statistics: Introduce Learning Analytics and Student Success features
description:
Extend Statistics from descriptive analytics to actionable learning analytics by helping instructors identify and support potentially disengaged students.

Key objectives:

* Define configurable criteria for identifying at-risk learners.
* Implement engagement monitoring and trend analysis.
* Detect students showing signs of disengagement or possible abandonment.
* Provide instructor-facing alerts and intervention indicators.
* Surface relevant student success metrics through analytics widgets.

The result of this phase should provide early-warning capabilities similar to those available in modern LMS platforms, helping institutions improve student engagement and retention.

summary: Deny AGS write operations for lineitem.readonly tokens
description:
*Short Description*
LTI 1.3 Advantage AGS access tokens requested with only {{https://purl.imsglobal.org/spec/lti-ags/scope/lineitem.readonly}} can be treated as write-capable because the scope checks use substring matching. This can allow tools with readonly AGS scope to create, update, or delete line items.

*Steps to Reproduce*

# Register or configure an LTI 1.3 tool that requests only the AGS readonly line item scope: {{https://purl.imsglobal.org/spec/lti-ags/scope/lineitem.readonly}}.
# Request an access token from Sakai's LTI 1.3 token endpoint with that scope.
# Use the returned token against an AGS line item write endpoint, such as POST, PUT, or DELETE.
# Compare with the code paths in {{lti/lti-blis/src/java/org/sakaiproject/lti13/LTI13Servlet.java}} and {{lti/lti-common/src/java/org/sakaiproject/lti13/util/SakaiAccessToken.java}}.

*Expected Behavior*
A token with only {{lineitem.readonly}} should authorize only AGS line item read operations. POST, PUT, and DELETE should be rejected unless the token has the exact AGS write scope.

*Actual Behavior*
{{handleTokenPost}} checks requested scopes with {{scope.contains(SCOPE_LINEITEM)}}, so {{lineitem.readonly}} also matches {{lineitem}}. {{SakaiAccessToken.hasScope}} also uses substring matching, so internal readonly scope strings can satisfy write-scope checks.

*Impact*
An LTI tool granted readonly AGS line item access may be able to mutate AGS line items, including create, update, or delete operations that should require the write scope. This violates the LTI AGS scope contract and can affect gradebook-linked integrations.

*Environment*

* App version: Sakai trunk / LTI 1.3 AGS implementation

summary: Validate LTI client assertion claims before issuing access tokens
description:
*Short Description*
Sakai's LTI 1.3 access token endpoint verifies the client assertion signature but does not appear to validate all required OAuth/LTI client assertion parameters and claims before minting an access token. Missing validation includes {{grant_type}}, {{client_assertion_type}}, {{iss}}, {{sub}}, {{aud}}, and {{jti}} replay handling.

*Steps to Reproduce*

# Configure a valid LTI 1.3 tool with a registered public key.
# Create a token request using a client assertion signed by that tool's private key.
# Omit or change required request/claim values such as {{client_assertion_type}}, {{grant_type}}, {{sub}}, {{aud}}, or reuse the same {{jti}}.
# Submit the request to Sakai's LTI 1.3 token endpoint and compare with {{handleTokenPost}} in {{lti/lti-blis/src/java/org/sakaiproject/lti13/LTI13Servlet.java}}.

*Expected Behavior*
The token endpoint should reject requests unless {{grant_type}} is {{client_credentials}}, {{client_assertion_type}} is {{urn:ietf:params:oauth:client-assertion-type:jwt-bearer}}, {{iss}} and {{sub}} match the tool client id, {{aud}} targets the token endpoint/audience, {{exp}} and {{iat}} are acceptable, and {{jti}} has not already been used.

*Actual Behavior*
{{handleTokenPost}} checks only that {{grant_type}}, {{client_assertion}}, and {{scope}} are present before parsing the assertion and verifying the signature. After signature validation it proceeds into scope processing without explicit checks for the required assertion type, exact grant type, {{iss}}/{{sub}} client id consistency, {{aud}}, or {{jti}} replay.

*Impact*
The token endpoint is not fully enforcing the LTI 1.3 / IMS Security Framework client assertion contract. Invalid or replayed signed assertions may be accepted, weakening access token issuance and causing interoperability/security failures with strict tools and platform audits.

*Environment*

* App version: Sakai trunk / LTI 1.3 token endpoint

summary: Send LTI launch locale as a BCP47 language tag
description:
*Short Description*
Sakai's LTI 1.3 launch payload emits the {{locale}} claim using Java {{Locale.toString()}}, which produces values like {{en_US}}. LTI Core 1.3 expects {{locale}} to use a BCP47 language tag, such as {{en-US}}.

*Steps to Reproduce*

# Configure and launch an LTI 1.3 tool from a Sakai site using a locale with language and region, such as English (United States).
# Inspect the LTI 1.3 launch ID token sent to the tool.
# Check the top-level {{locale}} claim.
# Compare with {{lti/lti-common/src/java/org/sakaiproject/lti/util/SakaiLTIUtil.java}}, where the locale is derived with {{rb.getLocale().toString()}} before being added to the LTI 1.3 launch payload.

*Expected Behavior*
The LTI launch should send the {{locale}} claim as a valid BCP47 language tag, for example {{en-US}}, using Sakai's effective site/user locale.

*Actual Behavior*
The launch can send Java locale-string formatting such as {{en_US}}, which is not the BCP47 format required by LTI Core 1.3.

*Impact*
LTI tools that validate the launch payload against the spec, or that depend on BCP47 locale parsing for localization, may reject the launch or choose the wrong locale. This is an interoperability and conformance issue for LTI 1.3 launches.

*Environment*

* App version: Sakai trunk / LTI 1.3 launch implementation

summary: Pinning and Unpinning results in a burst of queries to update the position of all sites
description:
When a user pins or unpins a site from the nav bar a burst of sql queries occur to update the order of all sites. This occurs because the order is 0 based and so every sites position must be renumbered.

----

Solution: Switch pinned-site POSITION to a monotonic sort key

Problem
Pinning/unpinning a site forced a full re-sequence of a user's pinned sites. Every addPinnedSite, removePinnedSite, and savePinnedSites call loaded all of a user's PinnedSite rows and rewrote each position to a contiguous 0..N index. This treated position as a dense array index, which:

* loaded and re-saved the entire pinned set on every mutation (extra queries and writes that scale with the number of pinned sites), and
* required reading all rows just to compute "the next position" when appending.

Solution
Treat POSITION purely as a monotonic sort key — values must be strictly increasing for ordering, but may contain gaps and need not be contiguous. Only the relative order matters, not the absolute values.

Changes

* New repository method findMaxPositionByUserId(userId) (PinnedSiteRepository + PinnedSiteRepositoryImpl): a Criteria max(position) query scoped to the user's currently-pinned rows (hasBeenUnpinned = false). Returns Optional.empty() when the user has no pinned sites (SQL max() over no rows yields null).
* PortalServiceImpl.addPinnedSite: when pinning, append after the current max position (max + 1, or 1 if none) instead of loading all rows and taking last + 1. Removed the re-sequencing loops in both the pin and remove paths.
* PortalServiceImpl.savePinnedSites: base new positions off the current max (max + 1) rather than off currentPinned.size() - sitesToUnpin.size(), since gaps make the count-based offset incorrect.
* Javadoc added across PinnedSiteRepository documenting that position is a gapped monotonic sort key and clarifying the pinned/unpinned semantics of each method.

Behavioral note
Positions are no longer reindexed on removal. Unpinning the middle of three sites now leaves a gap (e.g. positions 0, 2), and the next pin appends at max + 1 (3). Ordering is unchanged; only the stored values differ. The unit test in PortalServiceTests was updated to assert the gapped values.

Benefit
Pin/unpin operations no longer load and rewrite the user's entire pinned-site set — appends are a single max lookup plus one insert.

summary: Portal: dynamic variables in rich text content ({{siteterm}}, {{termstart}}, {{currentterm}}, ...) with an editor Variables dropdown
description:
Instructors often hard-code term-specific values (term name, first/final day of classes, instructor contact) into rich text content — Lessons pages, the Overview / Site Information Display, announcements, assignment instructions, syllabi. Every term rollover those values go stale and must be hunted down by hand.

This feature adds _dynamic variables_ that can be inserted anywhere the CKEditor rich text editor is used and are substituted with live values at display time, so content stays current automatically:

* _How it works:_ when {{portal.termtokens.enabled=true}} (default _false_), the portal injects a small data object ({{sakai.termsInfo}}, resolved from CourseManagement AcademicSession via the site's {{term_eid}} property) plus a substitution script into every tool page head — the same pattern MathJax uses. The script replaces an exact allowlist of {{{{token}}}} strings in the rendered DOM; stored content always keeps the raw tokens, so nothing is rewritten at save time and "current term" style values keep updating forever.
* _Authoring UX:_ a new CKEditor richcombo dropdown ("Variables") — registered globally in ckeditor.launch.js, placed between Templates and Source — lists every available variable by friendly name with a live preview of its value and an explanatory hover tooltip, grouped into categories (This Course / Term Dates / Right Now / The Reader). Instructors never type raw tokens.
* _29 variables_, including: course title, term name/code/year, first & final day of term (long + short formats), week-of-term / weeks-in-term / days-left-in-term, current term (name/code/dates — real-time, rolls over automatically, date-aware rather than relying solely on the IS_CURRENT flag), next term, instructor name/email (site contact), institution name, site link, today's date / day of week / month / year, and the reader's own name/email (computed per user, never cached).
* Values are formatted server-side in the viewer's locale and timezone (UserTimeService); term data is cached ~10 minutes per site/term/locale/timezone/day; viewer fields bypass the cache.
* The dropdown and panel are fully themed for dark mode via the Sakai design tokens, which also required theming CKEditor's dropdown panels ({{.cke_panel}}) in the default skin.
* Also fixes a latent editor caching bug: Sakai never set {{CKEDITOR.timestamp}}, so browsers cached custom editor plugins/lang files indefinitely across Sakai upgrades; it is now keyed to the portal CDN version.

Known v1 limitations (documented): substitution happens in the DOM, so email notifications, RSS feeds, and the search index see raw tokens; a server-side helper for those paths is a natural follow-up, as is a per-site "custom dates" feature for institution-specific tokens (add/drop deadline, finals week) that core Sakai has no data model for.

summary: Tests & Quizzes: feedback shown during a take is enforced client-side only (forgeable), and returns for post-deadline retakes
description:
h2. Summary

While a student is actively taking an assessment, whether feedback (correct answers, question-level feedback) is shown is decided from client-supplied input with no server-side entitlement check. The hidden "Show Feedback" link is the only thing enforcing the feedback policy, so a crafted request can reveal feedback mid-take even on a correctly configured assessment. Separately, for a post-deadline retake or forced resubmit the link legitimately reappears once the feedback date has passed, re-exposing the same leak through the normal UI.

This is the delivery-side companion to SAK-34476 (which addresses the authoring-side date validation). SAK-34476's authoring guard prevents the _misconfiguration_, but does not close this delivery-side gap, which affects even a properly configured "feedback on specific dates" assessment.

h2. Where

* {{DeliveryActionListener.setFeedbackMode(...)}} — for take / take-via-url actions it sets {{delivery.feedback = "true"}} whenever the request contains {{showfeedbacknow=true}}, with no check that feedback is actually available (no immediate-feedback / date / submission check). The feedback item JSPs then render correct answers and question-level feedback off {{delivery.feedback}} alone.
* {{DeliveryBean.getShowFeedbackLink()}} — renders the mid-take Feedback link when {{feedbackComponent.getShowImmediate() || feedbackOnDate}}. {{feedbackOnDate}} is true whenever feedback delivery is "on specific dates" and that date has passed; it is (re)computed at the start of each take, including a post-deadline retake.

h2. Impact

* A student can retrieve the instructor's answer/feedback content while still taking the assessment. "On specific dates" feedback is intended for review after submission, not during a take; only Immediate Feedback is meant to display feedback while taking.
* Reproduces on an assessment whose feedback date is correctly in the future (the show-feedback link is hidden, but the server still honors a forged {{showfeedbacknow=true}}), and through the normal UI on a post-deadline retake/resubmit once the feedback date has passed.

h2. Expected

During an active take, only Immediate Feedback should show feedback. Gate both the link ({{getShowFeedbackLink}}) and, more importantly, the server-side flag ({{setFeedbackMode}}, take modes) on Immediate Feedback for take actions, so "by date" feedback can never surface during a take and a forged parameter is ignored. Preview and review paths should be unchanged.

Affects: 23.x, 25.x, 26-SNAPSHOT (delivery code unchanged across these). A fix is available.

summary: Tests & Quizzes: button to email a student that grading/comments were updated, with bulk send
description:
h3. Problem

A common T&Q workflow: assessments are auto-graded and released immediately on submission, but essay/short-answer questions must be hand-graded later. The instructor grades them afterward and adds a grader comment — but the student has no way of knowing the manual grading happened. Nothing prompts them to come back and look; instructors resort to separate emails or announcements.

Assignments already covers its equivalent case with the per-assignment "send notification email to student when the grade is released" option; T&Q has no student-facing "your grading changed" notification at all.

h3. Proposed feature

* A small _"Email student: grading updated"_ button per submission row on the Total Scores page (next to the grader comment box) and on the individual student grading page.
* Sends a generic templated email — "Your instructor has added comments or updated the grading on <assessment> in <site>" — with a link into the site's T&Q tool. No score in the email.
* Only shown when the submission is graded and the assessment's feedback is currently visible to the student (immediate / on-submission, or feedback-by-date already reached); hidden when the assessment has no feedback.
* Re-sending later (e.g. after further comment updates) is allowed; a short cooldown and an "Email last sent: <time>" note under the button prevent accidental double-sends.
* Delivery respects the student's existing Tests & Quizzes notification preferences (immediate vs digest), reusing the standard Samigo email template pipeline (EmailTemplateService).
* _Bulk send moved to SAK-52709_, which folds the notify checkbox into a general Select column with batch actions.

h3. Test plan

# Publish an assessment with immediate (or on-submission) feedback and grades sent to gradebook; several students submit; auto-grading releases scores.
# Total Scores shows a _Notify_ column with a per-row send icon only on rows with a graded, for-grade submission. Rows with no submission show nothing; in the "All submissions" view, non-graded attempts show nothing; with feedback set to "No feedback" (or a feedback-by-date still in the future) the column is absent entirely.
# Edit an essay score / add a grader comment and click that row's send icon → pending edits are saved first, the student receives the templated email (site + assessment title + link into the site's T&Q tool, no score in the email), an event is logged, and a blue _info_ banner reports "Grading-update email sent to 1 student(s)." (not a red error banner).
# The row flips to "Sent" with "Email last sent: <date/time in the instructor's locale and time zone>" wrapped inside the slim Notify column. Clicking again during the ~1 minute cooldown is prevented; after the cooldown a re-send works and the banner counts sent vs skipped ("N skipped (notified moments ago)") correctly.
# Delivery honors each student's Tests & Quizzes notification preference: immediate → email, digest → daily digest, ignore or no email address → skipped and not counted as notified.
# The individual student grading page offers the same single send under the Comments box, and _Update & Notify_ saves exactly like Save and then sends.
# Repeat the key checks in dark mode: the info banner, notify column states, and comment boxes all render legibly.

summary: Tests & Quizzes: multi-select batch actions on Total Scores (notify / delete / adjust / comment selected)
description:
h3. Problem

The Total Scores page offers only per-row actions (delete-attempt trash icon, the new grading-updated email from SAK-52708, per-row score/comment edits). Instructors managing large rosters repeat the same action row by row. Meanwhile the tool's own Assessment List already has a working multi-select convention — a Select checkbox column plus "Remove Selected" / "Publish Selected" — and the tracker keeps asking for pieces of the same idea elsewhere (SAK-49926 wants a Select All header for the bulk-publish checkboxes, SAK-43018 wants Select All in Trash restore, SAK-34298 added bulk submission deletion).

h3. Feature (as implemented in the PR)

* A _Select_ column per submission row (absorbing the SAK-52708 notify checkbox), with a _Select All checkbox in the header_ — a first in Sakai, directly delivering what SAK-49926 asks for, in this tool.
* A collapsible _"Bulk grading & actions"_ composer above the table (collapsed state remembered per user), with a live "N selected" count:
** an _Adjustment_ field and _Comment_ box applied through one unified _Update_ button;
** an _Apply to_ target selector — Students with no submission (default; folds in the old "Apply This Score" control) / Students with a submission / Selected submissions / All participants;
** comment modes: only students without a comment (default) / append / replace;
** an _"Also email affected students"_ toggle that sends the SAK-52708 grading-updated email to just the students whose rows actually changed;
** _Delete Selected_ — the existing per-row soft delete applied to the selection, behind a count-aware confirmation, gated by the same delete permission as the trash column.
* Guard rails: above-max/negative adjustments warn first and apply only on a confirmed re-submit; hand-typed row adjustments that a bulk value would overwrite are highlighted and protected.
* Existing per-row affordances (trash icon, notify send icon, name link, per-row score/comment editing) all stay — the composer is additive.

h3. Test plan

# Publish an assessment; several students submit; open Total Scores.
# The _Bulk grading & actions_ bar sits above the table and collapses/expands; the collapsed state is remembered per user across visits. The _Select_ column's header checkbox checks/unchecks every row; the "N selected" count updates live.
# _Bulk adjustment:_ select 2–3 rows, enter an Adjustment, target "Selected submissions", click Update → a blue info banner reports "Applied to N participant(s).", the rows persist the adjustment, Final Scores update, and the gradebook reflects the change.
# _Targets:_ default "Students with no submission" matches the old Apply This Score semantics; "Students with a submission" and "All participants" apply to the right rows; ineligible rows are skipped and the banner reports the skipped count.
# _Guard rails:_ an adjustment above the max (or negative) shows a yellow warning banner first, and clicking Update again with the same value applies it; a non-numeric adjustment shows an error; "Selected submissions" with nothing selected warns; a row with a hand-typed adjustment that conflicts with the bulk value is highlighted and its typed value is kept (reported in the banner).
# _Bulk comment:_ "only students without a comment" (default) fills only empty boxes; "append" preserves existing comments and adds the new text; "replace" overwrites.
# _"Also email affected students"_ + Update → only students whose grade/comment actually changed receive the SAK-52708 email, honoring its cooldown; the notify result banner reports the count.
# _Delete Selected_ → the confirmation names the count; on accept, submissions soft-delete, rows disappear, gradebook entries clear, one delete event per row; hidden without the delete permission.
# Per-row affordances (trash, notify send icon, name link, inline edits) behave exactly as before; repeat key checks in dark mode — composer bar, banners, and conflict highlights all render legibly.

summary: T&Q: recover typed but unsaved answers from a local draft
description:
Students lose typed essay/short-answer text when a browser tab is closed, a network drop eats a save, or (with SAK-44349's guard) a stale-tab post is rejected. The text existed only in the DOM and is unrecoverable.

The CKEditor autosave plugin does not cover this in Tests & Quizzes delivery:

* its saveDetectionSelectors treat *any* form button click as a successful save and delete the stored draft — so a Next/Save click whose POST dies on a bad connection takes the draft down with it;
* its storage key embeds the page URL and the positional editor id, which are not stable across delivery renders;
* Samigo essay answers render as *plain textareas* by default (the rich-text editor is behind a toggle), which the plugin never sees.

Proposal (PR to follow): a small delivery-only script that snapshots typed answers (plain textareas and CKEditor instances) into localStorage, keyed by attempt + field + user, debounced at 2 seconds. Drafts are never deleted by button clicks; they expire after 7 days, are capped per field, and are removed once the server renders the field with confirmed content (so an intentionally cleared answer is not resurrected). On render, a draft is restored only into a field the server delivered empty, with a visible notice asking the student to review and save.

Transparency: this came out of AI-assisted work on SAK-44349 (multi-tab data loss); happy to rework or drop it if the community prefers a different approach to draft recovery.

summary: Lessons: shared "Inline Questions" gradebook item aggregating inline-question participation or correctness
description:
h2. Problem

Each graded Lessons inline Question item creates its own external gradebook column, and there is no way to share one column across questions or to grade participation across a page/site. Instructors who embed many inline questions and want a single "did the student engage" score have to spot-check by hand.

h2. What this adds

A single, site-wide gradebook item aggregated across a site's inline Question items:

* _Membership_ — each question can be included from its edit dialog; a "More Tools → Inline Question Gradebook Item" dialog also bulk-includes every question on the page or in the site (retroactive), and can auto-include newly created questions.
* _Scoring modes_ — participation (answered at all) or correctness (answered correctly). For manually-graded short-answer/essay questions in correctness mode, the instructor chooses whether any answer earns full credit or the question's own manual grade carries over as partial credit.
* _Item worth_ — either a per-question point value (item max grows with the count) or a fixed total, where each question counts as an equal percentage of that total (so the item's weight stays constant as questions are added).
* _Due date_ — shown on the gradebook item and surfaced in Date Manager under the Lessons section; a scheduled final recompute runs shortly after it passes.

Scores are always recomputed from stored responses (never incremented), so re-answers, regrades, and instructor overrides stay consistent; the configuration and membership flags carry through site duplication so the item arrives ready each term. Group-restricted questions are excluded (out-of-group students could never earn those shares). Not supported with per-group gradebooks.

h2. Implementation

Pure scoring logic in {{QuestionAggregateCalculator}} (api, unit-tested); settings/membership/scoring/the scheduled final pass in a component-level {{QuestionAggregateService}}; UI in the Lessons tool; Date Manager integration in site-manage.

summary: CKEditor: dark theme is lost when the editor document is recreated (white edit area on reopen)
description:
h2. Symptom

In dark mode a CKEditor edit area can render with a white background even though the surrounding page is dark. Reproducible by editing a Lessons inline Question item (the "Question Text" box is white), in a clean browser profile, and on production — so it is not stale cached CSS.

h2. Root cause

The dark-theme class is added to the editor iframe by a {{CKEDITOR.once('instanceReady', ...)}} handler in library/.../editor/ckeditor.launch.js. {{once}} themes only the first editor instance on the page; and even that instance loses the class whenever CKEditor rebuilds the editable document (mode switch, setData, a dialog reopening a reused instance) — so reopening a Lessons dialog to edit a question shows a white edit area.

h2. Fix

Theme every instance on instanceReady and re-apply on contentDom, which fires each time the editable document is (re)created (covering the old mode-switch handler). Relates to SAK-44562.

summary: Skin: unchecked Bootstrap check inputs render white in dark mode
description:
h2. Symptom

In dark mode, unchecked checkboxes/radios that use Bootstrap's {{.form-check-input}} class render with a white background — e.g. the Lessons checklist boxes glare white on a dark page.

h2. Root cause

The skin ({{library/.../sass/base/_defaults.scss}}) themes the _checked_ and _disabled_ states of checkboxes/radios but never sets an _unchecked_ background, so Bootstrap's {{--bs-form-check-bg}} (white) shows through on {{.form-check-input}} elements.

h2. Fix

Set the unchecked background to transparent on the shared checkbox/radio rule so it matches plain inputs. Light theme is unaffected.

summary: Tests & Quizzes: Total Scores disabled comment boxes render near-white in dark mode
description:
h2. Symptom

On the Tests & Quizzes Total Scores page in dark mode, the "Requires student submission" comment boxes (disabled textareas for rows with no submission) paint near-white, e.g. after sorting by Comments so the plain (non-awesomplete) variant renders.

h2. Root cause

An inline {{.disabled { background-color:#f1f1f1 }}} rule in totalScores.jsp is a light-mode grey with no dark-mode override.

h2. Fix

Mirror the {{.disabled}} rule under {{.sakaiUserTheme-dark}} with theme-aware colours.

summary: CKEditor: toolbar collapse/expand control is not themed in dark mode
description:
Follow-up to SAK-52714 (which fixed the white _edit area_ on document recreate, merged in #14748). This is a distinct visible symptom on the same editor.

*Problem:* The Lessons inline Question Text editor starts with a collapsed toolbar, so its collapse/expand control is prominent. In dark mode that control renders with a white background, and once the toolbar is expanded its arrow disappears (dark #333 arrow on the dark toolbar).

*Cause:* The collapser ({{.cke_toolbox_collapser}}) is styled by the Sakai skin ({{tool.css}}) for light mode only — white background, {{#333}} arrow. The dark-theme {{chameleon}} skin override in {{ckeditor.launch.js}} themes the toolbar, buttons, combos, elements-path and dialogs, but never touched the collapser.

*Fix:* Extend the chameleon override to theme the collapser background and border, and recolor its arrow to the theme text color — preserving {{tool.css}}'s arrow geometry (right when the toolbar is collapsed, down when expanded).

summary: Lessons: answer inline questions without a full page reload
description:
h2. Problem

Answering an inline *Question* item on a Lessons page (multiple choice, short answer, or poll) currently round-trips and *reloads the whole page*. On a long Lessons page with several questions this is disruptive — the page jumps, scroll position is lost, and every other item re-renders just to record one answer.

h2. Change

Submit the answer over AJAX using the tool's existing RSF UVB mechanism (the same pattern the checklist "mark complete" and grading forms already use), so the answer is still recorded and graded server-side while only that question updates in place — its status icon, feedback text, and (for polls) the results graph render inline, with no page reload.

Two related clarity improvements are included:

* *Clearer status labels.* A question that defines an answer key now reads *"Correct"* or *"Incorrect"* when answered, instead of the generic "Completed"/"Failed". Polls and participation-only questions (no answer key) keep *"Completed"*. Applied consistently to both the server render and the new AJAX path.
* *Survey/grading help.* The *"Select Correct Answer(s)"* header in the question editor now has a tooltip explaining that leaving every option unchecked makes the question a survey (any answer accepted), or — when a grade is assigned — marks it for manual grading.

h2. Verification

Exercised end-to-end on a dev stack as a student: answering multiple-choice and short-answer questions updates the status/feedback in place with no page reload; a correctly answered graded question shows "Correct", a wrong one "Incorrect", and a survey answer "Completed"; participation is still recorded and graded server-side exactly as before.

summary: Announcements: read receipts — see which students have viewed an announcement
description:
h2. Summary

Instructors have no way to see who has actually read an announcement. Sakai already posts a per-user {{annc.read}} event whenever a student opens an announcement's detail view, but nothing surfaces it.

This adds a *"View read receipts"* link next to the Revise action on each announcement. It opens a modal with one sortable table of the site's students showing, per student, whether they have *viewed* the announcement in Sakai (with the first-viewed time) and whether they have *email notifications enabled* for announcements. Rows are colour-coded (optional, on by default, toggleable): *green* = viewed; *yellow* = not viewed but email on (may have seen it via the email); *red* = not viewed and email off (likely has not seen it at all).

A disclaimer notes that receipts reflect *in-Sakai views only* — a recipient who read the announcement solely through the email notification is not counted.

h2. Implementation notes

* Reuses the existing {{annc.read}} event (no new tracking mechanism); an {{EventTrackingService}} observer persists it to a small {{ANNC_READ_RECEIPT}} table (message reference, user id, first-viewed time), keeping the earliest view and ignoring re-reads.
* The read event is also posted from the REST {{getAnnouncement}} single-item path so full-body REST reads are captured (the tool, the Overview/synoptic widget, and the dashboard widget already post it).
* The reader/non-reader lists are filtered to students; the email column is resolved from each user's {{sakai:announcement}} notification preference.
* Colours are theme-aware and high-contrast (WCAG AA) in both light and dark mode.

h2. Known limitations (documented, out of scope for a first pass)

* Only reads occurring after deploy are captured (no backfill).
* For a group-restricted announcement the "not yet viewed" list is site-wide rather than intersected with the message's groups.
* The synoptic widget's optional inline trimmed-body preview (when configured to show bodies) has no per-message hook and is treated as not-a-full-read.

summary: LTI dynamic registration import depends on close postMessage and final save
description:
*Summary*
Dynamic registration stores the registration response JSON in {{lti13_auto_registration}} and marks the registration complete, but does not populate the active tool fields used by the token endpoint and OIDC launch configuration. As a result, a newly dynamically registered LTI 1.3 tool cannot obtain an LTI Advantage service token.

*Environment*

* Sakai trunk / 26-SNAPSHOT
* Local Sakai exposed with Cloudflare Tunnel
* LTI harness: https://lti-conformance-harness.ottenhoff-1f2.workers.dev
* Harness dynamic registration endpoint: https://lti-conformance-harness.ottenhoff-1f2.workers.dev/register

*How we found it*
We were testing dynamic registration and token endpoint behavior using a minimal LTI 1.3 conformance harness backed by Cloudflare Workers. The harness dynamically registered as a tool, then sent a valid {{private_key_jwt}} client credentials request to Sakai's token endpoint. Sakai returned a token endpoint error before validating the harness key.

*Expected*
Dynamic registration should populate the active LTI 1.3 tool fields required by later protocol operations, including:

* {{lti13_tool_keyset}} from registration {{jwks_uri}}
* {{lti13_oidc_endpoint}} from registration {{initiate_login_uri}}
* {{lti13_oidc_redirect}} from registration {{redirect_uris}}
* {{deployment_id}} from the LTI tool configuration deployment id

The token endpoint should be able to retrieve the registered tool public key and validate a valid {{client_assertion}}.

*Actual*
The valid token request fails with:

{code:json}{ "error": "Public key retrieval failed" }{code}

Sakai log:

{noformat}ERROR o.s.l.LTI13Servlet.handleTokenPost Error getting public key
java.lang.RuntimeException: Could not find tool keyset url
    at org.sakaiproject.lti.util.SakaiLTIUtil.getPublicKey(SakaiLTIUtil.java:1359)
    at org.sakaiproject.lti.util.SakaiLTIUtil.getPublicKey(SakaiLTIUtil.java:1388)
    at org.sakaiproject.lti13.LTI13Servlet.handleTokenPost(LTI13Servlet.java:885){noformat}

Database state immediately after registration:

{noformat}lti13_auto_state = 2
lti13_auto_registration contains jwks_uri = https://lti-conformance-harness.ottenhoff-1f2.workers.dev/jwks
lti13_tool_keyset = NULL
lti13_oidc_endpoint = NULL
lti13_oidc_redirect = NULL
deployment_id = NULL{noformat}

The harness JWKS endpoint is publicly reachable and returns HTTP 200, so this is not a network failure retrieving the Worker JWKS. Sakai has no stored keyset URL for the dynamically registered tool.

*Code Pointers*

* {{lti/lti-blis/src/java/org/sakaiproject/lti13/LTI13Servlet.java}}: {{handleRegistrationEndpointPost}} extracts {{initiate_login_uri}}, {{jwks_uri}}, and {{redirect_uris}}, stores the JSON in {{tool.lti13AutoRegistration}}, and marks {{tool.lti13AutoState = 2}}, but does not map those values into the active {{LtiToolBean}} fields.
* {{lti/lti-common/src/java/org/sakaiproject/lti/util/SakaiLTIUtil.java}}: {{getPublicKey}} reads {{LTIService.LTI13_TOOL_KEYSET}} and throws {{Could not find tool keyset url}} when it is null.

summary: EntityBroker may commit HTTP response before response headers are configured for ActionReturn.outputString
description:
When an {{[user]}} returns an {{ActionReturn}} with {{outputString}} set, the response body is written before the response encoding and content type are configured.

Writing to the response output stream may commit the HTTP response (for example, when the response buffer is exceeded), preventing subsequent response header changes from taking effect.

This can lead to incorrect handling of downloads, such as CSV exports being displayed in the browser instead of being downloaded, depending on the response size and servlet container behavior.

*Proposed fix:*

Configure the response (encoding/content type) before writing {{ActionReturn.outputString}} to the output stream.

summary: Prevent LTI 1.3 JWKS rotation caused by stale Ignite cache name
description:
*Short Description*
The fix from [SAK-52379|https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-52379], commit {{46ba8af3c01406de87dafbbecc78f3fabd830134}}, configures the pre-SAK-50500 cache name {{org.sakaiproject.basiclti.util.SakaiKeySetUtil_cache}}. Sakai 25 requests {{org.sakaiproject.lti.util.SakaiKeySetUtil_cache}}, so Ignite dynamically creates it with the default 120-minute expiry and the JWKS keys are regenerated.

*Steps to Reproduce*

# Deploy Sakai 25 with the SAK-52379 fix.
# Request {{/imsblis/lti13/keyset}} and save the returned keyset and KIDs.
# Keep the Sakai/Ignite cluster running without a restart for more than 120 minutes.
# Request {{/imsblis/lti13/keyset}} again and compare it with the original response.

*Expected Behavior*
The keyset remains stable and rotates only according to {{lti.advantage.key.rotation.days}}, which defaults to 30 days.

*Actual Behavior*
The runtime cache is not matched by the eternal cache declaration. Its entries expire after 120 minutes, causing Sakai to bootstrap replacement public/private keys and change the JWKS KIDs.

*Impact*
LTI 1.3 launches can intermittently fail with invalid-signature or key-not-found errors when tools retain a previously fetched JWKS response.

*Environment*

* App version: Sakai 25.x
* Previous fix: SAK-52379 / {{46ba8af3c01406de87dafbbecc78f3fabd830134}}
* Package rename: SAK-50500

summary: Improve Turnitin email spoofing to avoid unnecessary user updates
description:
The current Turnitin integration supports the {{spoilEmailAddresses}} configuration option to avoid sending real user email addresses to Turnitin.

When enabled, the current implementation generates a randomized email address on every request. For example:

{noformat}[email]{noformat}

may become:

{noformat}[email]{noformat}

on one request and:

{noformat}[email]{noformat}

on the next request.

Since the Turnitin API receives the user identifier together with the email address, Turnitin treats these requests as user updates. This results in frequent unnecessary email updates for the same user and causes additional load on the Turnitin infrastructure.

Turnitin has reported that these frequent updates are generating unnecessary server load.

This issue proposes introducing a configurable email spoofing strategy while keeping the existing behavior fully backwards compatible.

The proposed strategies are:

* RANDOM (current behavior)
** Generates a new randomized email address on every request.
** Remains the default when {{spoilEmailAddresses=true}} is configured and no new strategy is specified.
* DETERMINISTIC (new behavior)
** Generates a stable pseudonymized email address derived from the Sakai user identifier.
** The generated email remains identical across requests, avoiding unnecessary Turnitin user updates.
* ORIGINAL
** Uses the original email address without modification.

Existing installations will not change behavior unless they explicitly opt into the new deterministic strategy.

# *Class-time change* — my section moved from 2:00 PM to 9:00 AM, so everything that opens at class start needs a new time of day across the whole term.

Today both mean editing every cell by hand; the bulk tools can't express a time-only change (the shifter works in whole days, and the column setters overwrite the full date+time).

* *A "Set times of day" bulk method* — pick a time, tick which kinds of date columns it applies to (Open/Start, Due/End, Accept-until, Feedback), and use the same "Apply to:" tool scope as the other bulk methods. Dates stay exactly as they are, items with no date are skipped, and Gradebook (date-only) is never touched. Same post-apply summary banner as the other methods.
* *A "set time only" mode on the per-column header setters* in the item grid, for surgical one-column fixes.

Depends on SAK-52598's PR #14726 landing first — implementation will start once that merges. Branch is prepared locally.

summary: Worksite Setup - Stuck on Create Site screen after navigating away to another tool and returning
description:
When you go to Worksite Setup -> Create New Site, you are taken to the "Create Site" screen. If you then navigate to another tool and click on Worksite Setup again, you'll get stuck on that "Create Site" screen every time you access Worksite Setup. If you click the "Continue" or "Cancel" button, you'll be sent back to Overview rather than continuing or canceling the setup.

summary: Kernel: Eliminate N+1 DB queries and cache thrashing in BaseAuthzGroupService bulk authorization
description:
h3. Problem Description
In Sakai sites with a very large number of enrollments (e.g., 5,000+ users), permission and authorization checks trigger an N+1 database query loop inside {{BaseAuthzGroupService}}.
Specifically, methods such as {{getAuthzGroupsIsAllowed}} and {{getUsersIsAllowed}} query the database individually for each user or group, resulting in thousands of redundant JDBC calls per page request and causing severe database thread contention.

h3. Solution & Changes

# *Bulk Fetching:* Refactored {{getAuthzGroupsIsAllowed}} and {{getUsersIsAllowed}} to retrieve permissions using bulk SQL queries ({{IN}} clause / batch checking), reducing query complexity from O(N) to O(1).
# *Cache Optimization:* Optimized {{authzUserGroupIdsCache}} to eliminate cache thrashing and repetitive invalidation overhead during large bulk authorization lookups.

h3. Impact

* Eliminates ~5,000+ individual JDBC queries during site/tool permission lookups in large courses.
* Greatly improves overall Sakai responsiveness and reduces database CPU load.

summary: Gradebook: Eliminate N+1 DB queries and optimize grade matrix loading for large courses
description:
h3. Problem Description
When accessing the main Gradebook page or Quick Entry page in courses with thousands of enrolled students (e.g., 5,000+ enrollments), the tool experiences severe rendering delays and timeouts.
The bottleneck is caused by N+1 database queries when fetching student enrollment details, grade items, and permissions sequentially inside loops during grade matrix construction ({{buildGradeMatrix}}).

h3. Solution & Changes

# *Quick Entry & Main Page Bulk Fetching:* Refactored enrollment and grade retrieval logic in {{QuickEntryPage}} and the main Gradebook views to bulk-fetch student grade scores in a single query map (O(1)).
# *Grade Matrix Optimization:* Optimized permissions and matrix assembly in {{buildGradeMatrix}} to avoid repeated per-user authorization checks.
# *StopWatch Monitoring:* Integrated {{GbStopWatch}} utility to allow detailed execution-time tracing of matrix build phases in logs.

h3. Impact

* Reduces database queries on Gradebook load from ~10,000+ queries down to single-digit bulk queries.
* Enables smooth page rendering and quick-entry grading for 5,000+ enrollment courses.

summary: Standardize user display name resolution across Sakai
description:
User names are currently displayed in different ways across Sakai. While some tools use {{User.getDisplayName()}}, others build the display name directly from user properties or use alternative approaches.

This inconsistency can result in different representations of the same user depending on the tool being used and makes it difficult to provide a consistent user experience across the platform.

The objective of this improvement is to standardize how user display names are obtained throughout Sakai by establishing {{User.getDisplayName()}} as the canonical API for displaying a user's name in the user interface.

As part of this work, Sakai tools should be reviewed to ensure they consistently use the standard API when displaying user names.

summary: Calendar iCal export uses DURATION instead of DTEND causing import failures with many clients
description:
The Calendar tool's iCal export method (generateICal in BaseCalendarService) generates events using the DURATION property instead of DTEND. While DURATION is technically valid per RFC 5545, many iCal consumers — including Sakai's own IcalendarReader — do not implement DURATION parsing and silently skip events that lack a DTEND property.

The fix is to replace the DURATION-based VEvent constructor with one that uses explicit DTSTART and DTEND DateTime values, derived from event.getRange().firstTime() and event.getRange().lastTime() respectively, with proper TZID attributes on both properties.

summary: Prevent oversized LTI 1.3 deep-linking launch tokens
description:
*Short Description*
Sakai copies OIDC transport parameters into the LTI 1.3 Deep Linking {{data}} claim and carries a fully encoded portal callback in {{deep_link_return_url}}, producing unnecessarily large launch tokens. The issue was discovered with ACS Content Controller when its internal redirect wrapper expanded a valid Sakai launch beyond CloudFront's maximum URL length.

*Steps to Reproduce*

# Configure a local, vendor-neutral LTI 1.3 test tool that supports OIDC login and {{LtiDeepLinkingRequest}}. The test tool must accept Sakai's form-posted {{id_token}}, decode and record claim sizes, and return a correctly signed {{LtiDeepLinkingResponse}} to Sakai using form POST.
# Have the test tool issue representative OIDC authorization parameters matching the observed case: a {{state}} of approximately 320 characters, a {{redirect_uri}} of approximately 200 characters, and a 36-character {{nonce}}. Make these lengths configurable so the test can demonstrate that tool-supplied OIDC parameter length does not inflate platform-owned deep-link state.
# From Lessons, add content using the configured external tool. Repeat through the Assignments deep-linking placement.
# At the test tool's launch endpoint, record the UTF-8 byte size of the decoded launch payload, the signed JWT, {{deep_linking_settings.data}}, and {{deep_linking_settings.deep_link_return_url}}. Do not log claim values or user data.
# Inspect {{deep_linking_settings.data}}. It currently contains the OIDC {{state}}, {{redirect_uri}}, and {{nonce}}, along with {{flow}} and a production sample value such as {{"remember":"the answer is 42"}}.
# Inspect {{deep_link_return_url}}. In the observed Lessons flow it was 835 characters, including a 756-character {{forward}} value containing an encoded portal callback, session association, CSRF token, flow, tool ID, and return URL.
# Complete the flow by having the test tool post a valid deep-link response and verify that Sakai creates the selected content item.

*Expected Behavior*
Sakai should keep LTI 1.3 deep-linking launches compact while preserving the full workflow and security properties.

The vendor-neutral tests should verify that OIDC {{state}}, {{redirect_uri}}, and {{nonce}} are not copied into {{deep_linking_settings.data}}; production launch data contains no sample {{remember}} values; and the optional {{data}} claim is either omitted or contains a short, opaque, single-use correlation value that is validated when returned.

{{deep_link_return_url}} should contain a bounded, random, short-lived state handle instead of a nested encoded callback. Associated return URL, user/session association, site, tool, flow, and CSRF context should be stored in an appropriate shared Sakai session/cache service, not static, singleton, or thread-local state. The full Lessons and Assignments flows must continue to accept valid responses, while replayed, expired, cross-user, cross-site, or wrong-tool handles are rejected.

*Actual Behavior*
{{LTISecurityServiceImpl}} copies nearly every request parameter except {{contentReturn}} into {{propData}}. {{SakaiLTIUtil.postContentItemSelectionRequest}} serializes unrecognized entries from that map into {{deep_linking_settings.data}}. {{LTIAdminTool}} also adds literal sample {{remember}} values in production code. The response parser requires a non-empty returned {{data}} claim but stores it in a shadowing local variable and does not retain or compare it.

In the captured launch:

* The decoded Sakai deep-link payload was 4,671 bytes.
* {{deep_linking_settings}} was 1,958 bytes.
* {{deep_link_return_url}} was 835 characters.
* {{data}} was 653 characters, including a 320-character OIDC state, a 200-character ACS redirect URI, and a 36-character nonce.
* ACS placed the original request in an internal wrapper and duplicated the return URL and data. Its resulting GET URL was 9,114 characters, including a 9,064-character JWT query value.
* CloudFront rejected that URL with HTTP 414 because its documented maximum URL length is 8,192 bytes: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/RequestAndResponseBehaviorCustomOrigin.html#RequestCustomMaxLength

Filtering the three OIDC parameters from Sakai's {{data}} claim projects the observed downstream URL to approximately 7,445 characters. Replacing the encoded callback with a short server-side state handle as well projects it to approximately 5,343 characters. These projections illustrate the benefit but must not be implemented or tested against ACS-specific behavior.

The LTI Deep Linking specification defines {{data}} as optional and requires it to be returned only when the platform supplies it: https://www.imsglobal.org/spec/lti-dl/v2p0/

*Impact*
Valid LTI 1.3 deep-linking launches can fail when a tool or intermediary carries launch state through infrastructure with common URL limits. The failure currently prevents instructors from selecting and adding ACS content in Lessons, and similar failures can affect other vendors whose internal workflows amplify platform-provided state. The current implementation also makes Sakai launch size depend on arbitrary tool-generated OIDC parameter lengths and unnecessarily round-trips protocol and session-related data.

*Environment*

* App version: Sakai master/trunk
* Flow reproduced: Lessons LTI 1.3 Deep Linking; Assignments should be included in regression coverage
* Discovery vendor: ACS Content Controller / ScormEngine dispatch integration
* Edge infrastructure: Amazon CloudFront, 8,192-byte maximum URL

description:
We use the Sakai Web Service to copy over content from template sites, as a manual “import from Site” would not be feasible. I noticed that with Sakai 25 the behavior of the “copySiteContent” method in the SakaiScript class changed significantly . And it is very different now to the “import from Site“ functionality.

Steps to reproduce:

* create a source sakai site with some tools
** overview tool → double column layout and widgets
** lessons tool with some content
** resources tool with content
** Discussion with some forums and topics
** Web Content with a URL
* Create 2 Destination Sakai Sites
** #1
*** Site Info tool only
** #2
*** Overview tool → double column layout
*** Lessons tool
*** Discussion tool
*** Resources tool
*** Web content tool with a URL
* Use this simple script to import via WebService “copySiteContent“
** {code:python}from zeep import Client

name = "admin"
pw = "admin"


*## sakai nightly
serverUrl = "https://trunk-maria.nightly.sakaiproject.org"

loginUrl = serverUrl + "/sakai-ws/soap/login?wsdl"
scriptUrl = serverUrl + "/sakai-ws/soap/sakai?wsdl"

loginProxy = Client(loginUrl)
scriptProxy = Client(scriptUrl)

*###################################################
sourceSiteId = ""

destinationSiteId = ""
*###################################################

sessionId = loginProxy.service.login(name, pw)
print("sessionId: " + sessionId)
result = scriptProxy.service.copySiteContent(sessionId, sourceSiteId, destinationSiteId)

print("Copy site from {0} to {1} was a {2}".format(sourceSiteId, destinationSiteId, result)){code}



The Destination Site show the following behaviour in my tests with the WebService

* #1
** Overview tool added (but not checked in “manage tools“; no tool title; no content imported; widgets added as separate tools (can only be removed via “tool order“
** Lessons tool added → default title; no content imported
** Resources tool added → no content imported
** Web Content Tool added → empty page title; default tool title; missing URL
** Discussion tool added → not imported

When using the “import from Site“ with #1, then no overview tool is added and all the other mentioned tools are added and content is imported
* #2
** Overview content not imported
** Lesson  content not imported
** Resources  content not imported
** Discussion content not imported
** Web Content content not imported

** When using the “import from Site“ with #2, then everything is correctly imported



Did anything change with Sakai 25 regarding the usage of the Web Service that we might have missed?
Is the difference in behavior between the Web Service and the Import from Site functionality intentional?

summary: Rubrics: Deleting a rubric leaves orphaned criterion outcome records
Rubrics: Database conversion leaves obsolete foreign keys that prevent rubric deletion after upgrade
description:
When upgrading to Sakai 25, existing Rubrics database constraints from older Sakai versions can prevent deleting rubrics that have been used for grading.



Fresh Sakai 25 databases created with auto.ddl=true do not contain these foreign key constraints, and rubric deletion succeeds. However, upgraded databases retain legacy foreign keys that reference rubric criterion outcome tables. These constraints are no longer present in the Sakai 25 schema and prevent the application from completing rubric deletion.



Example constraints found in an upgraded Sakai 25 database:



rbc_criterion_outcome.criterion_id

references rbc_criterion.id

constraint: FK_h43853lsee9xsay4qlic80pkv



rbc_returned_criterion_out.criterion_id

references rbc_criterion.id

constraint: fk_rbc_returned_criterion_id



Removing these constraints allows the rubric deletion workflow to complete successfully.



This appears to be a database conversion issue where obsolete Rubrics foreign keys from previous Sakai versions are not removed during upgrade.

summary: SCORM: Use EID instead of UUID
description:
The SCORM player populates {{cmi.learner_id}} with internal Sakai user ID instead of institutional ID (eid).

The SCORM 2004 data model element {{cmi.learner_id}} is currently populated with the learner's internal Sakai user ID (UUID), rather than their institutional ID (eid/displayId). This makes the value meaningless to receiving SCO content that expects a human-readable or institution-recognizable learner identifier — for example, a certificate of completion generated inside the SCO that displays the learner's ID back to them.

*Current behavior:*

In {{ScormApplicationServiceImpl.java}}, at SCO launch, {{cmi.learner_id}} is set as follows:

java

{noformat}element = CMI_LEARNER_ID;
DMInterface.processSetValue(element, learner.getId(), true, ioSCOData, validatorFactory);{noformat}

{{learner.getId()}} returns the internal Sakai UUID (e.g. {{ed1b5029-c40d-4f7d-9941-7cca9f33ea48}}), which is not meaningful outside the Sakai instance and is not the value students or staff recognize as their institutional ID (e.g. student0011).

*Relevant existing data:*

The {{Learner}} model ({{org.sakaiproject.scorm.model.api.Learner}}) already includes a {{displayId}} field, populated elsewhere from {{user.getDisplayId()}} (the Sakai eid), but it is currently only used internally for the tool's own reporting/results screens — it is never passed into the SCORM data model exposed to the SCO.

*Expected/requested behavior:*

{{cmi.learner_id}} should be populated with {{learner.getDisplayId()}} instead of {{learner.getId()}}, so SCO content that reads the SCORM-standard learner ID field receives the institution's recognizable ID rather than an opaque internal UUID.

*Proposed fix:*

java

{noformat}element = CMI_LEARNER_ID;
DMInterface.processSetValue(element, learner.getDisplayId(), true, ioSCOData, validatorFactory);{noformat}

*Rationale:*

* The SCORM 2004 spec explicitly leaves assignment of {{cmi.learner_id}} up to the LMS, with the only requirement being uniqueness within the SCO's scope — the eid satisfies this and is the institutionally meaningful value.
* No new data collection or schema change is required; {{displayId}} is already retrieved and available on the {{Learner}} object at the point {{cmi.learner_id}} is set.
* This affects any SCO built to personalize content using the learner ID passed via SCORM (e.g., certificates of completion, printed transcripts within a course).
