summary: Date Manager: Display correct Gradebook item weekdays across DST changes
description:
*Short Description*

Date Manager displays the previous day of the week for Gradebook item due dates when the browser's current UTC offset differs from the offset that applies to the due date. This is reproducible for dates in the U.S. standard-time period when testing during daylight saving time.

*Steps to Reproduce*

# Set the browser and operating-system timezone to {{America/New_York}}.
# Perform the test while the current date is in daylight saving time.
# Log in to Sakai as an instructor.
# Open a course containing the Gradebook and Site Info tools.
# In Gradebook, add items with due dates of October 31, 2026; November 1, 2026; November 2, 2026; January 15, 2027; March 14, 2027; and March 15, 2027.
# Confirm that Gradebook displays the entered due dates.
# Open Site Info, select Date Manager, and expand the Gradebook section.
# Compare the day-of-week label beneath each due date with a calendar.

*Expected Behavior*

Date Manager displays the weekday belonging to each Gradebook due date. For the dates above, the labels are Saturday, Sunday, Monday, Friday, Sunday, and Monday respectively.

*Actual Behavior*

Gradebook items whose due dates use the standard-time offset can display the previous weekday. Dates using the same offset as the browser's current date display the expected weekday.

*Impact*

Instructors see misleading weekday information while reviewing or changing Gradebook due dates in Date Manager. This can cause an instructor to move a due date unnecessarily or schedule work for the wrong day.

*Environment*

* App version: Sakai 25.x and current master
* Browser/OS timezone: a timezone that observes DST; reproduced with {{America/New_York}}
* Current date: daylight saving period

summary: Lessons: Embedding non sakai local content via url does override style classes and break settings
description:
In the *Lessons* tool, content can be added using *Add Content → Embed Content on the Page*.

When the embedded resource is an external web link, meaning it is not local to Sakai, the CSS/classes or item attributes appear to be modified incorrectly. As a result, some display settings can no longer be changed or saved, such as ( Height, Width, Item description)

The settings can be entered in the edit dialog, but they are not persisted after saving.



h3. Steps to Reproduce

# Create a site with the *Lessons* tool.
# Go to *Lessons*.
# Select *Add Content → Embed Content on the Page* → *Add New URL*
# Enter a non-Sakai local URL, e.g. public external website URL.
# Save the item.
# Edit the embedded item.
# Enter values for *width* and *height*.
# Save the changes.
# Reopen the item settings.


The previously entered width and height values are not saved.

h3. Console Logs

The browser console shows an error when this occurs.

{noformat}Uncaught TypeError: can't access property "nodeName", row.find(...).get(...) is undefined{noformat}




*_ShowPageproducer.printSubpage()_*


{noformat}if (!IframeUrlUtil.isLocalToSakai(itemUrl,
ServerConfigurationService.getServerUrl())) {
            item.decorate(new UIFreeAttributeDecorator("sakai-iframe-force-light"));
  }{noformat}

The problem seems to be that {{UIFreeAttributeDecorator}} overrides the already existing classes. Changing it to {{UIStyleDecorator}} seems to fix the issue.

summary: Preserve SameSite on non-HttpOnly Sakai session cookies
description:
*Short Description*
When {{sakai.cookieHttpOnly=false}}, Sakai ignores {{sakai.cookieSameSite}} and emits {{SAKAIID}} without a SameSite attribute. Embedded LTI 1.3 launches can consequently lose the authenticated Sakai session during the OIDC round trip and redirect to the login container.

*Steps to Reproduce*

# Configure an HTTPS Sakai instance with {{sakai.cookieHttpOnly=false}} and {{sakai.cookieSameSite=none}}.
# Restart Sakai and clear the browser's Sakai cookies.
# Load the portal and inspect the {{Set-Cookie}} response header for {{SAKAIID}}.
# Observe that {{SAKAIID}} contains {{Secure}} but does not contain {{SameSite=None}}.
# Launch an LTI 1.3 tool configured to open in an iframe.
# Observe that an OIDC callback without the Sakai session is redirected to {{/sakai-login-tool/container}}.

*Expected Behavior*
The {{SAKAIID}} cookie honors {{sakai.cookieSameSite}} independently of the {{sakai.cookieHttpOnly}} value, allowing the authenticated session to survive supported cross-site LTI launch flows.

*Actual Behavior*
Sakai delegates cookie creation to the servlet container whenever {{sakai.cookieHttpOnly=false}}, so the configured SameSite value is omitted from {{SAKAIID}}.

*Impact*
Sites that disable HttpOnly cannot apply Sakai's SameSite configuration. This can break embedded LTI 1.3 launches and other cross-site session flows.

*Environment*

* App version: Sakai master
* Browser: current Chrome or another browser enforcing SameSite-by-default
* Deployment: HTTPS

summary: LTI: Manual Deployment Form Enhancement for Deployment group
description:
Universities sometimes buy a license for only a specific school/department and it would be painful to have to add the entire list for that school/department manually. If an LTI tool needs to be deployed to a school/department, those site IDs can be pulled from the database and be automatically added to the Site IDs, saving the admin a lot of time.

Once a stealthed tool has been added and the admin clicks the Deployment # on the External Tools page, (there’s an inconsistency when trying to add a site while creating the tool: [https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-52592|https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-52592|smart-link] ), Manual Tool Deployment page displays with a Deploy Tool to Sites button. Initially, if no sites have the tool added, this page displays “The tool is not available in any sites”. 

Clicking Deploy Tool to Sites displays the Manual Tool Deployment form with the following fields: Notes, Deployment group (optional) and Site Ids.

Currently, a Deployment group can be added which will add a deployment ID to all sites entered in the form.

Proposal:

* Beside the Deployment group (optional), add the “i” icon for a pop-up explaining deployment groups
* Add a Select School/Department drop-down with the values pulled from the database

!image-20260817-203218.png|width=709,alt="image-20260817-203218.png"!

The Deployment Group section could have these side-by-side instead of each element taking up the entire width.

Both, adding a deployment group or selecting a school, are optional:

* Adding only a deployment group would require site IDs be added
* Selecting a school/department would load all the sites for that school/dept
** If the deployment group is blank, all these sites would use the school/department value for the deployment ID
** If the deployment group contains a value, then all the sites would use the deployment group as the deployment ID

*Deployment group*: works as it does currently, the user enters a value then enters site IDs below and those sites will have that deployment value.

*Select school*: If a school/dept is selected, then the Site IDs should automatically populate with every site in that school/dept. If needed, the admin can remove any not to be included.

The External Tools Deployments table needs to be updated also. 

* If the Deployment group is null, but a school/department exists for the course, that should show in the table under Deployment Group. (Currently, it does not. Only if something has been entered as the Deployment group does it show in that table.)
* If the above idea is implemented and a school/department is selected, all sites that populate the Site Ids field (and are kept) should show the school/department ID unless the Deployment group has been filled out also, then they would all have the Deployment group as the deployment ID.
* If a site has no school/department and no Deployment group has been added, the deployment ID defaults to 1. In the table, this would result as a blank under Deployment group and makes sense.

!image-20260817-204114.png|width=709,alt="image-20260817-204114.png"!

Testing information with the current setup and proposed changes: [https://docs.google.com/document/d/1k6Hnixfh0WV-_1R1O4puNKMCeCo1xeXQjTlePBo6A-g/edit?usp=sharing|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1k6Hnixfh0WV-_1R1O4puNKMCeCo1xeXQjTlePBo6A-g/edit?usp=sharing|smart-link]

summary: Enter Student/Access View Does Not Fully Respect “Display to Selected” Group Visibility
description:
Enter Student View / Enter Access does not fully respect selected groups via “display to selected” for items in several tools.

I have tested this in Lessons, Resources, and Announcements and found the following behavior:

For example, in Lessons, create an item and restrict its visibility to a group where the current instructor is not a member. Then activate Enter Student/Access View. The item is not visible in the Student/Access View.

If the current instructor is part of the selected group, the items are also visible in Enter Student/Access View. 
If the instructor is not part of the selected group, the items are not visible.

This has caused some confusion among our lecturers, as they checked the student view and could still see items related to staff. In my opinion, the promised functionality of Enter Student/Access View suggests otherwise, so the confusion is understandable.

I am not sure whether this is intended behavior. If it is, then this should at least be indicated to instructors in some way.

summary: Delegated Access "Become User" grants access to a target user's sites outside the granted hierarchy node
description:
Delegated Access’s Advanced Options panel lets an admin grant a delegated-access user the “Become User” privilege on a specific hierarchy node. The documentation article “How do I delegate site access to a user?” describes this feature as follows:

{noformat}“Note: The Become User tool will only function for the sites to which the user has been granted access.”{noformat}

In the following example setup, using the default configuration:


* User A is a member of Site-1 and Site-2.
* Site-1 is part of the hierarchy “Subject.”
* User B is granted delegated access to the hierarchy node “Subject”, with the advanced option “Allow user to use Become User tool for users in these sites” enabled on that node.
* User B uses the Become User tool on User A.
* User B now sees Site-1 and Site-2, even though Site-2 is not part of the “Subject” hierarchy node.


This behavior appears to contradict the promised or implied functionality of the delegated-access hierarchy node’s advanced option. My understanding is that, after becoming User A in the example above, User B should only see Site-1.

The documentation note  “The Become User tool will only function for the sites to which the user has been granted access” could possibly be interpreted differently.
However, it should at least be clarified whether this behavior is intended or whether it should be considered an issue.

summary: Prevent Lessons from creating /blti/null items after invalid deep-link responses
description:
*Short Description*
When an LTI Deep Linking response contains no usable LTI resource link, the Lessons callback creates an invalid item with the reference {{/blti/null}} instead of reporting the failure.

*Steps to Reproduce*

# Open a Lessons page and add an LTI item through a Deep Linking-enabled tool.
# Have the tool return no usable LTI resource link, such as an empty or unsupported item response.
# Return to the Lessons page.

*Expected Behavior*
Sakai reports that the response contains no usable LTI resource link and does not add a Lessons item.

*Actual Behavior*
The LTI callback warns that {{contentKey=null}} but still returns {{ltiItemId=/blti/null}}. Lessons persists an invalid LTI item with no title. Rendering the page can then fail with {{NullPointerException: Cannot invoke \"java.lang.CharSequence.toString()\" because \"replacement\" is null}} in {{ShowPageProducer.printSubpage}}.

*Impact*
The affected Lessons page cannot be rendered for instructors or students until the malformed database row is repaired or removed.

*Environment*

* App version: Sakai 25 and master

summary: Prevent published assessment settings from removing a Gradebook item before validation
description:
*Short Description*
When a published assessment that currently owns an automatic Gradebook item is changed to use a manually created Gradebook item without selecting one, saving the settings removes the automatic Gradebook item and displays a hard-coded Spanish error to users whose language is English.

*Steps to Reproduce*

# In a site with Tests & Quizzes and Gradebook, create an assessment containing at least one question.
# Publish the assessment and select the option that creates and sends scores to its own Gradebook item.
# Confirm that the assessment's item appears in Gradebook.
# Open the published assessment's Settings page.
# Under Gradebook Options, select the option to send grades to a manually created Gradebook item, but leave the Gradebook item selector at its empty prompt.
# Optionally change an unrelated setting, such as selecting "Send one email per day summarizing notifications for student submissions."
# Save the assessment settings.

*Expected Behavior*
Sakai should validate that a Gradebook item was selected before changing any Gradebook data. With an English user locale, any validation message should be displayed in English, and the existing automatic Gradebook item should remain intact.

*Actual Behavior*
Sakai removes the existing automatic Gradebook item and then displays the hard-coded Spanish message {{No se pueden crear exámenes sin ningún item asociado}}. The settings are not saved.

*Impact*
Instructors can lose an assessment's Gradebook item while saving published assessment settings. The unrelated setting they changed appears to cause the failure, and the Spanish message is confusing for users working in English.

*Environment*

* App version: Sakai 25 and master
* User language: English

summary: Allow the site navigation drawer to scroll in narrow desktop windows
description:
*Short Description*
When a desktop browser is narrowed until Sakai displays the bottom navigation bar, the site navigation drawer can extend below its available space. Mouse-wheel, trackpad, and scrollbar input may not scroll the course tool list, leaving lower tools inaccessible.

*Steps to Reproduce*

# Sign in to Sakai on a desktop or laptop with a mouse or trackpad.
# Open a course site containing enough tools for the site navigation list to exceed the available window height.
# Resize the browser to a narrow desktop view where the bottom navigation bar and 3x3 site-navigation button are displayed.
# Select the 3x3 site-navigation button to open the drawer.
# Attempt to scroll the course tool list with the mouse wheel or trackpad.
# Attempt to drag the vertical scrollbar to the bottom of the list.

*Expected Behavior*
After the fix, the course tool list occupies the available space between the drawer header and footer, scrolls independently with mouse-wheel, trackpad, keyboard, and scrollbar input, and allows every course tool to be reached.

*Actual Behavior*
The lower portion of the course tool list and its scrollbar can be clipped at the bottom of the drawer. Mouse-wheel and trackpad input do not move the list, and tools below the visible area cannot be accessed.

*Impact*
Desktop users who tile browser windows or work at the responsive breakpoint cannot access all tools in the active course unless they resize the window into a different navigation layout. This particularly affects users without a touchscreen.

*Environment*

* App version: [unknown]
* View: narrow desktop window using the bottom navigation bar
* Input: mouse or trackpad on a non-touch laptop

summary: Make private-message FAQ publishing configurable and prevent implicit forum creation
description:
*Short Description*

Private-message FAQ publishing is enabled for every Sakai site containing Messages and Discussions, with no configuration option. Viewing a sent or received private message can also silently create or recreate the automatically managed FAQ Forum and FAQ Topic.

*Steps to Reproduce*

# Add the Messages and Discussions tools to a site.
# Ensure the site has at least one sent or received private message.
# Open the private-message detail page.
# Open Discussions and observe that an FAQ Forum and FAQ Topic were created even though no one completed Post to FAQ Forum.
# Delete the FAQ Forum.
# Start a new Sakai session and view a sent or received private message in the same site.
# Return to Discussions and observe that replacement FAQ records were created with new IDs.
# Review Sakai configuration and observe that the feature cannot be disabled.

*Expected Behavior*

Administrators can control the feature with {{msgcntr.messages.publishToFaq.enabled}}, which defaults to {{true}} for backward compatibility. When set to {{false}}, the Post to FAQ Forum UI and actions are unavailable and viewing private messages never creates Discussions data. When enabled, an authorized user can explicitly complete Post to FAQ Forum, and that action creates the FAQ Forum or FAQ Topic when missing.

*Actual Behavior*

The feature is always available when Messages and Discussions are present. {{MessageForumPublishToFaqBean.init()}} calls {{getFaqForumForArea()}}, whose implementation creates and saves a forum when no result exists, despite the API documenting the method as returning the existing forum or null. Replacement records are attributed to {{admin}}, and no {{forums.newforum}} event identifies the creation.

*Impact*

Institutions cannot opt out of a specialized workflow that adds unexpected UI and persistent Discussions content to every eligible site. Instructors and administrators cannot permanently delete the generated forum because ordinary private-message views recreate it, making sites appear to modify themselves and making the changes difficult to audit.

*Environment*

* App version: Sakai 25.x and later
* Tools: Messages and Discussions

summary: Remove stale Samigo Gradebook items during Replace My Data
description:
*Short Description*
Using Site Info > Import from Site > Replace My Data for Tests & Quizzes moves existing published assessments to Trash but leaves their externally maintained Samigo Gradebook items behind. A replacement assessment with the same title can then appear to save or publish successfully without creating its Gradebook item.

*Steps to Reproduce*

# Create a source site and a destination site, each containing Tests & Quizzes and Gradebook.
# In the destination site, create an assessment, add at least one question, and publish it with the option to create and send scores to its own Gradebook item.
# Confirm that the assessment's externally maintained item appears in Gradebook.
# In the source site, create an assessment with the same title.
# In the destination site, use Site Info > Import from Site, select the source site, choose Replace My Data, select Tests & Quizzes, and complete the import.
# Open Tests & Quizzes > Trash and confirm that the destination site's original published assessment was moved to Trash.
# Open Gradebook and observe that the original assessment's externally maintained item remains.
# Publish the imported replacement assessment with the option to create and send scores to its own Gradebook item.
# Observe that publishing or saving completes without creating a Gradebook item for the replacement assessment.

*Expected Behavior*
Replace My Data should remove each replaced published assessment's externally maintained Samigo Gradebook item when the assessment is moved to Trash. Unrelated manually created Gradebook items must remain. A replacement assessment should then be able to create a new Gradebook item with the same title and send scores to it.

*Actual Behavior*
The import cleanup soft-deletes the published assessment without removing its external Gradebook item. The stale item blocks creation of the replacement item's same-titled Gradebook item, and the failure is not presented to the instructor.

*Impact*
Instructors can end up with published assessments that appear configured to send grades but have no Gradebook association. Existing scores may become stranded on stale items, and recovery requires restoring and renaming trashed assessments before recreating the correct associations.

*Environment*

* App version: Sakai 25.x as of June 25, 2026, and master
* Tools: Site Info, Tests & Quizzes, and Gradebook

# *Visits*: Focused on traffic volume, unique user metrics, and trend over time.

### Members who visited (Format: Count / Total Members + %). The number and percentage of officially enrolled site members who have accessed the site.

summary: MOTD: Add auto-rotating carousel for multiple messages
description:
Currently the MOTD tool (sakai.motd) only displays a single message at a time, even when several are active — there is no way to browse the other active messages without navigating away from the page. (Note: this is different from the Dashboard MOTD widget, which already shows multiple messages stacked side by side — see SAK-46842.)

Request: add an optional auto-rotating carousel display for sakai.motd, so admins can publish several active messages and have them rotate one at a time automatically, with manual previous/next controls, instead of only ever showing one.

h3. Proposed behaviour

* Opt-in via sakai.properties: motd.carousel.enabled (boolean, default false) turns the carousel on. Existing installs keep today's single-message behaviour unless an admin explicitly enables it.
* Bootstrap 5 carousel: auto-rotates through all active (non-draft) MOTD messages, most recent first, at a configurable interval (motd.carousel.interval, default 4000ms), with manual previous/next arrows and slide indicators.
* Admins control which messages rotate simply by publishing or drafting them through the existing MOTD workflow — no extra configuration UI needed.
* A single very long message is capped at a configurable maximum height (motd.carousel.max-height, default 400px) and scrolls internally past that, instead of growing the widget (and pushing the rest of the page down) without limit.
* The containing iframe resizes correctly for each message regardless of how much its content height differs from the others, with no residual scrollbar.

h3. Implementation notes

Implemented on trunk in the message-tool module (sakai.motd tool: sakai.motd.xml, chef_synoptic_message-List.vm, SynopticMessageAction.java, recent.properties), with motd.carousel.enabled / motd.carousel.interval / motd.carousel.max-height documented in default.sakai.properties. A pull request will follow.

summary: Statistics New Analytics: Submissions and Grades
description:
Based on T&L's comments in ticket SAK-52659, we propose 2 new sections:

# *Submissions*: Focused on tracking submission timeliness, pending grading workload, and student submission delays.

## Tools Selector: Interactive toggle buttons to filter metrics by selected tool (e.g., Assignments, Tests & Quizzes).
## KPIs:
### On-time submissions (Count + %). The total number and percentage of student submissions delivered on or before the due date.
### Late submissions (Count + %). The total number and percentage of submissions delivered after the established deadline.
### Missed submissions (Count + %). The total number and percentage of assigned items that were past due and never submitted.
### Submissions to grade (Count / Total + %). The number and percentage of completed student submissions currently awaiting evaluation by the instructor.
### Students at risk (Count / Total + %). The number and percentage of enrolled students displaying critical submission delays or missed deadlines.
### Median late delay (Duration). The midpoint duration of submission delays among late entries, offering a realistic estimate of typical student tardiness.
## Visual Chart: Stacked horizontal progress bar representing overall Submission status (On time, Late, Missed).
## Accordion Breakdowns: By user and By item.
# *Grades*: Focused on grading progress, class performance benchmarks, and academic risk detection. Only include the items linked to Gradebook.
## Tools Selector: Interactive toggle buttons to filter metrics by selected tool (e.g., Assignments, Gradebook).
## KPIs:
### Items graded (Count / Total + %). The number and percentage of evaluable items that have been graded out of the total available.
### Students fully graded (Count / Total + %). The number and percentage of enrolled students who have received final grades for all required items.
### Class average (Score + %). The overall mean grade achieved across all evaluated students and items.
### Students below threshold (Count / Total + %). The number and percentage of students whose cumulative score falls below the defined passing or risk threshold (configurable at the platform or site level).
## Visual Chart: Horizontal bar chart representing the Grading funnel (Enrolled, With grades, Meeting threshold).
## Accordion Breakdowns: By user and By item.

The default threshold value is 50%. This value can be configured at three levels:

# For the entire platform, using {{sitestats.grades.threshold}} in {{sakai.properties}}. The value must be an integer between 0 and 100.

h1. 

h3. v1.18.48 (September 1st, 2026)

* PLATFORM: JDK27 support added [#4072|https://github.com/[user]/lombok/issues/4072].
* BUGFIX: {{[user]}} usage on JDK26 no longer results in class files that require {{lombok.jar}} to be on the runtime classpath (which should not be neccessary). [#4040|https://github.com/[user]/lombok/issues/4040].
* FEATURE: New [config key|https://projectlombok.org/features/configuration] {{lombok.checkReturnValueAnnotation}} (values: {{none}}, {{lombok}}; default: {{none}}) lets lombok generate {{[user]}} on generated methods where the return value should not be ignored, such as {{[user]}} methods and {{[user]()}}. A future lombok release may flip the default to {{lombok}}. [#4013|https://github.com/[user]/lombok/pull/4013].
* PROMOTION: {{[user]}} has been promoted to the main package. Otherwise, no changes have been made to the annotation. The old experimental annotation will remain for a few versions, at which point it will be marked as a deprecated annotation. Eventually it'll be removed. If you had {{lombok.config}} configuration for this annotation, the configuration keys for this feature have been renamed. [#2209|https://github.com/[user]/lombok/issues/2209].
* OLD-CRUFT: {{lombok.experimental.Wither}} and {{lombok.Delegate}} are deprecated remnants; these features were moved (to respectively {{lombok.With}} and {{lombok.experimental.Delegate}} over 5 years ago. They are now removed entirely. If your project is dependent on an older version of lombok which still has those; fret not, lombok still processes these annotations. It just no longer includes them in the jar.
* FEATURE: CheckerFramework: Lombok now adds {{[user]}} to constructors it makes if you have enabled checker framework via {{lombok.config}}.
* BUGFIX: CheckerFramework: Lombok would add {{[user]}} to the {{build()}} method of any generated builder, even if it is a builder for invoking a method; in that case, the side-effect-free nature of {{build()}} mirrors the side-effect-free nature of the method invocation you've built. Lombok now checks if the method it generated a builder for is side effect free / 'check return type'.

summary: Polls: bulk CSV import doesn't handle non-UTF-8 files and gives generic, unlogged errors
description:
While reviewing the bulk poll CSV import feature added in SAK-52400 / SAK-52725, three related problems were found in PollImportController / PollsServiceImpl.importPollsFromCsv:

h3. 1. Sample template and uploaded file encoding

downloadSample() writes csv.getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8) with no BOM, and readUploadedFile() decodes uploads with a hardcoded InputStreamReader(..., StandardCharsets.UTF_8), with no encoding detection or fallback. When a user opens the sample in Excel on Windows and saves as the default "CSV (Comma delimited)" (not "CSV UTF-8"), Excel writes the file as Windows-1252. Decoding that as UTF-8 does not throw: Java's default decoder silently replaces every accented character with U+FFFD, and if the header row is affected, isValidHeaderRow() rejects the file outright with no hint that encoding is the cause.

h3. 2. Import errors don't identify the failing row or column

parseImportedPolls()/buildImportedPoll() throw PollImportException with a fixed set of error codes, most of which collapse into the generic WRONG_FORMAT (invalid header, blank question, fewer than two options, invalid Access value, and any unexpected parser exception all share the same message). None of the messages include the 1-based row number, so with a multi-row batch the user cannot tell which line is wrong.

h3. 3. No server-side logging

None of the validation failures in the import pipeline are logged. The whole class only has two unrelated log.warn calls (missing site when resolving groups, and file read IOException). An admin investigating a user's report has nothing to check in the Sakai logs.

h3. Proposed fix

* Detect a UTF-8 BOM on upload; if absent, try strict UTF-8 decoding and fall back to Windows-1252 on failure. Add a UTF-8 BOM to the downloaded sample so Excel opens and re-saves it as UTF-8.
* Include the CSV row number in import error messages.
* Split WRONG_FORMAT into more specific error codes (invalid header, missing question, too few options, invalid access value) with clearer messages.
* Log a warning server-side (site, row, error code) whenever an import is rejected.

summary: Date Manager: Shift Dates and bulk setters do nothing with the jQuery UI date picker (23.x backports)
description:
Since SAK-51728 and SAK-52523 the Date Manager client script reads each table cell's current date from the picker's visible input and strictly parses it as an ISO wall-clock string (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm). That is correct for the native datetime-local picker introduced by SAK-46717 (Sakai 25+), but Sakai 23 still ships the jQuery UI based lang-datepicker, whose visible input holds a locale formatted string such as 03/30/2026 00:00. Every row therefore fails to parse, logs "Invalid date format: 03/30/2026 00:00" and is skipped, so Shift Dates (and the bulk setters) silently do nothing on a 23.x deployment that carries these changes.

Verified on a production Sakai 23 instance: the served initDatePicker.js is byte-identical to the SAK-52523 commit and the served lang-datepicker.js is byte-identical to the 23.x jQuery UI picker.

Fix: make the Date Manager script picker-agnostic so the same file works on 23.x and master, which also unblocks backporting the current Date Manager to 23.x:

* Read a cell's current date from the picker's ashidden iso8601 field (which both pickers maintain) via the existing parseInputDateValue instead of parsing the visible input.
* When a jQuery UI datepicker widget is attached to the input, write new dates through datepicker("setDate") and store the ISO8601-with-offset string the widget itself writes; otherwise keep the native datetime-local path unchanged.
* Bind hidden-field change listeners with jQuery, since the jQuery UI picker fires jQuery-only change events that native addEventListener listeners never see (this would leave the Fit / column fill / term date buttons disabled on 23).

Steps to reproduce (23.x with SAK-52523 applied): Site Info > Date Manager, enter a number of days in Shift Dates, click Shift All Dates. No dates change; the browser console shows one "Invalid date format" warning per cell.

summary: MOTD carousel: a message's embedded <style> can leak its colors onto other messages
description:
SAK-52865 added an opt-in auto-rotating carousel to sakai.motd (motd.carousel.enabled) so more than one message can be shown and rotated through in the same render, instead of just one. This regression only shows up once that carousel is enabled with more than one message eligible to display.

h3. Problem

A message's rich-text body can embed its own <style> tag with generic, unprefixed selectors - for example, an institution-wide announcement template that colors a stripe via a shared class name such as "fondo_kolore", with the actual color set inline inside each message's own <style> block. Before the carousel, sakai.motd only ever rendered one message at a time, so two such <style> blocks never coexisted in the same document. With the carousel, every eligible message's body is rendered into the DOM at once (one per Bootstrap .carousel-item), so two different messages built from the same template but using different colors for the same class name collide: the browser resolves same-specificity selector matches document-wide by source order, so whichever message's <style> block comes later in the DOM silently wins that class's color for every message using it, not just its own.

h3. Steps to reproduce

# Set motd.carousel.enabled=true (restart required) and place sakai.motd where it can show two eligible messages/announcements.
# Create two announcements built from the same rich-text template that embeds its own <style> for a shared, unprefixed class name (e.g. a colored stripe), each using a different color for that class.
# View the site's MOTD widget and let the carousel rotate through both (or use the prev/next controls).

Expected: each message keeps its own color on its own slide, same as when viewed on its own outside the carousel. Actual: both slides end up showing the same color - whichever message's <style> block happens to be later in the rendered DOM. Confirmed live with getComputedStyle() on the colliding class in both slides: both resolved to the same value, with one message's real color silently overridden by the other's later <style> rule at equal specificity.

h3. Proposed fix

Scope each message's own body markup - and any <style> it embeds - inside its own Declarative Shadow DOM root (<template shadowrootmode="open">) in chef_synoptic_message-List.vm, so its embedded styles never leak past its own subtree, matching the isolation a message already has when shown alone. The outer .textPanel wrapper stays in the light DOM so the skin's own styling and inherited properties (font, color) still apply normally. A small script upgrades this for browsers that support attachShadow() but not yet the native declarative-shadow-DOM HTML parsing; browsers with neither Shadow DOM mechanism fall back to the original, pre-fix behaviour (no worse than before). Implemented and verified locally; PR to follow.

summary: Polls: bulk CSV import/export should support regional date and delimiter conventions (Excel locale mismatches)
description:
h2. Problem

Excel on a machine configured with a regional locale that uses a comma as the decimal separator (Spain, most of South America, Portuguese, and most of continental Europe) writes CSV files differently from the US/UK convention the Polls bulk import expected:

* Dates: opening and re-saving a CSV in Excel reformats date cells into the OS's short date convention (e.g. dd/MM/yyyy or dd/MM/yy for Spain) instead of the yyyy-MM-dd the importer required, so a previously valid file could no longer be re-imported after being edited in Excel.
* Delimiter: Excel on those same locales writes CSV files using ';' as the field delimiter instead of ',', because ',' is reserved as the decimal separator - the whole header row was read as a single column and the import was rejected outright.

h2. Solution

Dates: on import, try the user's locale short date format (matching what Excel actually writes, 2-digit year included), then the same day/month order with the year forced to 4 digits (matching a full year typed by hand), then the documented yyyy-MM-dd default. The downloadable template and on-screen example now always write a 4-digit year for readability.

Delimiter: choose ';' as the first delimiter to try when the user's configured decimal separator is ',' (the same signal gradebookng already uses for the same reason in ImportGradesHelper/ExportPanel), falling back to the default ',' when that guess doesn't produce a valid header row. Only a header-validation failure triggers the fallback; any other validation error means the delimiter was already correct.

h2. Trade-off: ambiguous dates

Accepting the locale's day/month order means a date like 06/01/2026 is no longer rejected outright - it now parses according to the account's date order (e.g. day/month for es-ES, so 6 January), instead of only ever matching ISO. This is the same trade-off Excel itself makes whenever someone types a date by hand: interpreting it by regional convention instead of requiring an unambiguous format. It only affects the case where both readings (day/month and month/day) are valid dates; anything with a day or month out of range still gets rejected regardless of order.

h2. Files changed

* polls-api: PollImportCsvFormat.java
* polls-impl: PollsServiceImpl.java, PollsServiceTests.java, components.xml, PollsServiceTestConfiguration.java
* polls-tool: PollImportController.java
* polls.properties, polls_es.properties

summary: Assignments: Treat peer assessment with no scores as "Commented"
description:
An instructor can provide feedback without scores, and it is released to students if the instructor clicks the Release Grades link on the submission list. 

However, for an assignment set up as a peer assessment, a peer review that has comments/feedback only but no score is not released. The instructor would have to put a score and/or comments to be able to release that to students.

I feel that a peer review assessment with no score should be treated the same as instructor providing comments only and released with the Release Grades link.

summary: Keep the Courses widget working when a course term is unavailable
description:
*Short Description*
The Dashboard Courses widget can stop rendering all pinned sites when one course's term does not match an entry in the returned academic terms. It can leave the initial "You haven't pinned any sites yet" message visible even though the sites API returned HTTP 200 with pinned sites.

*Steps to Reproduce*

# Pin a course whose stored term label is absent from the academic term list. For example, the course has {{"term": "2026 Fall Semester "}} while the academic term has {{"name": "2026 Fall Semester"}}.
# Pin another course with a valid academic term and a project site.
# Open Dashboard and view the Courses widget.

*Expected Behavior*
All pinned site cards should render, including the course with an unmatched term. Valid terms should remain available in the term selector, and an unmatched term should not interrupt processing of subsequent sites or create an invalid selector option. Exact term-name matching can remain unchanged.

*Actual Behavior*
The failed lookup adds {{undefined}} to the available terms. Processing a subsequent course can throw {{TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'name')}}; rendering the selector throws {{TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'id')}}. The widget can retain the misleading no-pinned-sites message.

*Impact*
A single inconsistent or obsolete course term can prevent an affected user's entire Courses widget from rendering. Pinned sites remain accessible through portal navigation.

*Environment*

* App version: client build unknown; reproduced with the Sakai 25.x course-list component. The same unchecked lookup is present in current master.
* Browser: Chromium reproduction with a successful mocked sites response.

summary: Site Info: Manage Groups and Manage Participants deny access to users with group/site membership permissions
description:
Users who hold the granular Site Info permissions, but not site.upd, see the "Manage Groups" and "Manage Participants" entries in the Site Info menu, but get "You do not have permission to change access to the site" (java.notaccess) when they click them. A typical case is a Teaching Assistant role with site.upd.grp.mbrshp.

h3. Cause

SAK-51119 (commit 2d05a87f66a) added a siteService.allowUpdateSite() check to the entry point of every Site Info sub-page, closing the student access reported in SAK-50640 / SAK-51116. For two of those pages the check is stricter than the permission Site Info itself uses to show them:

* doManageGroupHelper: the menu shows "Manage Groups" with site.upd.grp.mbrshp (MenuBuilder), the kernel accepts saving the site with that permission (BaseSiteService.save()), and SiteAction already uses allowUpdateSite || allowUpdateGroupMembership elsewhere; only the entry check requires site.upd.
* doMenu_siteInfo_manageParticipants: the menu shows "Manage Participants" with site.viewRoster, and the page itself is built for allowUpdateSite || allowViewRoster || allowUpdateSiteMembership, rendering the edit controls only with site.upd.site.mbrshp; doUpdate_participant() enforces that permission again server-side on save. The entry check requires site.upd, which also locks out users with site.upd.site.mbrshp.

h3. Proposed fix

Align each entry check with the permission already used to show that menu entry:

* Manage Groups: site.upd or site.upd.grp.mbrshp.
* Manage Participants: site.upd, site.upd.site.mbrshp or site.viewRoster to open the page (read-only list with only site.viewRoster). Adding, removing or changing participants still requires site.upd.site.mbrshp (or site.upd), unchanged.

Students remain denied: in the default realm templates neither Student nor access holds site.upd.grp.mbrshp, site.upd.site.mbrshp or site.viewRoster, so the access closed by SAK-50640 / SAK-51116 / SAK-51119 is not reopened.

summary: LTI: Return empty list for some LTI13Servlet methods if no external tool placements
description:
The precipitating case for this improvement involves the LTI 1.3 integration with McGraw Hill services. When attempting to pair a Sakai course site with a McGraw Hill course or section via the Lessons tool, McGraw Hill (for some reason) requests line items associated with the Sakai site. Currently, LTI13Servlet.handleLineItemsGet returns a 403 via the checkToolHasPlacements method. The 403 causes a disruption with the McGraw Hill integration, such that activities from McGraw Hill cannot be deployed to the Sakai Lessons tool as content items.

The attached screencast, McGrawHillIntegrationExample-20260929.mp4, shows the problem in action.

The current workaround for this issue is to first deploy the McGraw Hill LTI 1.3 integration to the site navigation for the Sakai site in question. Then adding of McGraw Hill content items via the Lessons tool (Add Content > Add Learning App) can proceed without a problem, because checkToolHasPlacements returns true (does not return a 403 to the external tool).

Revising how LTI13Servlet.handleLineItemsGet handles a false value returned by checkToolHasPlacements can supplant the need for the workaround described above. In other words, instead of a 403, handleLineItemsGet could return a 200 and an empty list.

Technically, checkToolHasPlacements immediately returns a 403 to the external tool if there are no tool placements found. An exceptional case for this behavior could be made for just handleLineItemsGet and handleNamesAndRoles. However, there are eight total methods for distinct LTI 1.3 requests:

# handleLineItemScore
# handleNamesAndRoles (needed)
# handleGroupService
# handleLineItemsPost
# handleLineItemsUpdate
# handleLineItemsGet (needed)
# handleLineItemsDetail
# handleLineItemsDelete

Should those flagged with ‘needed’ in the list above be the only exceptions?
